AXE-2.4.1-bypass-verified.my_measurement: Fresh page per leg, 14 routes x 1280/1024/420 x light+dark (84 legs, 0 probe errors). On every single leg document.activeElement after boot is the page H1 (tabindex -1, set by app.js focusHead), and one Tab from that arrival state lands on the first canvas control, never on a.skip[data-testid="skip.canvas"]: signin.persona.frontdesk (signin), board.chair.1 (board, temp-board), money.tab.era, chairs.card.a-1050.expand, exams.row.enc-9003.open, close.decision.d-1.keep, risk.row.d-1.why, roles.daypass.add, perio.full, enc.rail, checkout.rail, ledger.explain, phone.simulate. skipIsFirstTab = false on 42/42 route x width legs. The link itself is sound: focused directly it is visible at top 8px, is the first focusable in DOM order, href="#canvas", and Enter puts focus in #canvas with the hash unchanged on 84/84 legs. axe 4.13.0 bypass + skip-link on 10 routes: 0 violations, 0 incomplete, both rules pass.
AXE-2.4.1-bypass-verified.threshold: 100% of 16 routes at 1280, 1024 and 420: first Tab = skip link, visible; Enter lands focus in #canvas. axe bypass/skip-link: 0 violations.
AXE-2.4.1-bypass-verified.scope_correction: Broader than claimed. The auditors named 9 screens; I measured 0% pass on every route I could reach — the 9 claimed plus chairs, exams, risk, roles and temp-board. It is a shell defect (app.js render(): focusHead(c) on route change), not a per-screen one. The axe clause of the threshold passes everywhere; only the first-Tab clause fails.
AXE-2.4.1-bypass-verified.why: Re-measured from a clean page on every route: first Tab is the skip link on 0 of 42 route x width legs, against a threshold of 100%, so the registered contract fails on the wrong side everywhere. The innocent explanation the auditors flag is real — arrival focus on the h1 is already inside #canvas, so the top bar is in fact bypassed and axe reports nothing — but the registered test is 'reload, press Tab once, assert activeElement is a.skip', and that is unambiguous.
AXE-2.4.1-bypass-verified.fix_direction: One shell change in app.js render(): leave the sequential-focus start point at the document after the first paint (scroll/announce the h1 without focusing it), or reconcile the heuristic to accept arrival focus inside #canvas as the bypass.

WCAG-2.2.1.my_measurement: Static sweep of prototype/js for setTimeout/setInterval found exactly three content-affecting timers, all re-measured live at 1280x900 light. (1) Board/temp rail: after pressing rail1.chip.0 the .pointed ring is on board.card.a-1042.arrive at +150 ms and gone at +6.2 s (shell.js:187, 6000 ms); no control on the page matches /longer|off|timer|stay|dismiss|extend|pause/. (2) PIN pad after three missed PINs: refusal reads 'Wait five minutes - device locked', the only control is 'Close', no countdown text, no extend control (shell.js PIN_LOCK_MS = 5 min). (3) Perio: after an undo the .pe-flash reads 'Undo: removed 3 at tooth 2 site 1' at +300 ms and '' at +5.0 s (perio.js:102, 4500 ms). No turn-off, no >=10x adjustment, no 20-second warning on any of the three.
WCAG-2.2.1.threshold: 0 time limits under 20 hours without a turn-off, a >=10x adjustment, or a 20-second warning with >=10 extensions.
WCAG-2.2.1.why: Three timers under 20 hours, none with a turn-off, a 10x adjustment or a 20-second warning: 3 against a threshold of 0. Severity lowered from P1 because two of the three legs are off the daily flow (the ring needs a temp on their first shift to press a rail step; the lockout needs three consecutive missed PINs) and all three hide text that survives elsewhere — the ring's verb in #live, the flash in Settings > Last key pressed — so nothing is lost, only the visible ring and echo.
WCAG-2.2.1.fix_direction: Hold the .pointed ring and the perio flash until the next press replaces them instead of on a timer, and print a live countdown (or register the WCAG Essential exception) on the five-minute device lock.

WCAG-2.4.11.my_measurement: Tab walk of all 54 stops on #/dentist/encounter/enc-9002, light, resting state, computing max overlap of each focused rect against every non-ancestor position:sticky/fixed element. 1280x900: one sticky (.topbar, 0-61) and 0 elements 100% covered. 1024x900 operatory: two stickies (.topbar 0-113 and div.stack.enc-gate-col, top 743.3, bottom 884) and 4 focused elements 100% covered by the gate column — enc.temporality.today, enc.temporality.planned, enc.temporality.existing and enc.note.field.plan (cover 1.000 each). 420x860 phone: 2 focused elements 100% covered — enc.proc.d2392 and enc.note.field.plan — plus 2 partially covered.
WCAG-2.4.11.threshold: Minimum (AA): 0 focused elements 100% covered. Enhanced (AAA, should): 0 focused elements partially covered.
WCAG-2.4.11.scope_correction: At 420 the resting-state count is 2 fully covered (enc.proc.d2392 and enc.note.field.plan), not the 1 the row names; the 1280 leg is clean, as the row says. I did not reproduce the 'two killer rows standing -> 13 stops' figure, so the confirmed number is the resting-state one.
WCAG-2.4.11.why: The sticky .enc-gate-col paints over the work canvas below 1280 and 4 focused controls at 1024 and 2 at 420 end up entirely hidden while focused, against a minimum threshold of 0 — the wrong side, in the screen's resting state on the operatory profile a clinician uses all day.
WCAG-2.4.11.fix_direction: Give #canvas scroll-padding-bottom (or every chart/note focusable a scroll-margin-bottom) equal to the gate height plus 8 px, so the browser's own focus scroll never parks a control under the sticky gate.

CLT-neutral-irreversible.my_measurement: Re-measured every visible .btn.irreversible at 1280x900 light on load and in the driven states. Alone in its row with zero sibling controls: checkout.post (85.5x44, .co-postrow, innerHTML is the button alone), close.closeday (129x44, .btnrow), enc.file (547.6x44 at 1280 / 992x44 at 1024, .stack, siblingButtons []), money.era.era-1.postmatched (164.1x44, .btnrow), money.writeoff.post (85.5x44, .btnrow), roles.daypass.save 'Issue day pass' (171.7x44, .btnrow). Perio omission gate: pressing refusal.control moves focus onto perio.licence.implant (.btn.irreversible, activeElement confirmed) and its .seg row holds only the other three irreversible reasons — no reversible or quiet sibling. No irreversible button anywhere is focused on load and none carries autofocus (0/all).
CLT-neutral-irreversible.threshold: 100% of irreversible buttons: not focused on load, have an adjacent reversible alternative of equal height; 0 irreversible buttons alone in a row.
CLT-neutral-irreversible.scope_correction: Two of the eight claimed rows do not fail the registered threshold. Chairs: I reproduced Ready for exam at 375x44 with Chart perio 145.3 (38.8%), Write note 139.7 (37.3%), Rail 74 (19.7%) — all .btn.quiet at an identical 44 px height, not focused, not alone — so it passes the threshold line and fails only the '>= 60% width' clause that lives in the measurable_test, not the threshold. Ledger: Send statement 182.9x44 with Preview .btn.reversible 103.5x44 (56.6%) — same width-only failure. Overlays: phone.stepup.submit is alone on its grid row by geometry (232x56, no control within 4 px of its top; Cancel 608x44 sits 68 px below, outside the pad), but its container .pinpad holds 11 .btn.quiet siblings at an identical 56 px height, and .pinpad is not one of the containers the measurable_test enumerates — that row is ambiguous either way. The six alone-in-a-row rows above are not ambiguous.
CLT-neutral-irreversible.why: Six irreversible commits stand alone in a .btnrow/.co-postrow/.stack with no control beside them, against a threshold of 0, and the perio reason row offers four irreversible buttons and no neutral one with focus landing on the first — so the heuristic fails on the wrong side. The neutrality clauses (never focused on load, no autofocus) hold everywhere, as the auditors said.
CLT-neutral-irreversible.fix_direction: Put an equal-height reversible partner in each of the six lone rows (Post, Close day, File, Post matched, write-off Post, Issue day pass) and move Cancel into the perio reason .seg.

CLT-recognition-keys.my_measurement: Across all 14 routes x 1280/1024/420 x both themes, document.querySelectorAll('[aria-keyshortcuts]') returns [] and #canvas kbd count is 0 on every leg. Legends read from the live .sub: board and temp-board 'keys: A arrive, S seat, C checkout' (3); chairs 'keys: P perio, N note, R focus Ready for exam' (3); money 'Keys: P post matched . W write-off . A appeal' (3); close 'Tap the tile or press T' (1); perio 'Keys: 1-9 depth . Space bleeding . S suppuration . backspace undo . arrow skip . PgDn next tooth' (6). The close accelerator is live: aria-keyshortcuts on close.tied.tile is null, kbd count 0, and pressing 't' flips its aria-expanded false -> true.
CLT-recognition-keys.threshold: 0 legend-only shortcuts per screen. Any shortcut that exists only in the .sub legend fails; the legend may stay as a duplicate but not as the sole source.
CLT-recognition-keys.why: Every key advertised in a .sub legend is legend-only — 3 on board, 3 on chairs, 1 on close, 3 on money, 6 on perio — because no control in the prototype carries aria-keyshortcuts or a <kbd> child at all, against a threshold of 0 per screen.
CLT-recognition-keys.fix_direction: Set aria-keyshortcuts and print a small <kbd> chip on the Arrive/Seat/Checkout, Chart perio/Write note/Ready, Post matched/Write-off/Appeal, the Daily Close tile and the perio pad keys; keep the legend as a duplicate.

INT-real-world-words.my_measurement: Visible-text scan of the live DOM (1280 light), text nodes only, sr-only and hidden excluded. Close: the collapsed screen prints 'a refund, adjustment or write-off outside 07:30-17:30' (24-hour times on load, matched by /\b([01]\d|2[0-3]):[0-5]\d\b/); after Close day the stamp reads 'Closed 9/3 at 08:40 by Dr. Reagan . chain head a1c9...loc-1-1341'; the investigate rows print '#le-4504' and '#le-4506'. Compliance: the licence gate Why reads 'Clinical entitlements issue only against an active, verified staff_credentials row (...)'; the risk row face reads 'BAA: Ridge Dental Lab expires in 21 days (9/24)' with 'business associate agreement' only inside the closed Why; the issued card reads 'magic link sent to their phone; TOTP on their own device' with no gloss. Money: the ERA card heading is 'Delta Dental 835 . era-1', the batch line carries 'TRN 20260903-90112', and the aging rows print 'c-72 . D2740 Crown, porcelain/ceramic', 'c-65 . D2392 ...', 'c-51 . D4341 ...'.
INT-real-world-words.threshold: 0 bare codes without a word; 0 raw store keys, ISO timestamps, 24-hour times or unformatted cents visible on any screen
INT-real-world-words.why: Every token the three rows name is on the glass exactly as described: two 24-hour times and a raw chain hash and three ledger ids on Close, a store table name and two unglossed acronyms on Compliance, and store keys era-1 / c-72 / c-65 / c-51 plus TRN on Money — against a threshold of 0 raw store keys and 0 24-hour times. Everything else does pair its code with a word (CDT, CARC, entitlements, money, dates), so the failure is narrow but on the wrong side.
INT-real-world-words.fix_direction: Print 12-hour times, label or drop the chain hash and ledger ids, replace 'staff_credentials row' with 'a verified licence on file', spell out BAA and TOTP on the row face, and show the payer's own batch and claim numbers instead of era-1 / c-nn.

INT-labels-visible-above.my_measurement: Opened each overlay surface at 1280x900 light and enumerated input/select/textarea plus [role=textbox]. Real form controls: palette.input (INPUT, no <label for> and no visible aria-labelledby target; aria-label 'Search patients, appointments, claims, reports, and actions' plus placeholder 'Type three letters... try walkout statement, day sheet, Office Journal'); palette.confirm.dob (INPUT, visible label 'Date of birth', labelAbove true, no trailing colon, but placeholder 'MM/DD/YYYY' is a disappearing format hint — the format is also repeated in the aria-label and the hint paragraph is separate); phone.request.ar-1.reason (INPUT, visible label 'Send back with one line', labelAbove true, no colon). The two PIN readouts pin.display and phone.stepup.display are DIV role=textbox aria-readonly=true with an aria-label only, border '0px none' and background rgba(0,0,0,0).
INT-labels-visible-above.threshold: 100% of inputs labelled by visible text; 100% labels above (except check/radio); 0 placeholder-only labels; 0 trailing colons
INT-labels-visible-above.scope_correction: The denominator is wrong. Under the registered measurable_test ('for every input, select, textarea') there are 3 controls on these surfaces, not 5: the two unlabelled 'fields' the row counts are div[role=textbox][aria-readonly=true] PIN dot readouts, not inputs. So 2 of 3 inputs are labelled by visible text above (67%, not 40%), and exactly 1 is placeholder-and-aria-only: palette.input. The row's observation that the two PIN displays also have no border and no visible label is accurate, just outside the test's element list.
INT-labels-visible-above.why: Threshold asks for 0 placeholder-only labels and 100% labelled by visible text; palette.input — the search box every persona reaches from the top bar — has neither a visible label nor a visible labelled-by target, so both clauses fail on the wrong side even after the denominator is corrected.
INT-labels-visible-above.fix_direction: Put a visible 'Search' label above palette.input (an sr-only label is allowed only beside a visible search button), and give the two PIN readouts a visible 'PIN' label and a border so the empty field reads as a field.

CLT-jakob-nav.my_measurement: Serialised #topbar on 14 routes x 1280/1024/420 x both themes. #topbar.firstElementChild is span.brand on every signed-in route, and the control order is identical everywhere: topbar.location, topbar.search, the nav buttons, topbar.author, topbar.privacy, topbar.theme, topbar.signout. [aria-current] inside #topbar returns exactly one item on board, temp-board, money, chairs, exams, close, risk, roles — and an empty list on perio, encounter, checkout, ledger and phone/approvals, at all three widths and in both themes. Cause is shell.js:42-43: the marker is set only when r.route equals a NAV entry, and none of these five routes is a nav destination.
CLT-jakob-nav.threshold: Identical nav label sequence on 100% of screens for the same persona; .brand is the first child and search the second control on every screen; exactly one aria-current=page per screen. Any reordering, renaming or missing marker fails.
CLT-jakob-nav.scope_correction: The checkout-ledger row's second finding is wrong: it says 'search is the third control, not the second - the location switcher sits between them'. .brand is a <span class="brand"> with no tabindex and no role — not a control — so topbar.location is the first control and topbar.search the second, on every screen including Checkout and the Ledger. That clause passes; only the aria-current clause fails. The four claimed screens all fail it, and so does signin (which renders no nav at all, so it is arguably out of scope).
CLT-jakob-nav.why: Exactly-one-aria-current-per-screen is the threshold and these five routes carry zero, reproduced at every width and theme, so the 'you are here' marker really is missing for a whole charting or checkout session. The label sequence, brand-first and search-second clauses all hold.
CLT-jakob-nav.fix_direction: In shell.js mark the nav item that owns the current route (board for checkout, money for ledger, exams for encounter, chairs for perio, and an Approvals entry or the Andon control for phone) with aria-current="page".

COLOR-roles-per-screen.my_measurement: Re-ran the registered method (Set of computed color over visible elements with text, Set of computed background-color excluding rgba(0,0,0,0)) on a fresh page per leg, 3 widths x 2 themes. chairs: 8 text / 7 background at 1280 and 1024 in both themes, 8 / 6 at 420 in both themes. close: 11 text / 7 background in all six contexts. money: 8 text / 6 background in all six contexts.
COLOR-roles-per-screen.threshold: textColours <= 7 and backgroundColours <= 6 per screen. Baseline: board 11/9, temp-board 11/10, close 11/7, money 8/6, chairs 8/7 fail; signin 3/3, exams 3/3, perio 5/4, encounter 5/4 pass.
COLOR-roles-per-screen.why: Every figure reproduces the registered baseline exactly and lands over the ceiling: chairs 8 > 7 text and 7 > 6 background, close 11 > 7 text and 7 > 6 background, money 8 > 7 text (backgrounds 6, at the limit, so only the ink clause fails there).
COLOR-roles-per-screen.fix_direction: Collapse one severity fill ladder per screen — let the Daily Close location rows inherit the card ground, merge the chairs info/review tints — and give the money disclosure summary the quiet-button ink instead of link blue.

INT-error-wording.my_measurement: Drove every reachable refusal on the two compliance routes at 1280x900 light and read .refusal > [data-testid=refusal.verb] and .whytext directly. Verb lines: 'Remediate, compensate, or accept this conflict' (6 words, x3), 'Name the temp before issuing the pass' (7), 'Add a credential before granting clinical work' (7), 'Ask a seat that grants roles' (6), 'Set a shift end later than now' (7) — all <= 12. Regex /\b(please|sorry|oops|invalid|valid|forbidden|illegal|prohibited|you forgot|error \d|0x[0-9a-f]+|exception|null|undefined|NaN)\b/i over verb + why: 0 hits. Generic-message regex: 0 hits. Why word counts: 20, 21, 22, 23 — and the segregation-of-duties gate raises three Whys at once, of 53, 56 and 49 words.
INT-error-wording.threshold: 0 regex hits; 0 generic messages; 100% of verb lines <= 12 words; 100% of Why texts <= 40 words
INT-error-wording.scope_correction: Three Whys exceed the 40-word ceiling, not one. Granting the full extra-entitlement set raises three sod_conflict gates side by side — the refund path (53 words), the write-off path (56) and the deposit path (49) — each built from the same fraud-path + compensating-control + 'Remediate drops the extra entitlement...' template, so the overrun is one template used three times, and the auditors measured only the first.
INT-error-wording.why: Everything the threshold asks for holds except the Why ceiling: 3 of 8 measured Whys run 49-56 words against a limit of 40, and the overrun is the reusable SoD template, so it fires on every conflict a person can raise.
INT-error-wording.fix_direction: Trim the shared SoD Why template to the fraud path and the compensating control — the three decision buttons already say what each one does — which brings all three variants under 40 words at once.

WCAG-1.4.10-reflow-320.my_measurement: Fresh page per leg, device=phone, light. At 320x860 and 320x568 documentElement.scrollWidth = 320 on every claimed route (0 px page overflow) and the [data-testid] set at 320 equals the 1280 set on all of them. Disallowed / unnamed 2-D scrollers I reproduced: chairs #canvas (MAIN, tabindex -1, no role/name) scrollWidth 336 vs clientWidth 320; owner/close #canvas 365 vs 320 once close.tied.tile is opened (culprit SPAN.chip.required '▲Gap −$312.40', right edge 365); biller/money #canvas 336 vs 320 after pressing money.era.era-1.postmatched (three '.btn' read-back Confirm labels 292 wide in a 232 px box, white-space nowrap, overflow visible). Allowed wrappers that overflow but are neither focusable nor named: .perio-wrap 901/288 at 320 and 901/388 at 420 (tabindex null, role null, aria-label null); .enc-odont-wrap 408/262 at 320 and 824/658 at 1280 desk (tabindex/role/label all null); .rl-tablewrap on compliance/roles 516/262 at 320 (tabindex/role/label all null). By contrast .wrap-x on checkout (595/262) and ledger (535/262) carry tabindex=0 and role=region with a name, so the pattern exists. Step-up dialog on #/phone/approvals at 320: documentElement.scrollWidth 321 vs innerWidth 320 — 1 px of real page overflow.
WCAG-1.4.10-reflow-320.threshold: 0 px horizontal page overflow on 100% of routes; 2-D scrollers only among the 4 allowed table/chart wrappers, each focusable and named; testid set difference = empty.
WCAG-1.4.10-reflow-320.scope_correction: board: REFUTED. At 320 the only 2-D scroller on frontdesk/board (952/320) and temp/board (790/320) is #topbar, which the registered measurable_test names explicitly as a shell case allowed provided no control is hidden ('the .topbar at <=640 ... must not hide any control'); the testid set at 320 equals the 1280 set (nothing lost) and focusing each of the 9 top-bar controls scrolls it into the bar, so no control is hidden. Nothing else on board overflows. Same for encounter's exams route (topbar only) and for compliance/risk (topbar only) — the compliance defect is on compliance/roles only. overlays: only claim (3) is a threshold breach (321 > 320 in the step-up dialog); claim (1) is the same tolerated top bar and claim (2), the 38 px .andon .grow column at 420, is an internal squeeze, not a page or 2-D scroller — and I could not reproduce 'Open approvals' painting over the sentence (no overlap at 420x860). Confirmed rows: chairs, close, compliance (roles), encounter, money, perio, overlays (dialog only).
WCAG-1.4.10-reflow-320.why: Page overflow is 0 everywhere except the step-up dialog (321 px), but the canvas becomes a 2-D scroller on chairs, close and money, and the three overflowing table/odontogram wrappers carry no tabindex, role or accessible name, which is the wrong side of 'allowed wrappers, each focusable and named'.
WCAG-1.4.10-reflow-320.fix_direction: Build .perio-wrap, .enc-odont-wrap and .rl-tablewrap with ui.js scrollRegion() as .wrap-x already is, and stop the canvas overflowing at 320 (min(320px,100%) on .ch-list, wrap the Gap chip and the long Confirm labels).

CUST-3.3.8-prefs-no-auth-cost.my_measurement: 1280x800 desk light. Preference half passes: pressing topbar.theme then topbar.privacy on #/owner/close opens 0 [role=dialog], 0 pin.display elements and writes no auth event (only focus/click events). PIN half fails on all three pads. Author pad (topbar.author): its full text is 'who is charting? enter the other person's pin 1 2 3 4 5 6 7 8 9 ⌫ 0 go why this signs you out ... cancel' — no badge/NFC/tap/card/scan/passkey/forgot word, no show-digits or reveal control, and dispatching a paste of '222' on [data-testid=pin.display] leaves it empty (the display is a role=textbox div with no paste handling). #/phone/approvals step-up pad: identical — altAuth false, showDigits false. Shared-desk Daily Close (device=shared): [data-testid=close.pin] is a bare type=password, inputmode numeric, maxlength 6 input; its .field contains a label, a hint and 0 buttons — no alternative, no reveal, no recovery path.
CUST-3.3.8-prefs-no-auth-cost.threshold: 0 authentication prompts caused by preference changes; >= 1 non-memory alternative or assist on the PIN pad.
CUST-3.3.8-prefs-no-auth-cost.why: The first clause passes exactly as the auditors said, and the second fails on every PIN surface I could open: zero non-memory alternatives and zero assists (no reveal, no paste, no badge), so identifying yourself on the shared desk is a pure memory test.
CUST-3.3.8-prefs-no-auth-cost.fix_direction: Add one assist to the shared pads — a show-digits toggle on pin.display / close.pin, or paste support, or a badge tap.

WCAG-3.3.2.my_measurement: 1280x800 desk light (identical at 420 phone). 3 fields fail on the overlay surfaces. palette.input (INPUT role=combobox, opened from topbar.search): label[for] null, no wrapping label, aria-labelledby empty; its only name is aria-label 'Search patients, appointments, claims, reports, and actions' plus a placeholder 'Type three letters… try walkout statement, day sheet, Office Journal'. pin.display (DIV role=textbox, author pad) and phone.stepup.display (DIV role=textbox, step-up dialog): label[for] null, aria-labelledby empty, named only by aria-label ('PIN typed so far; Enter is Go' / '… Enter is Approve'), and both compute border '0px none' on background rgba(0,0,0,0), so the empty field has no visible boundary. close.pin on the shared desk does carry a visible <label for=dc-pin>Your PIN</label>, so the pattern exists in the codebase.
WCAG-3.3.2.threshold: 100% of fields have a visible persistent label; 0 fields labelled by placeholder or aria-label alone.
WCAG-3.3.2.why: Three of the overlay fields have no visible persistent label at all — aria-label or placeholder is their only name — which is the wrong side of '0 fields labelled by placeholder or aria-label alone'.
WCAG-3.3.2.fix_direction: Give palette.input and both PIN displays a visible <label for> above the field, and give the PIN displays a real border so the empty box is visible.

INT-temp-first-screenful.my_measurement: 1280x800 desk light and 420x860 phone light, counting button/a[href]/input/select/summary/textarea/[tabindex=0] fully inside the viewport, excluding .topbar and .skip exactly as the registered test says. Over the bar: frontdesk/board 25 and temp/board 29 (limit 20) with 6 distinct severity fills at 1280 (stop, required, review, style, info, clear — limit 3); hygienist/chairs 21 (limit 20) with 4 fills; dentist/encounter 50 (limit 14) at 1280 and 34 at 420; hygienist/perio 133 at 1280 (128 of them grid cells) and 41 at 420; #/signin 21 at 1280, and at 420 'Open my home' sits at y 1202 in an 860 px viewport, below the fold; biller/ledger 19 at 1280 (limit 14). Under the bar: checkout 12, exams 3, money 10, risk 10, roles 7, close 6.
INT-temp-first-screenful.threshold: 2 of 2 reviewers agree on purpose and first action for 100% of routes at 1280 and ≥ 90% at 420; ≤ 14 interactive elements in the first screenful (≤ 20 on Board/Chairs where each row carries one action); ≤ 3 severity fills at once; 0 decorative-only elements
INT-temp-first-screenful.scope_correction: close: REFUTED as measured. The canvas first screenful holds 6 interactive elements, not 17 — the auditors' 17 includes the 11 top-bar controls that the registered test excludes — and 2 severity fills, so both counting clauses pass; what remains is the reviewer observation that close.closeday sits at y 1171 below an 800 px fold, which is a judgement, not a threshold breach. overlays: REFUTED. With a request waiting at 420x860 and the canvas at scrollTop 0, the h1 'Approvals' is at y 416 and the first card head at y 563 — both inside the first screenful — the first-screenful count is 6 and severity fills 2, and 'Open approvals' does not overlap the Andon sentence (the 38 px one-word-per-line column is ugly but does not push the head out). Confirmed rows: board, chairs, checkout-ledger (Ledger only — Checkout passes at 12), encounter (Encounter only — Exams passes at 3), perio, signin.
INT-temp-first-screenful.why: Six of the eight claimed screens are over the registered element count on my own measurement, two of them (board, perio) grossly so; but close and overlays pass every counting clause once the top bar is excluded as the test requires.
INT-temp-first-screenful.fix_direction: Count the odontogram and the perio grid as one role=grid control with roving tabindex, and move the secondary strips (board readiness, chairs 'Since last visit', ledger rail, signin QA toggles) behind one disclosure.

CLT-split-attention.my_measurement: 1280x800 desk light and 1024x900 operatory light, measuring the .page-head .sub top against the referent's top in page coordinates and comparing closest .card ancestors. board: sub 'keys: A arrive, S seat, C checkout' at y 108; first Arrive at 676 (568 px away, different container), first Checkout at 410 (302 px away, different container), no Seat button exists at rest — 3 of 3 referents fail. chairs: sub keys at y 108; Chart perio and Write note at 328 (220 px at 1280, 257 px at 1024), both inside .card while the sub is in .page-head; 'R focus Ready for exam' has no referent on screen. money: sub 'Keys: P post matched · W write-off · A appeal' at y 160; Post matched at 401 (241 px, different container); Write off and Appeal are not on the ERA tab at all. close (device=shared): pressing close.closeday then close.closeday.confirm raises '▲Required Enter your PIN to post' at y 1216 while [data-testid=close.pin] sits at y 228 — 988 px apart, different cards; the only bridge is the refusal's own 'Enter PIN' control. perio (1024 operatory): the cell legend 'Cell: depth (or —) · small grey = prior exam · ● bleeding …' is at y 900 against the first cell row at y 413 — 487 px away, outside .perio-wrap and below the fold at load.
CLT-split-attention.threshold: 0 hints whose referent lives in a different container or > 200 px away. Baseline: the 'keys: …' legends in page-head .sub refer to buttons in cards 300-2000 px below, failing; the refusal 'Why' text inside .refusal passes.
CLT-split-attention.scope_correction: All five screens reproduce. Numbers differ slightly from the auditors' (board Arrive 568 not 546; chairs 220 at 1280 not 198; close PIN gate 988 not 944; perio legend 487 not 443.5) because I measured top-edge to top-edge in page coordinates; every one is still on the failing side.
CLT-split-attention.why: Every legend I checked lives in .page-head while its referent lives inside a .card, and four of the five are also more than 200 px away, so both halves of the threshold fail on all five screens.
CLT-split-attention.fix_direction: Print the key on the control itself (<kbd> beside Arrive / Chart perio / Post matched), move the perio cell legend inside .perio-wrap, and raise the PIN gate beside the PIN field.

INT-no-disabled-use-held.my_measurement: 1280x800 desk light and 420x860 phone light. hygienist/perio/enc-9001: 24 button[disabled] present at rest at both widths, none inside a dialog — the six sites of each missing tooth (1, 16, 17, 32) render as disabled .psite buttons reading 'x'. compliance/roles: 0 button[disabled] in any state I could reach, so the house Held pattern holds; but after opening roles.daypass.add and tabbing out of the empty name field, roles.daypass.save turns into 'Held' (aria-label 'Held: decide on the conflict or complete the form, then issue') at y 774 with 0 visible .refusal on the page, and the only explanation is the field hint 'Enter the temp's full name as it appears on their licence.' at y 311 — 463 px away, and the button's own .btnrow contains nothing but the word 'Held'. Pressing the button does raise a refusal, and that one sits 12 px above it, which is correct.
INT-no-disabled-use-held.threshold: 0 button[disabled] on any screen except inside a dialog that is itself in progress; 100% of .btn.held have an adjacent visible reason
INT-no-disabled-use-held.why: Perio ships 24 greyed-out disabled buttons outside any dialog, against a bar of 0, and the compliance day-pass primary goes Held on blur with no visible reason within 200 px, against a bar of 100% adjacency.
INT-no-disabled-use-held.fix_direction: Render missing-tooth cells as inert table text rather than disabled buttons, and print the held reason as a line in the .btnrow whenever the primary is held without a standing gate.

CDS-ICON-size-24.my_measurement: 1280x800 desk light, reading getComputedStyle on live nodes and on ::before. .chip .glyph computes 11px on every screen that has chips: board 105 glyphs, temp board 105, chairs 32, checkout 5, ledger 2, close 6 (plus one 34px tile glyph that passes), compliance/risk 4, compliance/roles 25, encounter 1, money 3, #/phone/approvals 1 — all 11px against a 16px chip floor. .btn.irreversible::before ('▮') computes 11px on checkout.post, ledger.statement.send, close (2), encounter, money and perio — against a 20px button floor. .pressmark computes 12px on checkout, encounter, perio and on all three pressed signin toggles. components.css:8 sets .btn.held::before font-size 14px. 0 of the measured glyph classes reaches its floor.
CDS-ICON-size-24.threshold: Icon box >= 20px on buttons and >= 16px on chips; 0 meaning-carrying glyphs under 16px (prototype 11px glyphs fail).
CDS-ICON-size-24.scope_correction: All nine claimed screens reproduce; I also see the same 11px .glyph on compliance/risk and on the Encounter, so the defect is shared-component-wide rather than screen-specific.
CDS-ICON-size-24.why: Every functional glyph class measures 11-14px, and the registered threshold names the 11px prototype glyphs as failing, so the measurement is unambiguously on the wrong side.
CDS-ICON-size-24.fix_direction: One change in components.css: .chip .glyph to 16px, .pressmark to 16px, and the .btn ::before bars/lock to 20px.

CLT-redundancy.my_measurement: 1280x800 desk light unless noted. chairs: over 6 cards, 'No changes since last visit' (5 words) appears on 5 of them (83%) and 'Deltas come from stored rows only: the medical-history alert…' on 6 of 6 (100%) — both over the 50% bar. money (ERA tab): inside the one ERA card the chip '▬37 matched' sits beside the batch line 'Delta 835 · 41 lines · 37 matched, ready to post · EFT $21,385.00 …', so the chip duplicates text already in the card. overlays (#/phone/approvals after phone.simulate, 420 phone and 1280 desk): both pending .ph-card carry the identical 'Write-offs at or above $150.00, and any refund, adjustment, or write-off outside business hours…' paragraph — 2 of 2 cards, 100%. perio (1024 operatory, save with a not-tolerated reason): the saved card shows chips '●Saved' and '●Recall' beside the h2 'Full chart saved'.
CLT-redundancy.threshold: 0 non-action strings > 3 words repeated across >= 50% of cards; 0 chip/text duplicates within one card. Baseline: Chairs repeats 'Since last visit No changes since last visit More' on 5 of 6 cards, failing.
CLT-redundancy.scope_correction: All four screens reproduce. Chairs is worse than claimed: a second string ('Deltas come from stored rows only…') repeats on 6 of 6 cards. On overlays I could not reproduce the four within-card duplicates as exact repeated leaf strings ('$410.00', 'Sam Dawson', '8:40 am' recur as fragments inside the store sentence rather than as duplicated nodes) — the 100% Why-paragraph repeat, which is the threshold breach, does reproduce.
CLT-redundancy.why: Each screen puts a non-action string longer than three words on at least half its cards, or a chip that repeats words already in the same card, against a bar of zero.
CLT-redundancy.fix_direction: Hoist the repeated Why paragraph and the empty 'Since last visit' strip out of the per-card body, and let each count live in either the chip or the line, not both.

CDS-DETAILS-disclosure.my_measurement: 1280x800 desk light, plus 420x860 phone for the approvals cards. Every collapsible region I found is a native <details>/<summary>: 0 div click handlers, every summary 44px tall, and the open attribute flips on press. Widths: on biller/ledger/p-303 the six rail summaries are 295px wide around 51-122px of text (Appointments 295/119, Coverage 295/80, Recall 295/51, Balance 295/67, Open plans 295/95, Last filed note 295/122), computed display 'flex'; on #/phone/approvals both cards' 'Why am I seeing this?' summaries are 394px wide at 1280 and 362px at 420 around 143px of text, display 'flex'. The canvas disclosures do hug: checkout 'Why this decision' 148/132 and 'Why this estimate' 152/136, ledger 'Why this statement' 163/147, board 'Why these chips' 123/107, close 'Why directional' 117/101, risk 'Why' 45/29 — all display 'inline-flex'.
CDS-DETAILS-disclosure.threshold: 100% of collapsible regions have a keyboard-operable toggle with correct expanded state; toggle height >= 44px; 0 disclosures implemented as plain div click handlers.
CDS-DETAILS-disclosure.scope_correction: Both claimed screens reproduce the measurement, but note which clause breaks: all three clauses quoted in the registered threshold line PASS (native keyboard-operable summaries, 44px tall, correct open state, 0 div handlers). The failing clause is the shrink-wrap assertion carried in the registered statement and measurable_test ('computed width <= text width + 32px'), which the 295px rail summaries and the 394/362px .ph-why summaries miss by 150-250px.
CDS-DETAILS-disclosure.why: The numbers hold — those eight summaries are far wider than their labels, so the focus ring spans the whole column instead of hugging the text — but this breaches the statement's shrink-wrap requirement, not any of the three numeric clauses in the threshold line, which all pass.
CDS-DETAILS-disclosure.fix_direction: Give .rail summary and .ph-why summary display: inline-flex / width: fit-content, as the canvas disclosures already have.

MQ5-color-scheme-follow-os.my_measurement: Fresh context, no theme query. With colorScheme 'dark' emulated, #/signin loads with document.documentElement data-theme 'light', body background rgb(243,241,235) (cream) and matchMedia('(prefers-color-scheme: dark)').matches true — the OS preference is ignored, and #/frontdesk/board behaves identically (data-theme 'light', same cream background, root color-scheme 'light') under both dark and light emulation. index.html line 2 hard-codes <html data-theme="light">, and grep finds 0 occurrences of prefers-color-scheme in tokens.css, base.css or components.css. The sign-in theme control exposes exactly two testids, signin.theme.light ('✓Light') and signin.theme.dark ('Dark') — no 'System' state.
MQ5-color-scheme-follow-os.threshold: OS scheme honoured on first paint with 0 flash frames; override persists per user across reload; 3-state control (System/Light/Dark) present.
MQ5-color-scheme-follow-os.why: The OS dark preference is not honoured at any point, let alone at first paint, and the control is two-state, so two of the three threshold clauses fail outright.
MQ5-color-scheme-follow-os.fix_direction: Add a prefers-color-scheme block in tokens.css with the light palette on :root, and a third 'System' state on the sign-in theme control.

WCAG-2.5.3-label-in-name.my_measurement: Fresh context per route, 1280x900 (phone 420), light and dark, axe-core 4.13.0 with label-content-name-mismatch explicitly enabled. Violation nodes per route (identical in both themes): board 29, temp-board 29, chairs 7, roles 7, ledger 4, encounter 2, exams 2, phone 2, close 2, checkout 1, risk 1, money 1, perio 99. My own contains/starts sweep over every visible labelled control (name = aria-labelledby > aria-label > text): board 72/101 contain (71%), 43/101 start (43%); chairs 25/33 contain (76%), 17/33 start (52%); roles 15/22 contain (68%), 7/22 start (32%); ledger 31/36 contain (86%); encounter 58/60 contain but only 23/60 start (38%) - all 32 teeth show '1'..'32' and are named 'Tooth 1'; perio 12/207 contain (6%) because every entered grid cell shows a digit and is named 'Tooth n site m'; money passes at load (canvas 10/10) but in the read-back after Post matched 27/31 contain (87%) with the three Confirm buttons named 'Confirm line 14: post $540.00 and a contractual write-off of $50.00' against the visible 'Confirm - post $540.00, write-off $50.00'. Named offenders reproduced verbatim: board.card.*.expand 'Details' -> 'Show forms and balance for <name>' (x25), board.chair.N 'Chair N . HK DDS' -> 'Chair N, author Dr. Hana Kim, DDS. Show device author', chairs.card.*.note 'Write note' -> 'Write the note for <name>' (x6), ledger.showpatient / ledger.asof / ledger.statement.send, roles.row.u-* '<name> . <licence>' -> 'Show grants for <name>' (x6), topbar.search 'Search Cmd-K' and .authorchip.
WCAG-2.5.3-label-in-name.threshold: 0 violations of label-content-name-mismatch; 100% of controls whose accessible name contains the visible text, >= 95% starting with it, each exception listed.
WCAG-2.5.3-label-in-name.scope_correction: All 8 claimed screens reproduce on the wrong side of the threshold. Broader than claimed: close, exams and risk also fail the 100%-containment clause (2 nodes each, the shared topbar.search and .authorchip). Sign-in is the only route that passes (100% contains, 96% starts).
WCAG-2.5.3-label-in-name.why: Re-measured from scratch with axe enabled and an independent name/text sweep; every claimed screen returns label-content-name-mismatch violations and falls short of both the 100%-contains and the 95%-starts clauses, on the same controls the auditor named.
WCAG-2.5.3-label-in-name.fix_direction: Lead every aria-label with the printed words ('Details: forms and balance for <name>', 'Write note for <name>', 'Show grants for <name> . DDS', 'Search Cmd-K - patients, claims and actions') and put the cell value into the perio cell name.

WCAG-3.3.1.my_measurement: Money Desk, 1280 light, fresh page: opened money.writeoff.p-306, typed '-50' into money.writeoff.amount and blurred it. Field gets class .invalid and border-top-color rgb(234,88,12); aria-invalid null, aria-describedby null, 0 .refusal nodes rendered, and the whole canvas innerText contains no error sentence - a colour/border change and nothing else. Pressing Post then does render '(Required) Enter an amount above zero' with a 'Fix amount' control, so press-time detection is sound. Perio at 1024 light: opened perio.tag.add and pressed perio.tag.save with an empty Observation - perio.tag.text gets aria-invalid='true' plus .invalid, and the sentence 'Say what you saw.' IS appended as visible text, but it is appended to the shared #pe-tag-hint that both fields point at, 181 px above the input, and it does not name the field.
WCAG-3.3.1.threshold: 100% of automatically detected input errors produce visible text that identifies the item; 0 errors signalled by colour or border change alone.
WCAG-3.3.1.scope_correction: The 'colour or border change alone' clause is breached only on money (blur path). On perio the error is not colour-alone - aria-invalid='true' and a visible sentence are both present; what fails there is the weaker clause, that the visible text identify the item (it is a shared hint 181 px away that names no field). My perio distance is 181 px, not the 142.8 px claimed.
WCAG-3.3.1.why: The money blur state is a clean, daily-flow breach of the must-level clause - .invalid plus an orange border with zero error text and no ARIA - so the root cause stands; the perio row is real but weaker than claimed.
WCAG-3.3.1.fix_direction: Render the same 'Enter an amount above zero' line under money.writeoff.amount on blur with aria-describedby + aria-invalid, and give each perio tag field its own message that names it instead of appending to the shared hint.

INT-verb-labels.my_measurement: Counted .btn elements in #canvas, excluding .held, aria-pressed toggles and the 7 worklist tabs, at 1280 light on a fresh page per state. Board: 62 canvas action buttons, 28 verb-first = 45% ('Details' x25, 'Checkout' x9). Chairs: 18, 12 verb-first = 67% (six .ch-strip buttons read 'Since last visit ... More'). Daily Close: 5 at load with close.sod.roles = 'Roles' = 80%; 7 with the variance tile open, 6 verb-first = 86%. Roles: 12, 1 verb-first = 8% (eleven person-name row buttons); Risk 6/6 = 100%. Encounter: 12, 4 verb-first = 33% (5 procedure picks 'Composite 2-surf D2392' etc., 3 note starters, plus 'Rail' and 'Back to Exams'). Money: 10 after excluding the tabs, 9 verb-first = 90% ('Write-off or adjustment'). Overlays: across the palette, the author PIN pad and the phone approval, 15 of 16 action labels are verb-first = 94% ('Back to results' is the exception; keypad digits exempted). Perio: across load + glove pad + omission gate + tag form, ~20 action buttons after exempting the digit pad, ~8 verb-first = 40% ('Settings', 'Supp', the four licence commit buttons 'Implant'/'Crown margin'/'Patient could not tolerate'/'Third molar absent', six observation buttons). 100% sentence case and 0 labels reading OK / Yes / No / Submit on every screen.
INT-verb-labels.threshold: ≥ 95% of action buttons start with a verb; 100% sentence case; 0 labels that are 'OK', 'Yes', 'No' or 'Submit'
INT-verb-labels.scope_correction: Refuted on checkout-ledger and on signin. Every canvas action button on Checkout is verb-first (Back to Board, Add write-off or adjustment, Post = 3/3) and so is every one on the Ledger (Open Money Desk, Send statement, Preview = 3/3); Sign-in's only canvas action is 'Open my home' = 1/1. The claimed 33%/33%/50% is produced by counting the shared top-bar destinations (Main St, Board, Money Desk, Daily Close, Roles), the theme toggle and the eight rail tabs - navigation, not action buttons - which is the wrong denominator for this threshold and would fail every screen in the product identically. Confirmed on the other 8 screens.
INT-verb-labels.why: Eight of the ten claimed screens have canvas action buttons well under the 95% floor on my own count; checkout-ledger and sign-in reach 100% once navigation and toggles are excluded, so those two rows fall.
INT-verb-labels.fix_direction: Rename 'Details' -> 'Show details', 'Checkout' -> 'Check out', the chairs strip to 'Show more', close.sod.roles -> 'Open Roles', the money primary -> 'Write off a balance', 'Back to results' -> 'Return to results', and put a verb-first control beside the Roles person cell instead of making the name the button.

CDS-ERR-message-prefix.my_measurement: Drove each invalid state on a fresh page at 1280 light and read the live field. Checkout (press Post): checkout.amount aria-invalid null, .invalid absent, aria-describedby -> the unchanged hint 'Prefilled with the patient portion estimate.' which follows the input in DOM order, sits 48 px below it, computes font-weight 400 and colour rgb(61,74,99), with no .sr-only 'Error:' span. Daily Close on a shared device (?device=shared, the only state that renders the PIN): close.pin has aria-invalid null and aria-describedby null; the refusal 'Enter your PIN to post' sits 988 px from the field. Roles day-pass (save with an empty name): roles.daypass.name has aria-invalid='true' but #rl-name-hint follows the input, 48 px below, weight 400, rgb(61,74,99), no hidden prefix; roles.daypass.end the same - 2 of 2. Encounter (press File with killers standing): enc.note.field.assessment and enc.note.field.plan both report aria-invalid null and aria-describedby null with no field-level message at all. Money (blur -50): aria-invalid null, aria-describedby null, orange border only. Overlays: palette.confirm.dob hint follows the input, 48 px below, weight 400, rgb(61,74,99), no prefix; phone.stepup.display has aria-describedby null and aria-invalid null while its short-PIN sentence renders at weight 400 in rgb(154,52,18). Perio: the message precedes the input (appended to #pe-tag-hint) but at weight 400 in rgb(61,74,99) with no .sr-only 'Error:'.
CDS-ERR-message-prefix.threshold: 100% of invalid fields have a preceding, described-by message with the hidden prefix; 0 messages placed only below the input or only as border colour.
CDS-ERR-message-prefix.why: Across all seven claimed screens, 0 of the invalid fields I could produce carry a preceding, described-by message in bold error colour with a hidden 'Error:' prefix; four of them (close, encounter, money, phone step-up) carry no described-by error message at all.
CDS-ERR-message-prefix.fix_direction: On the press that refuses, set aria-invalid on the named field and point aria-describedby at a message element rendered between the label and the input, styled --stop-ink at weight 600 and opened by an .sr-only 'Error:'.

CLT-chip-vocab.my_measurement: Counted visible .chip nodes and distinct labels per route, 1280 light and dark, fresh page each. Board and Temp Board: 105 chips, 29 distinct labels, both themes; chips per .card - the Checkout-queue card 16, board.card.a-1060 (Aiko Tanaka) 5, four more cards at 4. Chairs: 20 chips, vocabulary 12 (passes) but chairs.card.a-1042 carries 8. Roles: 25 chips, vocabulary 14; per table row Dana Whitfield 8, Dr. Blake Reagan 7, Sam Dawson 4, and one SoD decision chip renders 67 px tall against the 29 px of every other. Risk: 4 chips, vocabulary 4. Money: 3 chips / vocabulary 3 at load (passes both clauses), but after pressing Post matched the single 'Delta Dental 835 . era-1' card carries 6 (37 posted, 3 deltas, 1 denial, plus one reason chip per delta row) with vocabulary 5.
CLT-chip-vocab.threshold: chipVocabulary <= 12 and chips per card <= 3 pass. Baseline: Board and Temp Board 29 distinct labels across 105 chips fail; Roles 14 fails; Chairs 12 passes on vocabulary.
CLT-chip-vocab.scope_correction: Within compliance only Roles fails; Risk passes both clauses (4 chips, vocabulary 4, 1 per row). Chairs and Money fail only the per-card clause, not vocabulary - and Money passes both at load, failing only in the post-matched read-back.
CLT-chip-vocab.why: Reproduced the registered baseline exactly - Board 29 distinct labels over 105 chips, Roles 14 - and independently measured per-card counts of 16, 8, 8 and 6 against a ceiling of 3.
CLT-chip-vocab.fix_direction: One status chip per card face; move type/eligibility/alert/entitlement words into a meta line or the existing disclosure, and give the ERA delta rows their reason as text rather than a chip on the batch card.

INT-no-double-submit.my_measurement: Board, 1280 light, fresh page, board.card.a-1042.arrive. page.dblclick -> appointment status 'arrived', appointmentEvents for a-1042 = ['appointment.arrived'], one mutation. Two real mouse clicks 80 ms apart at the same coordinate -> status 'arrived', the same single event; elementFromPoint at that coordinate after the first click resolves to no button at all (the Arrive slot is taken by the arrived stamp, which is where board.js sends focus), so the second click landed on nothing. Two programmatically dispatched detail-1 MouseEvents 80 ms apart -> status 'arrived', one event, second target null. Chairs, a-1042 seated from the Board first, chairs.card.a-1042.ready: dblclick -> encounter.exam_requested count 1; two mouse clicks 80 ms apart -> encounter.exam_requested count 1. Duplicate mutations measured across all four legs on both screens: 0.
INT-no-double-submit.threshold: 0 duplicate mutations across all primary controls under both dblclick and two-clicks-in-300 ms
INT-no-double-submit.scope_correction: Neither claimed screen reproduces a duplicate mutation. What I did reproduce on Chairs is a different defect: the slot 'Ready for exam' vacates is taken by 'Write note', which is kind 'quiet' and so carries no ev.detail guard, and both the dblclick and the two-click leg navigated to #/hygienist/encounter/enc-9001 - a neighbouring control firing once, not the pressed action running twice. The auditor's own board evidence also records 'arrived' exactly once in every leg.
INT-no-double-submit.why: The registered threshold counts duplicate mutations, and I measured zero on every primary control and both gestures; the guard at ui.js:42-43 plus the focus-moves-off-the-slot rule hold. The slot-reuse hazard the auditor actually found is a signifier/afford question, not this heuristic.

CDS-TAG-tint-shade.my_measurement: Read getComputedStyle on every live .chip, 1280 light and dark, fresh page per route. font-size 13px and font-weight 600 on every chip on all eight screens (both clauses pass). Text-on-fill contrast computed from the live colour and the nearest opaque background: light 6.88:1 to 16.86:1, dark 8.58:1 to 11.38:1, 0 pairs below 4.5:1 on any screen (that clause passes too). padding-left and padding-right compute 10px on every chip on every screen, in both themes - components.css:39 sets '.chip { ... padding: 0 10px; }' - against the registered 8px. Non-interactive chips with cursor 'pointer': Chairs 4 (nested in the .ch-strip button, both themes), Daily Close 3 once the variance tile is open (nested in the .dc-loc location buttons), Overlays the palette-row chips (2 visible on a 'Vega' query, one per result row, inheriting pointer from .palette-row). Board, Checkout, Ledger, Risk, Roles, Encounter and Money all measure cursor 'auto', tabindex null, role='status'.
CDS-TAG-tint-shade.threshold: font-size >= 13px; font-weight >= 600; text/background contrast >= 4.5:1 in both themes; padding-x == 8px (prototype 10px fails scale); 0 non-interactive chips with cursor pointer.
CDS-TAG-tint-shade.scope_correction: All eight claimed screens fail the padding clause (a single shared-component defect). The cursor clause fails only on Chairs, Daily Close (tile open) and Overlays; the five other screens pass it.
CDS-TAG-tint-shade.why: Measured 10px horizontal padding on every chip on every claimed screen against a threshold that names 8px, plus pointer-cursor status chips nested inside buttons on three of them; the type and contrast clauses pass exactly as claimed.
CDS-TAG-tint-shade.fix_direction: Set .chip padding to 0 8px and cursor: default in components.css:39, and lift the status chips out of the .ch-strip / .dc-loc / .palette-row buttons.

TYPE-line-height-1.5.my_measurement: base.css:4 sets the body line-height to 1.45; the only overrides above it are .explain .sentence 1.6, .md-* 1.5, .dc-sentences li 1.5, .rl-* 1.5/1.6 and the rail's 1.4. Measured on live nodes that actually wrap to two or more lines, 1280 light unless stated. Daily Close: 6 of 6 wrapping prose elements at 1.45 (15px/21.75px and 13px/18.85px), 9 of 9 with the variance tile open, including the element carrying the .explain and .sentence classes on itself (the 1.6 rule is a descendant selector and does not reach it). Encounter: 5 of 5 at 1.45; Exams the same. Sign-in: the intro .muted wraps at 15px/21.75px = 1.45. Money: at 1280 the .md-* classes do render 1.5 and only one wrapping element measures 1.45; at 420 the page-head .sub wraps to 3 lines at 15px/21.75px = 1.45 and the 'Posts the 37 matched lines...' caption wraps at 13px/18.85px = 1.45, and in the post-matched read-back three .btnrow captions wrap at 1.45. Headings compute 1.2 on every screen, inside the 1.1-1.3 band.
TYPE-line-height-1.5.threshold: Wrapping prose ratio >= 1.5 (prototype body is 1.45 and .rail-msg/.rail-sum .body are 1.4, so they fail; .explain .sentence 1.6 and .md-* 1.5 pass). Headings 1.1 to 1.3.
TYPE-line-height-1.5.scope_correction: Close, encounter and signin fail at every width I measured. Money is width- and state-dependent: at 1280 the money-desk classes that do the wrapping are already at 1.5, and the 1.45 body token only bites at 420 and in the post-matched read-back. Not claimed but equally affected: board, chairs, checkout, roles, risk and phone all carry wrapping prose at 1.45, and the ledger rail adds four elements at 1.4.
TYPE-line-height-1.5.why: The body token is 1.45 and every wrapping prose element that inherits it measures 1.45 on my own reads, which is the wrong side of the 1.5 floor; only the money row needs narrowing, since at 1280 its prose mostly comes from the .md-* rules that already pass.
TYPE-line-height-1.5.fix_direction: Take the base.css body line-height token to 1.5 (22.5px at 15px) and raise .rail-msg / .rail-sum .body off 1.4.

INT-signifiers.my_measurement: Overlays: with the palette open at 1280 light the backdrop is <div class="overlay" data-testid="dialog.backdrop">, role null, tabindex null, computed cursor 'auto' - and ui.js:180-181 attaches a click listener to it; I dispatched a click on it and the dialog count went to 0, so a bare, unstyled div is a working close control. Chairs: at both 1280 and 420 light I measured 0 non-control elements carrying a pointer cursor or a handler outside a control, 0 inert elements styled as buttons, and 0 controls under 44x44 px (the same is true across every other route in this batch - the under-44 count is 0 everywhere). The 4 chairs chips that compute cursor 'pointer' sit inside the .ch-strip <button>: they inherit the cursor, carry no handler of their own, and pressing them presses the strip, so they are neither inert nor non-control handler holders.
INT-signifiers.threshold: 0 non-control elements with handlers; 0 inert elements styled as buttons; 0 controls < 44×44 px
INT-signifiers.scope_correction: Confirmed on overlays only. The chairs row is refuted: all three registered clauses measure 0 on that screen, and the inherited pointer cursor on chips nested inside a real button does not meet any of them (that observation belongs to CDS-TAG-tint-shade, where I did confirm it).
INT-signifiers.why: The dialog backdrop is a non-control element with a click handler that really closes the dialog, which is exactly clause one of the threshold; chairs meets all three clauses and its row falls.
INT-signifiers.fix_direction: Keep the in-dialog Close/Cancel button as the close signifier and give the backdrop a role and cursor (or leave closing to Escape and the button), rather than shipping an unmarked div as a control.

MQ5-prefers-contrast-more.my_measurement: Daily Close at 1280, fresh context with Playwright contrast emulation. matchMedia('(prefers-contrast: more)') returns true and '(prefers-contrast)' returns true, and the page is unchanged: the same 55 text nodes with identical computed colours and identical ratios under 'more' and under 'no-preference', in both themes. grep over prototype/css finds 0 prefers-contrast queries (the only media features present are max-width and prefers-reduced-motion), so the 'no unqualified query' clause passes vacuously and nothing thickens. Light under contrast:more - 3 nodes below the 7:1 requirement: the tile caret ▾ at 20px/400 = 6.2:1, the 'High' chip word at 13px/600 = 6.88:1, and its ▲ glyph at 11px/600 = 6.88:1. Dark under contrast:more - 0 nodes below 7:1 (worst small text 7.6:1). Default state holds in both themes: 0 nodes below 4.5:1 (large text below 3:1).
MQ5-prefers-contrast-more.threshold: Under contrast:more every text pair >= 7:1 (large text >= 4.5:1) in light and dark; default state still >= 4.5:1; 0 unqualified prefers-contrast queries.
MQ5-prefers-contrast-more.scope_correction: Correcting the count: 3 nodes, not 4. The 34px ▲ tile glyph at 5.18:1 is large text and the threshold explicitly allows large text >= 4.5:1, so it passes; the auditor listed it among the failures. Dark passes the 7:1 bar outright, so the failure is light-theme only.
MQ5-prefers-contrast-more.why: There is no prefers-contrast block at all, so contrast:more changes nothing, and in light three small-text pairs remain between 6.2:1 and 6.88:1 - the wrong side of the registered 7:1 floor.
MQ5-prefers-contrast-more.fix_direction: Add a @media (prefers-contrast: more) block that swaps the --ink / severity ramp to a >= 7:1 set (starting with --ink-2, the required chip pair and the caret) and thickens the 1px rails.

WCAG-4.1.3-status-messages.my_measurement:

Board #/frontdesk/board: 107 live regions at load (105 role=status chips + #andon + #live); one Arrive press = 105 role=status nodes removed and 105 re-inserted, 1 #live text write at 65 ms. Close #/owner/close (Keep 90 more days): 5 added / 6 removed, 1 #live write at 61 ms. Money #/biller/money (Post matched): 7 added / 4 removed, 1 #live write at 44 ms; moneydesk.js:35+456 writes the same sentence into BOTH #live and an in-canvas

(reproduced live: both read 'Posted the $20.00 write-off'). Roles #/compliance/roles: 27 live regions at load, one row expand = 25 added / 25 removed, 0 #live writes. Checkout #/frontdesk/checkout/a-1044: 5 added / 5 removed. Perio #/hygienist/perio/enc-9001 operatory 1024x900: depth key '3' after selecting a site = 0 #live text mutations, #live stays empty, 2 live regions replaced. Encounter #/dentist/encounter/enc-9002 with two killers standing: pressing tooth 30 = 3 #live text mutations (clear at 21 ms, then 'Chart or dismiss tag #30' and 'Add an assessment' at 30 ms) and 3 live regions replaced — the press re-announces two gates it did not raise and never announces the tooth. Overlays #/phone/approvals phone 420x900: the step-up PIN submit = 3 live-region text mutations (#live cleared, #andon repainted, #live set) plus 4 live regions added / 4 removed; #live says 'Approved $410.00. Posted with your name as second approver.' while the visible .ph-done says 'Approved $410.00 · posted with your name as second approver · the biller's write-off is on the ledger' (string equality false); on a hygienist seat, Simulate announces 'Request ar-1 is waiting for you' while the card reads 'Nothing waiting for you'. 0 aria-live=assertive and 0 role=alert on every route measured.
WCAG-4.1.3-status-messages.threshold: 100% of focus-keeping state changes produce exactly one #live announcement within 300 ms; <= 2 live-region mutations per action; 0 assertive regions outside stop-severity; 0 duplicate announcements of the same gate.
WCAG-4.1.3-status-messages.scope_correction: Scope holds on all 8 claimed screens and is wider — checkout AND ledger, chairs (34 live regions at load), risk and phone show the same shared-component cause (ui.js:50-55 chip() sets role='status' and every screen re-mounts its canvas). One number corrected: on Encounter I measured 3 #live text mutations per tooth press, not 6, and each gate verb was announced once per press rather than twice; the defect stands (3 > 2, and gates the press did not raise are re-announced while the tooth selection is not announced at all).
WCAG-4.1.3-status-messages.why: Reproduced from clean pages: a single press replaces up to 105 role=status live regions that did not exist at page load, so the per-action live-region budget of 2 is exceeded by two orders of magnitude on the Board and by 4-50x on close, money, roles, checkout and overlays; perio announces nothing at all on its main grammar key, and overlays' #live text does not equal the visible text.
WCAG-4.1.3-status-messages.fix_direction: Drop role='status' from ui.js chip() and from the re-rendered in-canvas sr-only copies, keep #live (and a non-live #andon) as the single persistent channel, and announce perio's apply() sentence through it.

Keyboard-only repeat on a second fresh page: focus the button, Enter -> 119 -> 156, dialogs 0; a second Enter does not re-post (stays 156). Confirming one read-back line: 156 -> 158 in one press, dialogs 0, no undo. Write-off $20.00 (under the $150.00 dual-release threshold): ledger 119 -> 120 on one press, dialogs 0, and the ledger route it writes to offers only Explain / Show patient / Open Money Desk / As of today / Send statement / Preview — no void or reverse. Close #/owner/close, 1280x900 light: Close day opens role=group aria-label 'Confirm close day' with the per-tender read-back and Close day / Cancel (dayCloses stays 6 until confirmed) — that one passes. WCAG-3.3.4.threshold: 100% of money-moving and data-destroying actions satisfy at least one of reversible / checked / confirmed; confirmation dialogs on reversible actions = 0 (the understanding document says each simple save does not need confirmation).
WCAG-3.3.4.scope_correction: Scope confirmed on both claimed screens. Note on the Close row: of its three unguarded presses only 'Match these' and 'Clear with reason' are reconciliation writes; 'Retire' changes the practice dual-release threshold rather than posting money, so it is irreversible-and-unconfirmed but sits at the edge of the 'posts money, voids, deletes' wording. The Money row needs no such allowance.
WCAG-3.3.4.why: Reproduced the headline claim exactly, by pointer and by keyboard, from a clean page: Post matched writes 37 ledger rows on one press with zero dialogs, zero checks and zero reversal controls, and the line confirm and the small write-off behave the same; over-confirmation is 0, so only the under-protection half fails.
WCAG-3.3.4.fix_direction: Put the batch and line posts behind the same read-back step Close day already uses, or expose a 'Reverse this posting' control on the ledger rows they write; and make 'Clear with reason' collect the reason.

Every .btn.irreversible carries ::before content '▮' at 11px (measured on close.closeday, close.decision.d-1.retire, money.era.era-1.postmatched, checkout.post, ledger.statement.send, enc.file, perio.save, phone.request.ar-1.approve, pin 'Go'). Confirm steps: Close day's role=group confirm — h3 'Close Main Street for 9/3?' at 17px weight 600, ::before 'none', 0 .glyph, 0 svg, 0 elements at >= 24px, only the button's 11px ▮. Author PIN pad dialog — bold 'Who is charting?', 0 glyphs, 0 svg, 0 icons >= 24px, Go's ▮ at 11px. Phone step-up dialog — 0 glyphs, 0 svg, no icon >= 24px, consequence sentence 'Approving $410.00 …' at 13px weight 400 (not bold), Approve's ▮ at 11px. Issue day pass on #/owner/roles committed on the first press with no dialog.
CDS-WARNING-text-icon.threshold: 100% of irreversible confirms carry bold text plus an icon >= 24px; icon contrast >= 3:1 in grayscale.
CDS-WARNING-text-icon.scope_correction: 8 of the 9 claimed screens measured directly (board, checkout-ledger, close, compliance, encounter, money, overlays, perio). I could not reach the Chairs 'Ready for exam' outage gate from the seed (no such control renders on #/hygienist/chairs with outage=1), so the chairs row rests on the identical shared refusal component, which I did reproduce under the same outage gate on the Board (■, 15px, 14.2 x 21.8, verb 600) — same numbers the auditor reports for chairs.
CDS-WARNING-text-icon.why: Every warning mark in the product is a 15px text glyph in a ~22px box or an 11px ::before bar, and the three confirm steps that do exist (Close day, the PIN pad, the step-up) carry no icon at 24px or more at all; the bold-text half passes everywhere except the step-up's 13px/400 consequence line.
CDS-WARNING-text-icon.fix_direction: Give .refusal .glyph a fixed 24x24 box (or an inline 24px svg) and put the same mark beside each confirm heading; set the step-up consequence line in the bold weight.

CDS-LABEL-hint-body-size.my_measurement: 1280x900 light, getComputedStyle on live label and .hint nodes; document.body font-size is 15px on every route measured. Checkout 'Amount' label 13px rgb(61,74,99); Encounter 'Assessment' and 'Plan' 13px and every hint line ('Starters fill both fields…', 'Checks run when you leave a field', 'Filing as Dr. Hana Kim…', 'Today charges at File…') 13px; Money write-off form 'Write-off amount' and 'Reason code' 13px with the dual-release hint 13px; Compliance day-pass form 'Name', 'Role', 'Location', 'Shift end', 'Extra entitlements (not in the role)' all 13px with five hints at 13px; Close shared desk 'Your PIN' 13px and 'Shared desk: the PIN makes you the frozen poster…' 13px; Perio tag form 'Tooth' and 'Observation' 13px; Overlays palette confirm 'Date of birth' 13px with its hint 13px, author pad hint 13px, step-up prose 13px. Single shared cause: components.css:23 '.field label { font-size: var(--fs-1) }' and :27 '.hint { font-size: var(--fs-1) }' with --fs-1 = 13px and --fs-2 = 15px. Hint colour rgb(61,74,99) on the white/near-white ground is ~8.9:1, well over the 4.5:1 clause.
CDS-LABEL-hint-body-size.threshold: label font-size >= body font-size (13px vs 15px fails); hint font-size >= body font-size; hint contrast >= 4.5:1 (NHS grey-1 on white is ~7:1).
CDS-LABEL-hint-body-size.why: Every label and hint on all seven claimed screens computes 13px against a 15px body — the exact 13-vs-15 case the threshold names — from one shared CSS rule; only the contrast clause passes.
CDS-LABEL-hint-body-size.fix_direction: Set .field label and .hint to var(--fs-2) (the body size) and carry the secondary meaning with colour rather than size.

TYPE-scale-no-offscale.threshold: Zero off-scale declarations (components.css currently has 11 at 9/10/11/12/13/14/15px); zero off-scale computed sizes; <= 5 distinct sizes per screen (baseline: board 5 incl. 11px, money 6, encounter 7, perio 6 incl. 10px).
TYPE-scale-no-offscale.scope_correction: Screens confirmed as claimed and the defect is wider — checkout (6 distinct, incl. 11 and 12px), ledger (6, incl. 11px) and perio (6, incl. 10px on 168 nodes) also exceed or carry off-scale sizes. One number corrected: components.css holds 12 hard-coded off-scale declarations, not the 11 the threshold text quotes. Signin's row is right on the off-scale clause only — at 5 distinct sizes it does NOT breach the <= 5 ceiling.

MQ5-forced-colors.my_measurement: Chromium with page.emulateMedia({forcedColors:'active'}) — matchMedia('(forced-colors: active)').matches verified true in-page — 1280x900 (phone leg 420x900). Close #/owner/close: 8 visible canvas controls, 2 compute border-width 0px with outline-style none — close.decision.d-1.why and close.approvals.why (both <summary>); the chips do pick up a 1px rgb(0,0,0) border, so chip state is not background-only. Author PIN pad at #/frontdesk/board: 15 controls in the dialog, 2 keep no border — pin.display and pin.why; the dialog element itself computes border-width 0px. Phone step-up at #/phone/approvals device=phone: 14 controls, 1 keeps no border — phone.stepup.display; dialog border-width 0px. Source check: grep -rn 'forced-colors' over /home/user/Dental_Mgmt/prototype/css and /prototype/js returns no match — the only @media feature query in tokens.css is prefers-reduced-motion (tokens.css:89).
MQ5-forced-colors.threshold: 100% of interactive controls have >= 1px visible border/outline under forced colours; 100% of focus rings visible; 0 states conveyed only by background; >= 1 forced-colors block in the shared CSS.
MQ5-forced-colors.scope_correction: Both claimed screens confirmed, with two count corrections. Close: 2 borderless summaries in the default collapsed state, not 3 — close.counts.why only exists once the variance tile is expanded, so the third instance needs an extra press. Overlays: the author pad loses 2 of 15 controls (pin.display AND pin.why), i.e. 13 of 15 keep a border rather than 13 of 14; the step-up loses 1 of 14 as claimed, and both dialog boxes compute 0px.
MQ5-forced-colors.why: The CSS contains zero @media (forced-colors: active) blocks against a required minimum of one, and under emulated forced colours the PIN entry fields and several summary toggles lose every boundary while the modal boxes themselves have no edge.
MQ5-forced-colors.fix_direction: Add a forced-colors block that gives the PIN displays, the dialog box and every <summary> a ButtonBorder/CanvasText border and pins the focus ring to Highlight.

WCAG-1.4.1.my_measurement: Close #/owner/close at 1280x900, light and dark. Non-colour cues are complete: every visible .chip carries both a .glyph and a word (glyph-less 0, word-less 0) in both themes, the refusal carries its block glyph plus an sr-only severity word plus a 6px left rail, and every .btn.irreversible renders ::before content '▮' (close.closeday, close.decision.d-1.retire, and with the variance tile open close.variance.v-1.match and the confirm Close day). The luminance ladder fails. Reading the severity soft fills straight off :root in the live page — light stop #FEF2F2, required #FFF7ED, review #FFFBEB, style #F5F3FF, info #F8FAFC, clear #ECFDF5; dark #3A1414 / #3B1F0E / #3A2A08 / #2A1A4A / #1F2937 / #0F2E26 — and computing WCAG relative luminance: light stop .9099, required .9390, review .9625, style .9073, info .9536, clear .9468; dark stop .0145, required .0194, review .0257, style .0173, info .0215, clear .0220. Against the registered order stop < required < review < style < info < clear that is 2 inversions in light (review > style, info > clear) and 1 in dark (review > style).
WCAG-1.4.1.threshold: 100% of severity chips and refusal blocks carry a non-colour cue; 100% of .btn.irreversible show the bar glyph; severity luminance order is strictly monotonic in both themes (0 inversions).
WCAG-1.4.1.scope_correction: Screen scope confirmed (Close), and the cause is a tokens.css ladder shared by every screen. Correction to which pairs invert: measured against the full six-step registered order the inversions are review-over-style in both themes plus info-over-clear in light — the auditor named review/info and clear/info because the collapsed Close screen shows no style chip. The inversion counts they report (2 light, 1 dark) are right; the pairs are not.
WCAG-1.4.1.why: The non-colour-cue half of the rule passes on every chip, refusal and irreversible button I measured, but the severity soft-fill luminances are not monotonic in either theme, so grayscale readers cannot rank severities by fill — 2 inversions light, 1 dark, against a threshold of 0.
WCAG-1.4.1.fix_direction: Reorder the --*-soft values in tokens.css so luminance rises strictly stop < required < review < style < info < clear in both themes.

INT-instructions-before-input.my_measurement: Fresh page per screen at 1280 light, snapshot of every input/textarea/select BEFORE any typing, then submit-empty. The word 'required' appears nowhere in the canvas on any of the seven screens and not one control carries required or aria-required. Checkout: checkout.amount required=false, hint 'Prefilled with the patient portion estimate.'; Post with no tender raises 'Choose a tender' and with a blank amount 'Type an amount above zero' - both rules first stated in the refusal. Close (device=shared): close.pin required=false (the auditor's 'requiredMarked true' is wrong in the prototype's favour - it is not marked), maxlength=6, inputmode=numeric, hint 'Shared desk: the PIN makes you the frozen poster for every posting here.' with no length and no lock-out; the constraint lives only in the refusal Why, shell.js:84 'Six digits at most. Three misses lock this device for five minutes.' Compliance: roles.daypass.name required=false, first press raises 'Name the temp before issuing the pass'; as the compliance lead (Noor Ali, entitlements ['review_logs']) three presses issued 0 passes behind 'Ask a seat that grants roles - Dismiss', with nothing before the press saying so. Encounter: enc.note.field.assessment required=false, no hint, gate 'Add an assessment' only after blur. Money: money.writeoff.amount required=false, hint names only the $150 dual-release, gate 'Choose a reason code' first states the reason rule. Overlays: the author pad's only instruction is 'Enter the other person's PIN' (no digit count anywhere in the dialog before the press); the phone step-up does print 'Four to six digits.' Perio: perio.tag.tooth required=false (min=1 max=32 constrained), perio.tag.text required=false maxlength=140, and 'Tooth must be 1 to 32 and present in the mouth.' / 'Say what you saw.' are appended to the hint only after a touch or a refusal (perio.js:248).
INT-instructions-before-input.threshold: 100% of required fields marked before submit; 0 constraints revealed only in a refusal
INT-instructions-before-input.why: Reproduced on all seven claimed screens from clean pages: 0% of required fields are marked before submit and at least one constraint per screen is first stated inside a refusal, on both sides of the threshold.
INT-instructions-before-input.fix_direction: Put the requirement and the format in the label or the standing hint (tender group and Amount 'required, above $0.00'; PIN '6 digits, three misses lock this device'; Name 'required'; Assessment 'required'; reason code 'required'; Tooth '1-32, present teeth only'), and hold 'Add day pass' for a seat without grant_roles.

AXE-RUN-all-contexts.my_measurement: Vendored axe-core 4.13.0 (scripts/vendor/axe-core/axe.min.js) injected with addScriptTag, runOnly tags wcag2a/wcag2aa/wcag21a/wcag21aa/wcag22aa/best-practice, fresh context per leg. #/owner/close collapsed at 1280 light and dark: 0 violations - which is exactly what the repository harness records (a11y-baseline.json and a11y-after-fix.json both show owner/close v=0 in all six contexts, and scripts/a11y-check.mjs gives that route no drive function and never runs 320). One click on close.tied.tile at 1280 light AND dark: 1 violation, aria-required-children, impact critical, 5 nodes - #dc-loc-loc-3 'Element has children which are not allowed: [role=group]', .head.tender[role=row] 'Required ARIA children role not present: cell, columnheader, gridcell, rowheader', and close.tender.cash / .check / .card each 'has children which are not allowed: [role=status]'. At 320 (device=phone) with the tile, all three locations, close.variance.v-1.investigate and the Confirm close day group open: 2 violations, 15 nodes - aria-required-children critical 10 nodes (the five above plus the five Confirm close day rows) and aria-required-parent critical 5 nodes, every row in div[aria-label='Confirm close day'] 'Required ARIA parents role not present: grid, rowgroup, table, treegrid'. Identical in dark. Source confirms the shape: dailyclose.js:178-181 (role=table whose rows hold plain spans and a role=status chip, with role=group variance cards appended into the table) and :320-324 (role=row rows inside a role=group with no table wrapper).
AXE-RUN-all-contexts.threshold: 0 violations across all contexts (currently the script tolerates moderate/minor; the audit must not). 0 contexts with an error (an errored context is a missing measurement, never a pass).
AXE-RUN-all-contexts.scope_correction: Same defect is present in dark as well as light, which the row did not say; it is theme-independent.
AXE-RUN-all-contexts.why: The exact rule ids, impacts and node counts reproduce (5 nodes at 1280 with the tile, 15 nodes at 320 with the confirm open) against 0 violations in the collapsed state the harness is the only state it scans, so the harness must be extended to drive the tile, the confirm group and 320.
AXE-RUN-all-contexts.fix_direction: Give the .tender spans role=cell/columnheader, move the variance cards and the role=status Gap chips out of the role=table subtree, wrap the Confirm close day rows in a role=table, and add a close driver plus a 320 width to scripts/a11y-check.mjs.

CLT-proximity-ratio.my_measurement: Computed gaps read off live nodes at 1280 light on every claimed route, plus measured getBoundingClientRect distances between consecutive visible children. Within-group is 8px everywhere: .btnrow 8, .seg 8, .actions/.ch-actions 8, .pad 8, .pinpad 8, .odont 8, table.perio border-spacing 8. Between-group is 12px (.stack on checkout, ledger, close, risk, roles, encounter, money, perio; .ch-list 12 on chairs; .phone 12 on the phone surface) or 8px (.worklist on board, risk, exams, money read-back; .opcol 8 on board). Measured card-to-card distances confirm 12 and 8. Ratios: 12/8 = 1.5 and 8/8 = 1.0. No container on any of the nine screens reaches 2.
CLT-proximity-ratio.threshold: Ratio >= 2 (Ant Design tiers 8 / 16 / 24) passes; ratio < 2 fails.
CLT-proximity-ratio.scope_correction: Also fails on signin, exams and the phone approvals surface, which the row did not list - it is a token-level defect on every screen, not nine of them.
CLT-proximity-ratio.why: Every between-group container computes 8 or 12px against an 8px within-group gap, so the best ratio anywhere is 1.5 and the worst is 1.0, both under the registered 2.
CLT-proximity-ratio.fix_direction: Move .stack / .worklist / .opcol / .ch-list to var(--space-4) 16px or var(--space-5) 24px and leave the within-group containers at var(--gap) 8px.

INT-exit-and-undo.my_measurement: Driven from clean pages at 1280 (phone legs at 420). Dialog half: the author pad on Board closes on Escape, carries a visible Cancel, role=dialog aria-modal=true, and returns focus to topbar.author; the palette closes on Escape with a visible Close and returns focus to topbar.search; the phone step-up closes on Escape with a visible Cancel and returns focus to phone.request.ar-1.approve - 3 of 3 pass. Close, compliance, encounter, money and perio render 0 dialogs, so the dialog clauses are vacuous there. Inverse half fails on every claimed screen: Board has 8 distinct .btn.reversible labels (Checkout, Re-verify, Arrive, Re-verify all, Sign out, Call lab, Add day pass, Ping chair) and after Arrive and after Seat the page contains 0 buttons matching undo|unseat|unarrive|revert|reopen|withdraw|cancel - 0%.
