Close: 'Keep 90 more days' and 'Tighten' each replace the three decision buttons with a stamp leaving 0 decision controls and 0 inverse controls, and Escape does not close the Confirm close day group (group still present, focus unchanged) although its Cancel does and returns focus to close.closeday. Compliance: the day pass form's Add button really does toggle to Cancel (roles.js:301), but issuing a pass leaves 0 inverse controls, and a second press on Renew / Assign / Start only announces 'Already requested today' / 'Already assigned today' / 'Already opened today'. Encounter: a note starter overwrote a hand-typed Assessment and Plan with template text, with 0 confirm dialogs and 0 inverse controls; a tag dismissed with a reason leaves the row as '▬ Dismissed Reason: ...' with 0 enc.tag.* controls of any kind. Money: the write-off form offers only Courtesy / Hardship / Prior period / Post - no Cancel - and Escape leaves it open. Overlays: Simulate created request ar-2 with 0 controls to withdraw it. Perio: the glove pad has 15 keys and no Previous tooth; 'Next tooth' moved Tooth 2 to Tooth 3 and the pad's own ⌫ undo did not move it back.
INT-exit-and-undo.threshold: 100% of dialogs close on Escape and have a visible Cancel; focus returns to opener in 100%; >= 95% of reversible actions have an on-screen inverse
INT-exit-and-undo.scope_correction: The Board row's 'the PIN pad returns focus' and Overlays' dialog findings are right; the failing clause on all seven screens is the >= 95% inverse clause, and on Close additionally the Escape clause for the Confirm close day group (which is a group, not a dialog, so it is strictly outside the dialog clause).
INT-exit-and-undo.why: Every claimed screen has at least one reversible act that leaves no on-screen inverse - Arrive and Seat (0 of 8 on Board), Keep and Tighten on Close, an issued day pass and a repeated risk action on Compliance, the starter overwrite and the dismissed tag on Encounter, the whole write-off form on Money, Simulate on the phone, Next tooth on the perio pad - so no screen reaches the 95% floor.
INT-exit-and-undo.fix_direction: Emit a short-lived quiet 'Undo' beside each of these acts (unarrive/unseat, undo this review, reopen tag, undo starter, cancel the write-off, withdraw the simulated request, previous tooth) and let Escape close the Confirm close day group.

TYPE-measure-80ch.my_measurement: Registered method: clientWidth divided by the canvas-measured average glyph width of 'abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz ' in each element's computed font, at 1280 light. max-width computes to 'none' on every prose element on every screen. Close at idle: 6 of 10 prose elements over 80ch (137, 129, 117, 101, ...); fully expanded (tile, three locations, changed, late, both count lines, Investigate, confirm group, all details open) 22 of 28 over 80, widest 153ch. Money: page-head sub 101ch, .md-batchline 129ch, .md-plain / .md-next 126ch, aging intro 149ch - matching the row exactly. Signin: the intro p is 760px at 15px = 91ch (avg glyph 8.31px, the same figure the row reports). Encounter: only one prose element clears 80 at idle - 'Today charges at File - Planned estimates - Existing is history' in a 658px box at 13px = 91ch, not the 101ch the row states; 'Tap a dashed surface to confirm, again to remove' renders only once a tooth is selected. The row's 13px arithmetic is off (658/101 implies a 6.51px glyph where the same font measures 7.23px at 13px); the 15px figures agree exactly.
TYPE-measure-80ch.threshold: chars <= 80 for every prose element (must, WCAG); chars <= 75 for body prose (should).
TYPE-measure-80ch.scope_correction: Wider than the four claimed screens: prose over 80ch at 1280 light also on board (173), chairs (173), checkout (111), ledger (125), risk (149), roles (153), exams (173) and perio (173). Only the phone approvals surface (max 55ch, .phone max-width 420px) passes.
TYPE-measure-80ch.why: Every prose container on the product has max-width 'none' and the measured measure runs past 80ch on 12 of 13 surfaces, so the claim stands; only the Encounter row's character count needs correcting from 101ch to 91ch (still over the cap).
TYPE-measure-80ch.fix_direction: Give p / li / .explain .sentence / .sub / .small a max-width of about 44em inside the page containers, leaving grids, tables and button strips at full width.

WCAG-1.3.2-meaningful-sequence.my_measurement: 1280 light and dark, plus 1024/420/320 legs: 0 elements anywhere in the document compute a non-zero CSS order on either route, and DOM order is visual order - the order clause passes exactly as the row concedes. The live-text clause fails. Close: pressing Clear announces 'Cleared with reason' with 1 of 3 words and no verbatim match anywhere in the canvas; Match announces 'Matched $312.40 at Hillsboro' with only 'Hillsboro' on screen; 'Tightened the write-off threshold' and 'Retired the raised threshold' appear nowhere verbatim; the support number 615-555-0100 is not in document.body.innerText at all. Only 'Kept 90 more days' is present verbatim. Compliance risk: 'Already requested today', 'Already assigned today', 'Audit log opened' and 'Already opened today' all announce words that are nowhere in the canvas - the row keeps its first-press sentence and shows nothing new.
WCAG-1.3.2-meaningful-sequence.threshold: 0 elements with non-zero order; DOM order == visual order for 100% of grid-area children at every breakpoint; 100% of live texts present as visible text.
WCAG-1.3.2-meaningful-sequence.why: Reproduced on both screens: two of three registered clauses pass, but five announcements on Close and four on Compliance carry meaning that never reaches visible text, against a 100% bar.
WCAG-1.3.2-meaningful-sequence.fix_direction: Render each announcement where it happens - a cleared/matched stamp in the location row, a '◆ Already requested today' line on the risk row, and the support number on screen rather than only in #live.

CDS-TYPE-two-weights.my_measurement: Distinct computed font-weights over every visible text node, 1280 light. Chairs canvas 400 / 500 / 600 (500 on the 15 .btn.ch-strip text nodes, components.css:215) plus 700 on .brand = 4 document-wide. Checkout 400 / 600 / 700 and Ledger 400 / 600 / 700 (700 on table th). Compliance risk 400 / 600 in canvas + 700 .brand = 3; roles 400 / 600 / 700 in the canvas itself. Encounter canvas 400 (6 nodes) / 600 (60) / 700 (1) = 3, matching the row's 6/58/1. Money: the default ERA tab is 400 / 600 in canvas, but money.tab.denials renders 700 on the bold 'Next:' lead-in, giving 400 / 600 / 700 - the row's state reproduces. Signin canvas 400 (4) / 500 (9, components.css:157 .personas .btn .role) / 600 (27) plus 700 .brand = 4.
CDS-TYPE-two-weights.threshold: Distinct computed weights <= 2 and the bold one is 600 or 700; any 500 occurrence fails.
CDS-TYPE-two-weights.scope_correction: Also fails outside the six claimed screens: board (400/600/700), close (400/500/600/700 - one 500 node), exams (400/600/700) and perio (400/500/600, 168 of the 500s being the .ghost prior depths, components.css:90).
CDS-TYPE-two-weights.why: Every claimed screen renders three or four distinct weights, and chairs and signin additionally render the forbidden 500, on the failing side of both halves of the threshold.
CDS-TYPE-two-weights.fix_direction: Drop font-weight 500 from .btn.ch-strip, .personas .btn .role and .psite .ghost, and set table th and .brand to 600 so the product carries 400 and 600 only.

TYPE-tabular-money.my_measurement: Every text node matching a money pattern, with getComputedStyle fontVariantNumeric and textAlign on its parent, 1280 light (identical dark). Chairs: expanding chairs.card.a-1050 renders 'Balance $0.00 - $95.00 credit - Provider Bree L.' in a class-less <span> with font-variant-numeric: normal, text-align start - the only money on the screen, 0 tabular. Close fully expanded: 18 money nodes, 10 tabular - the .num tender cells and the confirm read-back are tabular and right-aligned, while the '▲ Gap −$312.40' and '▲ Variance $312.40' chips and every in-prose amount compute normal and align start. Money: the three read-back Confirm labels are .btn.irreversible with font-variant-numeric normal and text-align center ('Confirm - post $540.00, write-off $50.00', $214.00/$71.00, $208.00/$52.00), and span.amt '$410.00 open' is tabular but text-align start; the Variances tab adds three more non-tabular amounts (span.obj, span.muted proposed match, p.md-plain). Phone approvals after Simulate: .ph-amount is tabular; the .ph-sentence, the .ph-why p.small muted, the simulate button label and the sim note are all normal, and the andon's span.grow ('Write-off $410.00 on LF - MRN-306...') is normal too.
TYPE-tabular-money.threshold: 100% of money strings tabular and right-aligned; 100% of times and counts tabular.
TYPE-tabular-money.why: On all four claimed screens money is rendered in plain spans, button labels and prose that compute font-variant-numeric: normal and are not right-aligned, so none of them reaches the 100% bar.
TYPE-tabular-money.fix_direction: Add font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums to .chip, .ph-sentence, .ph-why, .obj and .btn labels that carry money, wrap in-prose and in-detail amounts in the existing .amt span, and right-align money in columns.

WCAG-1.4.6.my_measurement: Per-text-node contrast against the nearest opaque ancestor background, sRGB luminance, 7:1 for normal text and 4.5:1 for large (>= 24px, or >= 18.66px bold). Close at 1280, fully expanded (tile, three locations, changed, late, both count lines, Investigate, Confirm close day, all details open): light 103 of 118 visible text nodes reach the enhanced ratio = 87.3% (the row says 88% of 129 - the same measurement); dark 115 of 118 = 97.5% (row: 98%). The shortfall is 6 aria-hidden severity glyphs at 3.07:1, 3 more at 6.88:1, one caret at 6.20:1, four 13px .chip.required labels at 6.88:1 and one 13px summary at 6.24:1. Excluding the aria-hidden decorative glyphs the light figure is 92 of 97 = 94.8%, which would pass the 90% gate - so the close row only fails if decorative-but-visible glyphs are counted. Perio at 1024 light: 224 of 249 non-aria-hidden nodes = 89.96% (row: 89.6%), just under the gate, with 24 .psite.missing 'x' at 5.89:1 and one .btn.reversible label at 6.94:1; counting the 168 aria-hidden 10px .ghost prior depths as the visible text they are, 418 nodes and 53.8% (row: 53.6%). Dark perio 100% non-hidden, 99.8% with the ghosts. Primary --ink body text and the form labels are at 100% in both themes on both screens.
WCAG-1.4.6.threshold: >= 7:1 for normal text, >= 4.5:1 for large text; pass when >= 90% of visible text nodes meet it and primary body text (--ink) and form labels are at 100%.
WCAG-1.4.6.scope_correction: Perio fails on its own (89.96% excluding aria-hidden, 53.8% including the ghosts). Close fails only when the aria-hidden decorative severity glyphs are counted as visible text nodes (87.3%); excluding them it is 94.8% and passes. The genuinely non-decorative shortfall on Close is narrower than the row implies: four 13px chip labels at 6.88:1 and one 13px summary at 6.24:1.
WCAG-1.4.6.why: Both rows' numbers reproduce within half a point, but the Close row's failure depends entirely on counting aria-hidden decorative glyphs; Perio fails on its visible text alone.
WCAG-1.4.6.fix_direction: Lift --ink-3 and --required-ink to 7:1 on white and cream so the 13px chip and summary labels clear the bar, and raise the 10px .ghost prior depths in size and ink.

WCAG-2.4.13.my_measurement: #/dentist/encounter/enc-9002, focus applied to each edge tooth and computed style read live. The ring is outline 3px solid rgb(43,108,184) at outline-offset 2px on every control, so it needs 5px of slack. .enc-odont-wrap computes overflow-x: auto, overflow-y: auto, padding 0px 0px 4px (padding-left and padding-right 0). At 1280 desk: enc.tooth.1 leftSlack 0.0 and topSlack 0.0; enc.tooth.16 rightSlack 0.4, topSlack 0.0; enc.tooth.17 rightSlack 0.4, bottomSlack 4.0; enc.tooth.32 leftSlack 0.0, bottomSlack 4.0 - 4 of 4 sampled edge teeth clipped. At 1024 operatory: enc.tooth.1 and enc.tooth.32 leftSlack 0.0 and enc.tooth.16/17 topSlack 0.0 / bottomSlack 4.0 still clipped (right edges clear at 142px). Ring colour against the surface is unchanged elsewhere and meets the 3:1 change clause.
WCAG-2.4.13.threshold: outline-width >= 2 CSS px on all four sides (unclipped) and >= 3:1 change; 0 clipped rings. AAA in WCAG 2.2, so scored as should.
WCAG-2.4.13.scope_correction: Worse than claimed: the clipping is not only on the inline edges. Because the wrap has zero block padding at the top and 4px at the bottom, every tooth in the upper arch has its top ring clipped (topSlack 0.0) and every tooth in the lower arch its bottom ring clipped (bottomSlack 4.0 < 5) at both widths, not just the first and last tooth of each arch.
WCAG-2.4.13.why: The 3px ring at 2px offset needs 5px and the scroll container gives 0px inline, 0px top and 4px bottom, so rings are provably clipped at 1280 and 1024 on the screen's main control.
WCAG-2.4.13.fix_direction: Give .enc-odont-wrap 5px of padding on all four sides (or scroll-padding plus block padding) so a 3px ring at 2px offset draws a closed perimeter inside the scroller.

INT-irreversible-identity.my_measurement: Fresh page per leg, 1280 desk light unless noted. chairs (#/hygienist/chairs after seating a-1042 from the Board): chairs.card.a-1042.ready is class "btn irreversible"; one click -> status seated->ready_for_exam, appointmentEvents 6->7, 0 dialogs, focus moves to #chairs-queue-a-1042, button gone, 0 undo/withdraw controls. checkout (#/frontdesk/checkout/a-1044): tender card chosen, checkout.post "btn irreversible", one click -> ledger 119->120, credits 1->2, collectionDecisions 1->2, allocationIntents 1->2, 0 dialogs. ledger (#/biller/ledger/p-319): ledger.statement.send "btn irreversible", one click -> disclosures 0->1, 0 dialogs. close (#/owner/close): close.variance.v-1.match "btn irreversible", one click -> reconciliationMatches 0->1, 0 dialogs; close.variance.v-1.clear is "btn quiet" (an irreversible mutation not wearing the identity). compliance (#/owner/roles): roles.daypass.save "btn irreversible", name + shift end filled, one click -> dayPasses 0->1, userEntitlements 0->1, 0 dialogs, 0 held, 0 revoke/undo controls, focus to #rl-issued-head. money (#/biller/money): money.era.era-1.postmatched "btn irreversible", one click -> ledger 119->156 (37 rows), 0 dialogs. overlays (#/phone/approvals, phone 420): phone.request.ar-1.decline is class "btn reversible"; two presses (open reason, type, press again) -> approvals ar-1 status "declined" reason "appeal first", chip "Sent back", and the only canvas button left is phone.simulate (0 reopen/undo/reverse). perio (#/hygienist/perio/enc-9001): perio.tag.save "btn irreversible", one click -> tags 1->2, 0 dialogs.
INT-irreversible-identity.threshold: 100% of irreversible mutations behind .btn.irreversible; 100% have a two-step confirm; 0 identity pairs distinguishable by hue only
INT-irreversible-identity.why: Every screen named reproduces on the two-step clause: on the clear path the first press writes the store with zero dialogs and zero held steps, and two screens also break the identity clause (Close's "Clear with reason" is .btn.quiet, the phone's "Send back" is .btn.reversible while writing an undoable-by-nobody decision). I re-measured the perio row through Save tag rather than the 168-site clean save; one counterexample is enough to fall below 100%.
INT-irreversible-identity.fix_direction: Route the first press of Ready for exam, Post, Send statement, Match these, Post matched, Issue day pass and Save tag into the held read-back step that Close day already uses, and give Clear with reason / Send back the irreversible identity (or a real inverse).

WCAG-1.4.12.my_measurement: Sign-in at 1280, both themes, with the registered override injected (* line-height 1.5 / letter-spacing .12em / word-spacing .16em, p margin-bottom 2em). The three numbers reproduce exactly: signin.persona.frontdesk scrollWidth 249 vs clientWidth 244, .biller 250 vs 244, .temp 251 vs 244. But every one of those buttons computes overflow-x: visible / overflow-y: visible, and so does each ancestor (.personas and .signin visible, .canvas overflow auto with its right edge at 1280). Painted text extents (Range client rects): frontdesk right 511 vs button right 508, biller 768 vs 764, temp 1025 vs 1020 (viewport 1280). document.documentElement.scrollWidth 1280 === innerWidth 1280, so nothing is pushed off-screen or into a scroller. 0 overlapping control pairs; the nearest neighbour starts 5 px and 4 px after each spill. At 420 (single column) 0 button overflow, 0 clipping. Screenshot at verify/probes/b6/signin-ts.png: all nine labels render in full.
WCAG-1.4.12.threshold: 0 clipped or overlapping elements after the override; every control still readable and clickable.
WCAG-1.4.12.why: The auditor's numbers are right but the threshold reading is not: the registered test says to assert scrollWidth <= clientWidth "or overflow is visible/auto", and here overflow is visible all the way up, so nothing is clipped, nothing is lost, nothing overlaps and every control stays readable and clickable. The three labels spill 3-5 px over their own 2 px border into the 8 px grid gap - a cosmetic crowding, not a text-spacing failure.

CLT-similarity-identity.my_measurement: Re-classified every visible <button> (the registered measure's population) on 14 routes x 2 themes x 1280/1024, fresh page each. byIdentity.other at 1280 light: board 4 (topbar.author .authorchip + board.chair.1/2/3 .chair), temp-board 4, chairs 1, checkout 1, ledger 1, close 2 (authorchip + close.tied.tile), risk 1, roles 1, money 1, encounter 33 (authorchip + 32 .tooth/.tooth.enc-tagged), exams 1, perio 193 (authorchip + 192 .psite), phone 1. Identical at 1024 and in dark. Only signin is clean (quiet 21 / reversible 1 / other 0). With Daily Close's tile opened the off-identity set on close grows to 6 buttons (tile, close.location.loc-1/2/3 at weight 400, close.changed and close.late .dc-line), and opening the command palette adds <button class="palette-row"> (1 px border, weight 400) against .btn quiet's 2 px / 600.
CLT-similarity-identity.threshold: byIdentity.other === 0 on every screen and <= 4 distinct identity tuples product-wide (excluding aria-pressed/aria-current states). Baseline: Board 4 'other', Money 1, Chairs 1, Close/Checkout 1 fail.
CLT-similarity-identity.scope_correction: All nine claimed screens reproduce. The defect is wider than claimed: Exams also carries 1 (the author chip) and the temp Board carries 4, so 13 of the 14 routes fail - every signed-in screen. Only sign-in passes.
CLT-similarity-identity.why: Every claimed screen measures byIdentity.other > 0 against a threshold of exactly 0, and the shell's .authorchip alone puts a fifth button look on every signed-in route, so the product-wide tuple count is over four as well.
CLT-similarity-identity.fix_direction: Re-class .authorchip, .chair, .tooth, .psite, .tile/.dc-loc/.dc-line and .palette-row as .btn.quiet variants, or register the compound instruments (odontogram, perio grid) as role=grid so they leave the per-button population.

WCAG-3.2.4-consistent-identification.my_measurement: Fresh page per screen, 1280 light, plus driven states. Held-button contract ("reads exactly Held, aria-label 'Held: <what>'"): checkout.post under its gate = visible "Held", aria "Held: Post" (correct); chairs.card.a-1042.ready under outage = visible "Held", aria "Ready for exam held: Wait for the server - the exam queue is read-only", title "Ready for exam"; ledger.statement.send under outage = visible "Held", aria "Send statement is held: Wait for the server - statements cannot send". Three name shapes for one state. Labels mapped to more than one identity: board "Sign out" quiet+reversible, "Checkout" quiet+reversible, "Arrive" quiet+reversible; checkout/ledger "Send statement" quiet (checkout.collect.seg.send-statement) + irreversible (ledger.statement.send). Suffixes with more than one label: checkout/ledger "why" = 3 ("Why this decision", "Why this estimate", "Why this statement") and "close" = 2; compliance "open" = 2 ("Open", "Open Daily Close"); money "why" = 2 across tabs ("Why are 37 already matched?", "Why this code"); perio "save" = 2 ("Save exam" perio.save, "Save tag" perio.tag.save, both irreversible). Chip words outside ui.js STATUS/TYPE/ELIG: board 17 of 29, chairs 8 of 12, checkout+ledger 3 of 4, compliance 18 of 18, money 3 of 3, phone/palette 2 of 2, perio "Tagged #2 - waiting for dentist" after a tag save. Overlays PIN pads: the author pad (.pinpad from topbar.author) has role null, aria-label null and no length sentence ("Enter the other person's PIN"); the phone step-up pad has role="group", aria-label "PIN keypad" and "Four to six digits." One refusal, two control words: empty Go -> refusal.control "Clear and retype", wrong PIN -> "Enter PIN", both with verb "Retype the PIN - no match".
WCAG-3.2.4-consistent-identification.threshold: 0 testid suffixes with > 1 label; 0 labels mapped to > 1 identity; 0 chip words outside the shared tables; 0 support-line wordings other than SUPPORT.
WCAG-3.2.4-consistent-identification.scope_correction: All seven claimed screens reproduce. Two corrections: (a) on checkout-ledger a label DOES map to two identities - "Send statement" is quiet on the Checkout collect segment and irreversible on the Ledger - which the row said did not happen; (b) on money I reproduce two "why" labels through the tabs, not three (the third, money.era.line.*.why, needs the ERA read-back drawer).
WCAG-3.2.4-consistent-identification.why: Every clause of the threshold is breached on the claimed screens: suffixes with more than one label, labels with more than one identity, chip vocabulary outside the shared tables, and at least three different accessible-name shapes for the one "Held" state.
WCAG-3.2.4-consistent-identification.fix_direction: Let ui.js btn() own the held name (drop every 'X held:' / 'X is held:' ariaLabel override), split the overloaded 'why'/'open'/'save'/'close' suffixes, and move the screen-local chip words into the shared STATUS/TYPE/ELIG tables.

TYPE-min-any-text-12.my_measurement: Text-node and pseudo-element sweep, fresh page, 1280 and 1024, both themes. perio (#/hygienist/perio/enc-9001): 168 .psite .ghost prior-depth values at 10 px (72 '3', 69 '2', 12 '4', 15 '5'), identical at every width and theme; only the active cell's prior value is echoed in >= 12 px text. encounter (#/dentist/encounter/enc-9002): at load one sub-12 px node, the aria-hidden chip glyph at 11 px; after charting tooth 3 the '●' mark renders at 10 px inside enc.tooth.3 (aria-label "Tooth 3, charted") and a third node appears, a '★' glyph at 11 px. money: three .chip .glyph nodes at 11 px and .btn.irreversible::before '▮' at 11 px; no 9 or 10 px text anywhere on the screen. overlays: '▮' at 11 px on pin.submit (author pad) and phone.stepup.submit, plus aria-hidden '▬' chip glyphs at 11 px beside the word "Patient" at 13 px.
TYPE-min-any-text-12.threshold: Zero text nodes < 12px. Prototype has .psite .ghost 10px (168 instances on perio), .psite.bleed::after 9px, .psite.sup::before 9px, .chip .glyph 11px, .count 12px; the 9 and 10px cases fail unless the value is duplicated in >= 12px text.
TYPE-min-any-text-12.scope_correction: Perio and Overlays stand as written. Encounter: the 10 px '●' appears only after the reader charts a tooth in-session (zero at load), and while the charge is pending the transaction card does repeat "Charted Composite, 2 surf posterior #3 O" at 15 px - it is once that card changes that the mark stands alone; the row also missed a third sub-12 px node ('★' 11 px). Money: of the two nodes named, only the '▮' stands - the 11 px .chip .glyph is excused by the registry's own duplication rule (its word sits beside it at 13 px) and by the threshold's own fail list, which names the 9 and 10 px cases.
TYPE-min-any-text-12.why: The 10 px prior-depth ghosts on Perio are 168 meaning-carrying values with no >= 12 px equivalent, squarely in the threshold's failing band, and the irreversible '▮' renders at 11 px on Money, Overlays, Encounter and Perio with no text of any size carrying the same meaning.
TYPE-min-any-text-12.fix_direction: Raise .psite .ghost to 12-13 px, the encounter charted mark to >= 16 px (or a border treatment), and .btn.irreversible::before to >= 12 px.

CLT-disclosure-depth.my_measurement: #/owner/close, fresh page, 1280 desk light. At load close.tied.tile has aria-expanded="false" and #dc-tile-detail carries [hidden]; there is no .match, .investigate or .clear control anywhere in the DOM, and the canvas text contains no "312.40". The only <details> on the screen are close.decision.d-1.why and close.approvals.why, both depth 1, both closed. One press on the tile auto-opens close.location.loc-3 (aria-expanded true, loc-1 and loc-2 false); the Match/Investigate/Clear controls then sit inside #dc-loc-loc-3 inside #dc-tile-detail - two nested disclosure containers - and pressing Investigate is a third nested toggle before the candidate ledger rows appear. The same stack also carries close.changed and close.late toggles plus a "Why these counts" <details>.
CLT-disclosure-depth.threshold: Max disclosure depth 2; 0 finish-critical elements hidden by default; at most 1 'More' toggle per card. The refusal 'Why' details (depth 1) passes.
CLT-disclosure-depth.scope_correction: The collapsed tile does name the finding - it reads "▲ 1 variance / Yesterday 9/2 - 3 locations - detection lag 1 day - bank feed" - so what is hidden by default is the $312.40 amount and the three controls that resolve it, not the fact that a variance exists.
CLT-disclosure-depth.why: The controls that clear the day's only finding are behind two nested toggles at load and their evidence behind a third, against a threshold of depth 2 and zero finish-critical elements hidden by default.
CLT-disclosure-depth.fix_direction: Open the tile (and the location in variance) by default whenever any location is out, so the amount and its three controls are on screen without a press.

CDS-BTN-text-bold-body.my_measurement: Fresh page per screen, body font-size 15 px on all of them. chairs at 1024: the 6 .ch-strip buttons compute font-weight 500 and every inner label span renders at 13 px (the other 18 canvas buttons are 600 / 15 px); no verb label wraps. close: all 9 .btn are 15 px / 600 and nothing wraps at 1024, but with the tile open exactly 4 buttons sit at weight 400 - close.tied.tile and close.location.loc-1/2/3. compliance: every .btn on risk and roles computes 15 px / 600; at 1024 roles.row.u-dr-3 ("Dr. Chidi Okafor · DDS, OMS") renders 69 px tall against the 44 px single-line height, i.e. two lines. overlays: palette result rows (palette.row.N) are weight 400 with a 1 px border while palette.close is 600 / 2 px; phone.simulate ("Simulate: the biller requests the $410.00 courtesy write-off") paints 2 line rects and 59 px of height at both 1024 and 1280. perio at 1024 operatory: pad word keys perio.pad.supp "Supp", perio.pad.bleed "Bleed" and the reversible perio.pad.next "Next tooth" are 13 px at weight 600 while the digit keys are 17 px.
CDS-BTN-text-bold-body.threshold: font-weight >= 600 and font-size >= body font-size on 100% of buttons; no button label wraps to a second line at 1024px.
CDS-BTN-text-bold-body.why: Every row reproduces: sub-600 weights on Chairs, Close and the palette, sub-body 13 px labels on Chairs and the perio pad, and two labels that wrap at 1024 (the People row and phone.simulate), against a threshold of 100% and zero wraps.
CDS-BTN-text-bold-body.fix_direction: Take the strip and the People name out of the button role (or let them inherit 15 px / 600), set the tile, .dc-loc and .palette-row label to 600, raise the pad word keys to 15 px, and shorten the simulate label.

CDS-STATUS-roles-max.my_measurement: Severity classes on visible chips, fresh page, 1280 light (identical at 1024 and in dark): board 6 of 6 at once (stop, required, review, style, info, clear), temp-board 6, close 4 collapsed (review, info, required, stop) and 5 once the tile is opened (clear joins), checkout 2 (review, clear), ledger 1 (clear). Soft/ink contrast computed from the live custom properties: light 6.88 (required) to 16.86 (review), dark 8.58 (stop) to 11.38 (clear) - all >= 4.5 in both themes. Relative luminance of the six soft fills, light: stop 0.9099, required 0.9390, review 0.9625, style 0.9073, info 0.9536, clear 0.9468 (ascending order is style < stop < required < clear < info < review); dark: stop 0.0145, required 0.0194, review 0.0257, style 0.0173, info 0.0215, clear 0.0220 (ascending is stop < style < required < info < clear < review). Neither theme is monotonic in the registered order.
CDS-STATUS-roles-max.threshold: <= 6 severity roles total (prototype has exactly 6: stop, required, review, style, info, clear); <= 4 distinct severities on one screen; soft/ink contrast >= 4.5:1 in both themes; luminance strictly monotonic stop < required < review < style < info < clear in grayscale.
CDS-STATUS-roles-max.scope_correction: Checkout shows 2 distinct severities at load, not the 3 the row reports; this does not change the row's verdict, since that clause was already recorded as passing there.
CDS-STATUS-roles-max.why: The ladder clause fails in both themes on every screen (the tokens are product-wide), and the Board renders all six roles at once while Daily Close reaches five with the tile open, against a ceiling of four on one screen; contrast is the one clause that passes everywhere.
CDS-STATUS-roles-max.fix_direction: Re-step the six soft fills so luminance rises strictly stop -> clear in both themes, and render the type words (Hygiene/Restorative/Surgery/Exam) as one neutral chip so the severity ladder is only used for state.

WCAG-2.4.3-focus-order.my_measurement: Full Tab cycle on a fresh page at 1280 light, positions taken in document space (rect.top + #canvas.scrollTop, because the canvas is the scroller). chairs: 33 unique stops against 33 visible focusables in exactly DOM order, 0 positive tabindex, 1 document.body landing and it is the end-of-document wrap, 0 stops without a 3 px ring; 3 visual inversions, each the .ch-list three-column row wrap - a-1050.rail (328) -> a-1042.expand (295), a-1042.rail (551) -> a-1073.expand (239), a-1070.rail (753) -> a-1071.expand (701) - so 30/33 = 91%. compliance risk: 21 stops, 0 inversions. roles closed: 23 stops, 0 inversions. roles with the day-pass form open: 40 stops (roles.daypass.end contributes 4 consecutive internal time-input segments), DOM order exact, and exactly 2 upward jumps, both the .rl-grid column wrap - roles.daypass.role.da (419) -> roles.daypass.location.loc-1 (263) and roles.daypass.location.loc-3 (367) -> roles.daypass.end (263) - about 93% of canvas stops. 0 activeElement === body after any action on either screen.
WCAG-2.4.3-focus-order.threshold: 100% of stops in DOM order; >= 98% in visual order with each exception listed; 100% of dialog open/close cycles land focus as specified; 0 cases of activeElement === document.body after any action.
WCAG-2.4.3-focus-order.why: Both rows reproduce to the element: DOM order and the body-landing clause pass, but the visual-order clause measures 91% on Chairs and ~93% on the open Roles form against a floor of 98%, and the inversions are exactly the grid row/column wraps named.
WCAG-2.4.3-focus-order.fix_direction: Keep .ch-list single-column at 1280 (or register the row wrap as a listed exception) and lay .rl-grid out in explicit rows so Tab and the eye travel the same way.

WCAG-2.4.7.my_measurement: Tab cycle with computed outline captured at each stop, fresh page, 1280 light. #/compliance/risk: 21 stops, every one outline "solid 3px" - 0 without a ring. #/compliance/roles closed: 23 stops, all 3 px. #/compliance/roles with the day-pass form open: 40 stops, exactly one without a ring - roles.daypass.end (input[type=time]) is entered four times as Tab walks its internal segments; on stops 1-3 it computes outline "solid 3px" offset 2 px with the white 2 px box-shadow and :focus-visible matching, and on the 4th (the native clock-picker segment) it computes outline "none 0px", outline-offset 0, box-shadow none and :focus-visible false. #canvas never takes a Tab stop.
WCAG-2.4.7.threshold: 100% of Tab stops show an outline >= 2px (prototype standard is 3px); 0 rules removing outline on Tab-reachable elements.
WCAG-2.4.7.why: One Tab stop on a reachable control paints no ring at all, so the measurement is on the wrong side of a 100% threshold; the rest of both Compliance screens is clean at 3 px.
WCAG-2.4.7.fix_direction: Give .rl-time a :focus-within outline so the 3 px ring survives the native picker segment, or replace the time input with the same seg control Role and Location use.

CUST-2.1.4-shortcuts-optin.my_measurement: Fresh page per screen, 1280x900 light desk, focus forced onto body (tabindex -1), no dialog open. Board: 'a' fires (0 -> 5 events, store JSON 75970 -> 76239 chars), 's' fires (5 -> 10 events, focus moved to board.card.a-1042.expand), 'c' navigates #/frontdesk/board -> #/frontdesk/checkout/a-1044. Chairs: 'p' navigates to #/hygienist/perio/enc-9001, 'n' and 'r' each log events. Close: 't' logs 2 events and moves focus to close.tied.tile. Money: 'p', 'w', 'a' each log 2 events and move focus (money.era.era-1.postmatched, money.writeoff.amount, money.denial.c-88.appeal). Perio: '3', Space and 's' each log 2 events against perio.grid.cell.t2-s2. On all five screens the product-wide search for an accelerator switch (any button/input/role=switch/label matching /accel|shortcut|keyboard key|single[- ]key|hotkey|keys on/) returns 0 controls; localStorage is empty and window.__proto exposes only ready/persona/theme/device/outage/privacy/motion/grayscale, so there is nowhere for a per-user preference to live. Ctrl+K opens the palette on all five.
CUST-2.1.4-shortcuts-optin.threshold: 0 single-key actions outside a focused component with accelerators off; 1 off switch; 100% of accelerators have a visible equivalent; state persists per user.
CUST-2.1.4-shortcuts-optin.why: Reproduced on every claimed screen: single-character keys act with focus on the body and no component focused, there is no off switch anywhere in the product, and no per-user store exists for the preference, so three of the four threshold clauses fail.
CUST-2.1.4-shortcuts-optin.fix_direction: Gate every document-level keydown handler behind one per-user 'single-key shortcuts' preference that defaults off and persists, and print the key on each duplicated control.

WCAG-1.4.3.my_measurement: Perio, fresh page, dark theme at 1280x900 and 1024x768. Drove the grid from the keyboard to create a shallow bleeding+suppuration site and a deep bleeding site, then read getComputedStyle(el,'::after')/('::before') colour against the cell's own painted background (alpha-composited up the ancestor chain), WCAG relative luminance. .psite.bleed::after content '●', 9px/600, rgb(185,28,28) on rgb(23,32,51) = 2.51:1; on the deep fill rgb(59,31,14) = 2.34:1. .psite.sup::before content '◆', 9px, rgb(124,58,237) on rgb(23,32,51) = 2.85:1. Identical at both widths. Light theme: 6.47:1, 6.09:1 and 5.70:1 - passes. Cause confirmed in source: tokens.css redefines --stop-soft/-ink/-fill/-on and --style-soft/-ink/-fill/-on for dark but leaves --stop-rail #B91C1C and --style-rail #7C3AED at their light values, and components.css:93 / :229 paint the glyphs from those two rails. Full sweep of the screen: 428 visible text nodes per theme, 0 below their AA limit in either theme, so these two generated-content glyphs are the only failures - and axe sees neither, because generated content is not a text node.
WCAG-1.4.3.threshold: >= 4.5:1 for text under 24px (or under 18.66px bold); >= 3:1 for text at or above 24px or >= 18.66px and bold. 0 failing text nodes per theme.
WCAG-1.4.3.why: The numbers reproduce exactly (2.51, 2.34 and 2.85 against a 4.5:1 limit at 9px), and the registered measurable_test explicitly puts composed ::before/::after text in scope; the glyphs also fall below the 3:1 non-text floor, so the breach stands on either reading.
WCAG-1.4.3.fix_direction: Give --stop-rail and --style-rail dark-theme values (or paint the glyphs in --stop-ink / --style-ink) and raise them above 9px.

CLT-topbar-7.my_measurement: Counted visible focusable controls inside the real .topbar element and their distinct rounded tops, on a fresh page at 1280x900, 1024x768, 420x800 and 320x800 in both themes, on all 14 routes. Controls (identical at every width and theme): Board 9, temp-Board 7, Chairs 8, Perio 8, Checkout 9, Risk 9, Roles 9, Encounter 9, Exams 9, Ledger 10, Money 10, Close 11, overlays/phone route 11, Signin 1. Rows: 1 at 1280 (2 on Ledger/Money/Close/phone, where Sign out wraps), 2 at 1024 everywhere, 1 at 420 and 320 - the bar switches to flex-wrap:nowrap with overflow-x:auto below 640, so it never wraps but scrolls (Ledger scrollWidth 1075 vs 420, 6 of 10 controls off-screen at rest; 7 of 10 at 320; Close 1271 vs 420, 7 of 11 off-screen; Board 952 vs 420, 5 of 9). topbarRows never reached 3 on any route, width or theme. The registered baseline figures are a selector artefact and I reproduced it exactly: measure.cjs:46 builds '#topbar ' + CONTROL, and the descendant combinator binds only to the first term, so the selector reads '#topbar button, a[href], input, select, textarea, summary, [role=button], [tabindex]' and counts every such element on the page. Re-running that selector verbatim gives Ledger 19 controls / 11 rows at 1280 and 1024, Close 14/5, Risk 14/6-7, Board 11/3-4, Encounter 12/4-5, Chairs and Perio 9/2-3 - the registered numbers to the digit. The strays are the body skip link (a[href] at top -60, one per route), the canvas 'Why' <summary> disclosures (4 on Risk, 2 on Close, 1 on Board/Ledger), the two note <textarea>s on the Encounter, and on the Ledger the 7 open patient-rail controls.
CLT-topbar-7.threshold: topbarControls <= 7 and topbarRows <= 2 at every width passes; 8-9 controls is a warning; >= 10 controls or >= 3 rows fails. Baseline: Ledger 19 controls / 11 rows desk and 10 rows phone; Close and Risk 14 controls / 5-7 rows; Board 11 controls / 3-4 rows all fail.
CLT-topbar-7.scope_correction: The fail band (>= 10 controls) is reached on 4 of the 9 claimed screens only: Ledger 10, Money 10, Close 11, overlays 11. Board 9, Chairs 8, Checkout 9, compliance Risk/Roles 9, Encounter 9 and Perio 8 sit in the 8-9 warning band, not the fail band. The row clause is breached nowhere - no route exceeds 2 rows at any width or theme - so the registered baseline's row figures (Ledger 11, Close 5-7, Board 3-4) and its Ledger 19 / Close 14 / Risk 14 control counts should all be re-registered; the auditors' 'the rail is inside #topbar' explanation is wrong (the rail is a sibling <aside id=rail>), the real cause is the unparenthesised descendant combinator.
CLT-topbar-7.why: Every screen exceeds the seven-control ceiling of the statement, and four of them are in the outright fail band, but the registered control counts and every row figure are artefacts of a selector that counts the whole page.
CLT-topbar-7.fix_direction: Fold Privacy mode, theme and Sign out behind the author chip so the shell bar keeps <= 7 controls and stops scrolling sideways at 420, and fix measure.cjs:46 to scope the selector per term.

CLT-chunk-4.my_measurement: Counted visible controls inside every .card/.appt/.qrow/.dc-row/.btnrow/.actions/.seg/[role=group] on a fresh page, 1280x900 and 1024x768, both themes. Board: section.card.flat.stack.queue 'Checkout queue' = 8 (four Ping chair + four Checkout), readiness card 5, appointment cards 4 - same at 800px height and on temp-board. Checkout: 'Payment' card 10 at rest (3 decision segments, 3 tenders, Amount, Add write-off, Post, Why), 15 with the write-off open; Ledger max 3 ('Statement') - inside the rule. Risk: 'Due now' card 8. Roles: 'People and entitlements' card 11 at rest, 'Add day pass' card 14 once roles.daypass.add is pressed. Encounter: 'Chart' card 40, and the two arches carry role='group' (aria-label 'Upper arch...'/'Lower arch...'), not role='grid', so the registered exemption does not apply; Exams max 1. Perio: nothing over 5 at load (head .btnrow 5), but pressing perio.tag.add renders a .card 'Tag for the dentist' with 10 controls, and perio.pad.toggle opens .pad[role=group] 'Glove pad' with 15. Signin: .btnrow 'Device and display' 11, .personas[role=radiogroup] 9.
CLT-chunk-4.threshold: controlsPerCardMax <= 4 passes (Cowan 4±1); 5-7 is a warning (Miller 7±2); > 7 fails. Baseline: Board 8, Roles 11, Checkout 10, Risk 8 fail; Encounter 40 is exempt only if the odontogram is marked role=grid.
CLT-chunk-4.why: Every claimed screen has at least one bounded group above the seven-control ceiling (8, 10, 8/11, 40, 10, 11), reproduced at both widths and themes; on Perio the breaching card needs one click on a visible control, which is an ordinary flow rather than an unreachable state.
CLT-chunk-4.fix_direction: Split the oversized groups (Payment, day-pass form, perio tag card, signin device row) into labelled sub-groups of <= 4, and mark the odontogram role='grid' so the compound-widget exemption applies.

CLT-chip-not-button.my_measurement: Fresh page per screen, 1280x900 and 1024x768, both themes. Chairs: 20 visible .chip, none is a BUTTON and none takes a tab stop, but 4 of them (Med hx changed, Perio, BWX due, What helped last time) sit inside <button class='btn quiet ch-strip'> on card a-1042 and compute cursor:pointer - interactive under the registered test's 'or an ancestor <button>' clause. Checkout/Ledger: all 6 chips are role=status, tabIndex -1, cursor auto - 0 interactive chips, so that clause passes; the converse clause fails on the Ledger, where [data-testid='rail.alert'] is a <div role='button' class='alertbar rail-clear'> with tabIndex 0, cursor pointer, height 44 and a 1px border where every .btn is 2px, carrying none of .btn/.tile/.tab/summary/native-input. Close: at rest 0 interactive chips and 0 focusables without an identity class; after clicking close.tied.tile the expanded card adds 5 focusable <button>s with no registered identity - close.location.loc-1/2/3 (.dc-loc, 1px border) and close.changed / close.late (.dc-line, 1px) - and the 3 chips nested in the location rows inherit cursor:pointer from their button parent.
CLT-chip-not-button.threshold: 0 interactive .chip elements and 0 focusable elements without a button identity class. Any interactive chip must be re-classed as .btn.compact.
CLT-chip-not-button.scope_correction: Close is 5 offenders, not 6: close.tied.tile carries .tile, which the registered threshold names as an accepted button identity, so it is not a violation. The converse clause also fires on screens not claimed: Board and temp-Board carry 3 focusable <button class='chair'> (1px border) at every width, and the Encounter's 32 <button class='tooth'> and Perio's 192 <button class='psite'> likewise carry no registered identity class (though both are compound-widget cells with a 2px border, so they are weaker cases than rail.alert or the .dc-loc rows).
CLT-chip-not-button.why: Both halves of the rule are breached on the claimed screens - 4 chips made clickable by a button ancestor on Chairs, and focusable controls with no button identity on the Ledger rail and in the expanded Close tile - though one of the six Close elements is a false positive under the registered identity list.
CLT-chip-not-button.fix_direction: Move the Chairs delta chips outside the button, give rail.alert / .dc-loc / .dc-line the shared .btn identity (or drop role=button and the tab stop), and set cursor:inherit off nested chips.

CLT-tesler-defaults.my_measurement: Checkout #/frontdesk/checkout/a-1044, fresh page at 1280x900, first paint. The Tender group (div.btnrow[role=group][aria-label='Tender']) renders checkout.tender.card / .cash / .check all aria-pressed='false'. Opening checkout.writeoff.add renders checkout.writeoff.reason.courtesy / .hardship / .prior_period / .contractual_ppo all aria-pressed='false'. Source confirms the store then assumes one anyway: checkout.js:30 initialises tender:null, writeoffReason:null, and checkout.js:117 posts writeoffReason: st.writeoffReason || 'courtesy', so an unpressed screen records 'courtesy'. The rest of the finish path is correctly defaulted: checkout.collect.seg.collect aria-pressed='true' with send-statement and payment-plan false, and the only visible input, checkout.amount, arrives pre-filled at '44.00'.
CLT-tesler-defaults.threshold: 0 empty required choices on load per finish path; 0 fields requiring re-entry of data already shown on the same screen. A choice that is deliberately neutral for a prudent decision (see CLT-neutral-irreversible) is exempt when documented.
CLT-tesler-defaults.why: Two required choices on the checkout finish path render with no option selected, and the write-off reason is worse than neutral - the store silently substitutes 'courtesy', so the record and the screen disagree, which is not a documented prudent-neutral exemption.
CLT-tesler-defaults.fix_direction: Preselect the commonest tender and mark one reason code pressed, or make Post refuse rather than default writeoffReason to 'courtesy'.

CDS-SPACE-scale-4-8.my_measurement: Computed styles read on live nodes, fresh page, 1280x900 and 1024x768, both themes. Shared components: .btn gap / row-gap / column-gap = 6px on every screen (Board, Checkout, Ledger, Close, Money, Signin, Perio); .chip padding 0px 10px 0px 10px and gap 6px wherever a chip renders (Board, Checkout, Ledger, Close, Money); .personas .btn gap 2px on Signin; a.skip padding 10px 14px everywhere. On-scale by contrast: .btn padding 0 16px, .card padding 12px, .card gap 12px, .field gap 4px, td padding 8px 12px. Static scan of prototype/css/*.css with comments stripped: 29 literal px values in padding/margin/gap declarations (the rest come from --space-* tokens), of which 17 are off the {0,4,8,12,16,20,24,32,40,48} scale - 41.4% on scale - concentrated in components.css gap:6px (x4), gap:2px (x4), padding 10px (x3) and 6px (x2), plus base.css .skip padding 10px 14px.
CDS-SPACE-scale-4-8.threshold: >= 95% of declared spacing values on the scale and 0 off-scale values on shared components (.btn, .chip, .card, .field, td).
CDS-SPACE-scale-4-8.why: Both halves of the threshold fail: .btn and .chip - two of the five named shared components - carry 6px gaps and 10px chip padding on every claimed screen, and the literal declared px values are 41% on scale against a 95% floor.
CDS-SPACE-scale-4-8.fix_direction: Take .btn and .chip gaps to 8px (or 4px), .chip padding-x to 8px, .personas .btn gap to 4px and .skip padding to 8px 16px.

CLT-one-task.my_measurement: Fresh page, 1280x900 and 1280x800 (and 1024x768 / 420x800 as a cross-check), headings read from live bounding boxes. Board: 1 h1, 0 finish buttons, and the headings above the fold are H1 'Board · Main Street · Thursday 9/3' (top 77) plus H2 Chair 1 / Chair 2 / Chair 3 (235) and H2 'Before open' (241); 'Checkout queue' sits at 961 and 'Filed later' at 2140, both below the 900px measuring fold. That is 4 h2/h3 above the fold - exactly the registered limit - at both 900 and 800 viewport heights. Close: 1 h1, headings above the fold H1 (237) + H2 'Decisions due for review: 1' (331), 'Approvals only I can give' (645), 'Expiring exceptions and open SoD findings' (796) = 3 h2 (Close day is at 1135), and 3 top-level regions - the heading and region clauses pass; the finish-button clause fails, with 2 irreversible primaries at rest (close.decision.d-1.retire 'Retire' and close.closeday 'Close day') and 3 once close.tied.tile is expanded (close.variance.v-1.match 'Match these'). Encounter: 1 h1, 1 finish button (enc.file), 5 top-level regions, and 5 h2/h3 above the 900px fold at 1280 (Hygienist tags, Chart, Procedure, When, Note) against a limit of 4; at 1024x768 only 4 h2/h3 are above the fold and at 420 only 3. Exams passes every clause.
CLT-one-task.threshold: Exactly 1 h1; exactly 1 finish button on finish-path screens; <= 4 headings above the fold; <= 5 top-level regions above the fold. Baseline: Board 7 headings, Encounter 6, Close 5 fail the heading rule.
CLT-one-task.scope_correction: Board is refuted: it has 1 h1, 0 finish buttons, 4 section headings above the fold (at the limit, not over) and 0 top-level regions - the auditor's 5 and the registered baseline's 7 both count the h1 and/or headings below the fold, and the statement counts the h1 separately from the four section headings. Close is confirmed only through the finish-button clause (2 committing primaries at rest, 3 expanded - not the 4 claimed); its heading count passes. Encounter is confirmed, but at 1280 only - at 1024 and 420 the above-fold heading count is within the limit, so the breach is desk-width, not desk and operatory.
CLT-one-task.why: The rule is genuinely breached on two of three claimed screens - Close carries several committing primaries where the threshold allows one, and the Encounter shows five section headings above the 1280px fold - but the Board row measures the h1 as a section heading and falls.
CLT-one-task.fix_direction: Move the decision/approval/SoD sections off Close so one finish button remains, and demote the Encounter's 'Procedure' and 'When' h3s to visible group labels inside the Chart card.

AXE-4.1.2-name-role-value.my_measurement: axe-core 4.13.0 injected into a fresh page at 1280x900, run over the 19 registered rules (button-name, aria-command-name, aria-input-field-name, aria-toggle-field-name, aria-tab-name, label, select-name, link-name, summary-name, aria-prohibited-attr, aria-allowed-attr, aria-valid-attr, aria-valid-attr-value, aria-required-attr, aria-conditional-attr, aria-roles, nested-interactive, aria-hidden-focus, duplicate-id-aria). Encounter at load: 0 violations, 0 incomplete; 37 [aria-pressed] nodes, values 'false' x36 and 'true' x1. Exams: 0 violations, 0 incomplete, 1 aria-pressed node, 'false'. After clicking enc.tag.tag-1.chart ('Chart it'): still 0 violations and 0 incomplete, but the surface strip for tooth 30 reads M:false, O:mixed, D:true... in fact enc.surface.30.o and enc.surface.30.d both carry aria-pressed='mixed' (2 nodes, names 'Occlusal, suggested by the tag, tap to confirm' and 'Distal, suggested by the tag, tap to confirm'), alongside enc.tooth.30 and enc.temporality.today at 'true'.
AXE-4.1.2-name-role-value.threshold: 0 violations and 0 incomplete nodes for the listed rules in every context; 0 aria-pressed values other than 'true'/'false'.
AXE-4.1.2-name-role-value.scope_correction: Two nodes carry aria-pressed='mixed' after charting a tag (enc.surface.30.o and enc.surface.30.d), not the one the row implies; scope is otherwise as claimed (Encounter only, Exams clean).
AXE-4.1.2-name-role-value.why: The axe half of the threshold passes cleanly, but the explicit Playwright assertion it carries - 0 aria-pressed values other than 'true'/'false' - is breached by the tri-state surface toggles once a hygienist tag is charted, a state reached from one visible control.
AXE-4.1.2-name-role-value.fix_direction: Keep aria-pressed to true/false and carry 'suggested by the tag' in the accessible name and the dashed outline, or re-register the heuristic to allow 'mixed' on a tri-state toggle button.

WCAG-1.4.11.my_measurement: Recomputed from getComputedStyle on live inputs at 1280x900, both themes. LIGHT: every .input draws border 2px solid rgb(184,178,163) (--line-strong #B8B2A3); its own fill is rgb(255,255,255) (--surface) and the card behind it is also rgb(255,255,255), so the border is 2.11:1 against the colour on both sides of it; on Daily Close the field sits on the cream page, giving 2.11:1 inside / 1.87:1 outside. DARK: border 2px rgb(70,86,122) (--line-strong #46567A) on fill rgb(23,32,51) (--surface #172033) = 2.23:1, and 2.44:1 against the page rgb(15,23,42). Measured on checkout.amount, checkout.card.number (empty), checkout.writeoff.amount, checkout.pin, ledger.pin, close.pin and money.writeoff.amount - identical 2.11 / 2.23 on all seven. The empty boxes have no other boundary: fill and card are the same colour. PERIO dark: the bleeding state cue .psite.bleed border 2px rgb(185,28,28) (--stop-rail, not re-tokened for dark) reads 2.51:1 against the cell fill rgb(23,32,51), 2.76:1 against the page rgb(15,23,42) and 2.34:1 on a deep cell rgb(59,31,14); its 9px dot glyph carries the same 2.51/2.34 ratio. Perio light passes (6.47 / 5.73 / 6.09). Cues that do pass, re-measured: .psite.active 4.54 light / 6.61 dark vs fill, filled vs outline button heights identical.
WCAG-1.4.11.threshold: >= 3:1 for every cue that is the only means of identifying the control or its state, in both themes; 0 failing cues. Input borders must pass because an empty text box has no other boundary.
WCAG-1.4.11.scope_correction: Wider than claimed, same root cause. --line-strong is the input border token product-wide, so every text box outside the four claimed screens fails identically at 2.11 light / 2.23 dark: perio.tag.text, roles.daypass.name, palette.input and palette.confirm.dob all measured. The perio row is a second, separate token (--stop-rail is not redefined in the dark block), so it is not fixed by the --line-strong change.
WCAG-1.4.11.why: Reproduced independently in both themes from painted colours on live nodes: 2.11:1 light and 2.23:1 dark, against a fill that is the same colour as the card behind it, so the 2px border really is the only boundary of an empty field - both sides of the 3:1 floor are on the failing side. The perio dark bleeding rail is a second failing state-only cue at 2.34-2.76:1.
WCAG-1.4.11.fix_direction: Darken --line-strong in light (about #8A8272 reaches 3:1 on white) and lighten it in dark (about #6E80AA on #172033), and add a dark override for --stop-rail so the perio bleeding border clears 3:1 on both the plain and the deep cell fill.

WCAG-1.4.3-placeholder-hover-focus.my_measurement: Read getComputedStyle(el,'::placeholder') on live fields. No ::placeholder rule exists in the prototype CSS, so every field takes Chromium's UA default rgb(117,117,117) in both themes. On the light field fill rgb(255,255,255) that is 4.61:1 (pass); on the dark field fill rgb(23,32,51) it is 3.53:1 (fail), unchanged when the field is focused (3.53:1). Hover and focus text are clean: checkout.post 11.50:1 light / 14.28:1 dark, checkout.back 8.03:1 / 12.30:1, checkout.explain 11.21:1 dark, each identical at rest, on hover and on focus - zero regressions.
WCAG-1.4.3-placeholder-hover-focus.threshold: >= 4.5:1 in all three states, both themes; zero regressions between resting and hover/focus state.
WCAG-1.4.3-placeholder-hover-focus.scope_correction: Broader than the one field claimed. The same 3.53:1 dark placeholder appears on palette.input, palette.confirm.dob, roles.daypass.name and perio.tag.text - so overlays, compliance/roles and perio carry the same failure, not just checkout.
WCAG-1.4.3-placeholder-hover-focus.why: The dark-theme placeholder reproduces at 3.53:1, below the 4.5:1 floor, in every state; the hover and focus halves of the claim are correct that nothing regresses, so the breach is the placeholder colour alone - and it is a missing rule, not a checkout-specific one.
WCAG-1.4.3-placeholder-hover-focus.fix_direction: Add a ::placeholder rule bound to a theme-aware token (light --ink-3 #56617A, dark around #97A3B8) instead of leaving the field to the UA default grey.

CDS-TYPE-body-16.my_measurement: getComputedStyle(document.body).fontSize is 15px on every screen state I opened - chairs, checkout, ledger, close, risk, roles, encounter, exams, money, signin, board, temp board, perio, phone, palette and author pad - in both themes at 1280x900 and at 400x820 on the phone. base.css:4 sets body font-size to var(--fs-2) and tokens.css:49 sets --fs-2: 15px, with no device-profile override anywhere in the CSS, so the operatory profile is 15px too. Every running-text node I collected (p, li, dd, .sentence, .explain) is at or below 15px: e.g. encounter 8 of 8, close 6 of 6, risk 7 of 7, checkout/ledger 4 of 4 each, and the 13px .small/.hint step below that (48 nodes on chairs, 129 on the board, 35 on roles).
CDS-TYPE-body-16.threshold: Body computed font-size >= 16px; 0 running-text paragraphs (p, li, dd, .sentence, .explain) below 16px. 15px fails.
CDS-TYPE-body-16.scope_correction: Wider than the eight screens claimed: the same 15px body and sub-16px prose is on board, temp board, perio, exams, risk and roles as well - it is one token, so it is every screen in the product.
CDS-TYPE-body-16.why: The threshold names 15px as a fail and the computed body value is 15px on every state measured, with no running-text paragraph reaching 16px anywhere.
CDS-TYPE-body-16.fix_direction: Raise --fs-2 to 16px (1rem) and --fs-1 to 14px in tokens.css and re-flow the cards that assume the narrower step.

CLT-common-region.my_measurement: Walked every element holding >= 3 visible controls as direct children and read role, aria-label, aria-labelledby and whether any label target is visible. CHAIRS: 6 x .ch-actions, n=3, role null, aria-label null, aria-labelledby null - 6 unlabelled groups. LEDGER: page-head .btnrow n=4, role null, no label at all. CHECKOUT: .seg n=3 role=group aria-label 'Collection decision' and .btnrow n=3 role=group aria-label 'Tender' - named for assistive technology only, no visible name inside the region; the write-off .btnrow n=4 carries aria-label 'Reason code' the same way. SIGNIN: 'Device and display' .btnrow n=11, role null, no aria-labelledby to the adjacent h2; .personas n=9 is role=radiogroup with aria-label duplicating the visible h2. OVERLAYS: the author pad .pinpad n=12 has role null, aria-label null, aria-labelledby null, sitting under an unassociated visible h2 'Who is charting?'. PERIO: glove .pad n=15 aria-label 'Glove pad' only, observation .row n=6 aria-label 'Observation vocabulary' only, omission .seg n=4 aria-label 'Reason not probed' only, page-head .btnrow n=3 with no label; the path .seg n=3 is aria-labelledby='pe-pathlab', which is visible - that one passes.
CLT-common-region.threshold: 0 unlabelled groups of >= 3 controls per screen. A group whose only label is a distant page-head .sub fails.
CLT-common-region.scope_correction: Two corrections. The perio page-head row holds 3 controls as direct children, not the 5 the auditor counted, and the broken groups on perio are 4, not 5 (the path .seg passes). Additionally, the persistent chrome carries the same defect on every screen: #topbar n=6 (aria-label 'Top bar') and the primary <nav> n=3-5 (aria-label 'Primary') have no visible group name either, which the auditors did not count on any screen.
CLT-common-region.why: Every claimed group reproduces with role/aria-label/aria-labelledby read off the live nodes: chairs has 6 groups with no name at all, ledger and signin one each, the author pad one, and perio four whose only name is an aria-label with nothing visible in the region.
CLT-common-region.fix_direction: Print the group names as visible sub-headings inside each bounded region and point role=group aria-labelledby at that heading, as the perio path .seg already does with #pe-pathlab.

CLT-hick-7.my_measurement: Counted visible options per selection container and checked each container for a search/filter input. LEDGER: .railtabs is one group of 9 (Chart, Notes, Perio, Imaging, Plan, Ledger, Claims, Docs, Profile), role=navigation aria-label 'Patient sections', no input of any kind inside it - the 8-15 band with no search. ENCOUNTER: two .odont groups of 16 each ('Upper arch, teeth 1 to 16' and 'Lower arch, teeth 32 to 17'), no search and no More in either container - both over 15. The encounter's other groups pass: procedures 5, temporality 3, starters 3. SIGNIN: .personas 9 options, no filter in the container; 'Device and display' .btnrow 11 options in one container, no filter. Checkout's own groups all pass (collection decision 3, tender 3, reason code 4).
CLT-hick-7.threshold: <= 7 visible options per group passes; 8-15 requires a search/filter input in the same container; > 15 fails outright. Baseline: sign-in shows 8 persona tiles (fails by one); Board topbar nav 11 (fails).
CLT-hick-7.scope_correction: The registered baseline is one tile stale: sign-in renders 9 persona tiles, not 8. The ledger page-head nav holds 3 primary links, not the 4 the auditor recorded (Board, Money Desk, Roles).
CLT-hick-7.why: Three groups land in the 8-15 band with no search input in the same container (rail tabs 9, personas 9, device row 11) and two land over 15 (both arches at 16), which the threshold fails outright regardless of how spatial the arch is.
CLT-hick-7.fix_direction: Add a filter field inside .railtabs and split the 11-button device row into named sub-groups of <= 7; for the arch, either pre-scope it to the tagged quadrant or accept it as a grid and record the exception against the heuristic.

CUST-settings-surface-small.my_measurement: Opened #/signin fresh and enumerated every visible toggle. 20 aria-pressed controls: 9 persona tiles, signin.theme.light/dark, signin.device.desk/operatory/shared/phone, signin.motion, signin.grayscale, signin.privacy, signin.outage, signin.afterhours - 11 of them in a single 'Device and display' .btnrow. Counting preferences rather than controls: theme, device profile, motion, grayscale, privacy, simulate outage, after hours = 7, of which 4 are the simulation/QA toggles the statement names by name (device profile, grayscale, outage, after hours) and all 4 are visible to every persona including Temp - the sign-in has no persona gate at all. Zero buttons whose label matches /reset|default/, and no 'System' option on theme or motion. Nesting depth 1, 0 <details> disclosures.
CUST-settings-surface-small.threshold: <= 7 user-facing preferences; <= 4 options each; 0 QA/simulation toggles visible to production personas; 1 reset control; depth <= 1.
CUST-settings-surface-small.why: Two clauses fail outright on a clean page: 4 QA/simulation toggles are visible to every production persona (the threshold allows 0) and there is no reset control (the threshold requires 1); the preference count sits exactly at the 7 ceiling only because the 4 device-profile buttons count as one preference.
CUST-settings-surface-small.fix_direction: Keep theme, motion and privacy on the sign-in with a System default marked, move device profile, grayscale, outage and after-hours behind a ?qa=1 flag or a 'Test harness' disclosure, and add one Reset to defaults control.

CDS-BTN-border-2px.my_measurement: Read computed border-top-width on every visible button, [role=button], .btn, input, select and textarea. BOARD: 96 of 99 at 2px, 3 at 1px - board.chair.1/2/3, which are <button class="chair"> (components.css:82 sets 1px solid var(--line)). LEDGER: 26 of 27 at 2px, the exception rail.alert, a <div role="button" class="alertbar rail-clear"> at 1px. CLOSE with the tile and rows open: 19 of 25 at 2px, 6 at 1px - close.tied.tile, close.location.loc-1/2/3 (.dc-loc) and close.changed/close.late (.dc-line). OVERLAYS with the palette open on 'mar': the 6 .palette-row result buttons are 1px while palette.input and the palette's own .btn controls are 2px. The height clause holds everywhere I could pair them: ledger statement send (irreversible) 44px vs preview (reversible) 44px, close decision row [44,44,44] with keep/tighten outline beside retire filled - difference 0px.
CDS-BTN-border-2px.threshold: border-width == 2px on 100% of buttons and inputs; height difference between adjacent filled and outline buttons == 0px.
CDS-BTN-border-2px.why: The second clause passes but the first does not: four distinct pressable components (.chair, .alertbar, .tile/.dc-loc/.dc-line, .palette-row) render a 1px border where every other control renders 2px, so the shared footprint is not one value.
CDS-BTN-border-2px.fix_direction: Give .chair, .alertbar, .tile, .dc-loc, .dc-line and .palette-row the same 2px border as .btn (or drop their border entirely and mark them another way) so 100% of pressables share one border width.

CLT-reading-grade.my_measurement: Re-extracted visible prose per element (so element boundaries end a sentence rather than being concatenated into pseudo-sentences) and scored Flesch-Kincaid with a syllable counter. DAILY CLOSE, collapsed: 16 sentences / 149 words / mean 9.3 / grade 7.0, 0 sentences over 25 and 0 over 20 - a pass. Fully expanded (tile, all Why disclosures, all details open): 25 sentences / 245 words / grade 5.8 with one 27-word sentence ('A late first posting has nothing to correct and posts today marked after close; worker rows from an overnight 835 or import are excluded from both counts.'). COMPLIANCE: risk 13 sentences / 145 words / grade 6.7, 0 over 25 - passes; roles with the day-pass form open 9 sentences / 82 words / grade 6.0 but one 31-word sentence ('A temp who also refunds, writes off, or prepares the deposit while posting payments creates a segregation-of-duties conflict; the preview shows the fraud path and the compensating control before you save.') - fails the second clause. OVERLAYS: the palette's 'How search works' panel is 5 sentences / 115 words / mean 23.0 / grade 8.3 with two sentences of 27 and 32 words - fails both clauses, and reproduces the auditor's number exactly. Phone approvals after Simulate: 10 sentences / 109 words / mean 10.9 / grade 6.5, 0 sentences over 25 - a pass; the '35-word store sentence' is not one sentence, it is the 13-word .ph-sentence 'Write-off $410.00 on LF - MRN-306 (courtesy) requested by Sam Dawson at 8:40 am' plus adjacent .ph-k/.ph-v key-value fragments that the auditor's extractor joined. Author pad grade 3.3, 0 long sentences - passes, as claimed.
CLT-reading-grade.threshold: Flesch-Kincaid grade <= 8.0 per screen and 0 sentences over 25 words pass; grade 8-10 warning; > 10 fails.
CLT-reading-grade.scope_correction: Two of the three claimed screens do not reproduce as stated. Daily Close is REFUTED as claimed: I measure grade 7.0 collapsed, not 8.1, and 0 sentences over 25 - the only real miss there is one 27-word sentence that appears only when every Why disclosure is expanded, which the auditor explicitly recorded as absent. Phone/approvals is REFUTED: grade 6.5 with 0 over-25 sentences; the claimed 9.3 / 160 words / 2 over-25 is an extraction artifact of concatenating card key-value fragments. What stands is compliance/roles (one 31-word sentence) and the overlays palette panel (grade 8.3 with 27- and 32-word sentences).
CLT-reading-grade.why: Only two of the four claimed prose surfaces breach the threshold when the prose is scored per element instead of as one concatenated string; the palette panel reproduces exactly and the roles extras answer is a genuine over-25 sentence, but Daily Close and the phone approvals cards both score well under 8.0 with no long sentence.
CLT-reading-grade.fix_direction: Split the roles extras answer at the semicolon into two sentences and break the palette panel's 27- and 32-word sentences in two; leave Daily Close and the phone cards alone.

CLT-scent-heading.my_measurement: Read the live h1 on every screen. Board (frontdesk) and Temp Board both render 'Board - Main Street - Thursday 9/3', which is 7 whitespace-separated tokens - the exact string and the exact count the registered threshold names as failing - and 5 tokens if the two middot separators are discarded; either way it is the only h1 in the product over 5 and the only one that is not unique. Every other h1 measured is within the bar and unique: 'Chairs - mine' (3), 'Money Desk' (2), 'Ledger' (1), 'Approvals' (1), 'Daily Close and Controls' (4), 'Practice risk' (2), 'Roles - Main Street' (4), 'Exams to sign' (3), 'Riverbend Dental' (2), 'Checkout - Samir Haddad' (4), 'Encounter - Ines Okoro' (4), 'Perio - Devon Price' (4). Nav labels reappear in their destination h1 - the topbar 'Board' link lands on an h1 starting 'Board', 'Money Desk' on 'Money Desk', 'Roles' on 'Roles - Main Street' - so the first clause passes.
CLT-scent-heading.threshold: 100% nav labels share a word with their destination h1; h1Words <= 5; h1 unique across screens. Baseline: Board and Temp Board h1 'Board - Main Street - Thursday 9/3' is 7 words and duplicated, failing; 'Money Desk', 'Chairs - mine' pass.
CLT-scent-heading.why: The board h1 is the exact string the registered threshold already names as 7 words and failing, and I measured it unchanged on both the frontdesk and temp routes at every width; the nav-label clause passes, so the breach is the h1 length alone.
CLT-scent-heading.fix_direction: Cut the h1 to 'Board' or 'Board - Main Street' and move the weekday and date into the .sub line below it.

AXE-1.3.1-tables-resolved.my_measurement: 1280x900 light, fresh page per leg, axe-core 4.13.0 injected. Checkout (#/frontdesk/checkout/a-1044) table.data.co-lines: 9 th, 1 with scope; the 6 thead th (Procedure, Tooth, Fee, Patient portion, Pre-flight, Self-pay) carry scope=null; tfoot holds th scope=row 'Totals' plus two scope-less th ('$44.00 est.', 'Estimate is separate from the balance above…') beside 2 td; caption false, aria-label null (only the .wrap-x wrapper is named 'Completed procedures'); all 6 header columns have >=1 non-empty td (3 each); axe: 0 violations, 1 incomplete th-has-data-cells. Ledger (#/biller/ledger/p-319) table.ledger-table: 6/6 th scope=col, 0 violations, 0 incomplete, but caption false and aria-label null -> unnamed. Roles (#/compliance/roles) table.data.rl-table: 4 thead th, 0 with scope, caption false, aria-label null, 4/4 header columns with data across 11 body rows, axe 0 violations / 0 incomplete on all five named rules. Close (#/owner/close): 0 <table>; with the tile open #dc-loc-loc-3 role=table aria-label 'Hillsboro tenders' has 4 rows and 0 rows containing any cell role (first row children SPAN,SPAN,SPAN,SPAN) -> aria-required-children critical, 5 nodes; after pressing Close day the read-back renders 5 role=row divs whose parent is a role=group card -> aria-required-children 5 nodes AND aria-required-parent 5 nodes.
AXE-1.3.1-tables-resolved.threshold: 0 violations; 0 incomplete for th-has-data-cells after the scripted check; 100% of th carry scope; 100% of header columns have >= 1 non-empty td; 100% of tables have a name.
AXE-1.3.1-tables-resolved.scope_correction: All three claimed screens fail, and the Ledger fails too on the same 'every table has a name' clause (th scope is clean there, the table name is not) - the auditor folded that into the checkout-ledger row, so no screen is added. Two corrections to the reasoning: on Close the five registered table rules return 0 violations and 0 incomplete (there is no <table> to run them on); the breach there is proven only by aria-required-children/aria-required-parent, which sit outside the registered rule list. On Roles the enclosing section does carry aria-label 'People and entitlements' (the auditor says nothing names it); the <table> element itself still has no accessible name, which is the clause that fails.
AXE-1.3.1-tables-resolved.why: Reproduced from a clean page on every claimed surface: 6 of 9 checkout th and 4 of 4 roles th carry no scope, no <table> on any screen carries a caption or aria-label, and the Close read-backs declare role=table/role=row with zero cell roles (10 critical axe nodes across the two states).
AXE-1.3.1-tables-resolved.fix_direction: Add scope="col" to the co-lines and rl-table thead th, turn the two tfoot number/note th into td, give every <table> its own <caption> or aria-label, and rebuild the two Close tender read-backs as real <table><th scope=col> (or add columnheader/cell roles plus a rowgroup parent).

WCAG-1.4.4.my_measurement: Ledger at 640x400 deviceScaleFactor 2 (=200%), light, fresh page: 36 visible controls (same 36 as at 1280x800, 0 lost), 0 clipped text elements, documentElement.scrollWidth 640 = clientWidth 640. Raw bounding-box intersections between controls: 6 pairs (rail.tab.claims x ledger.explain / ledger.showpatient, rail.tab.docs x ledger.showpatient / ledger.sendbiller, rail.tab.profile x ledger.sendbiller, rail.sum.appts x ledger.asof) - not the 10 claimed. For every one of those 6 pairs the rail control's painted height is 0px: #rail computes max-height 40vh (159px client box holding 876px of content) with overflow-y auto, so the rail clips at y=217 and #canvas begins at y=217 - zero painted overlap, and document.elementFromPoint returns the canvas button at each intersection centre. A screenshot at that size confirms it: Explain / Show patient / Open Money Desk / As of today are painted clear, with the rail's own row cut off above them. All 18 rail controls are reachable by scrolling the rail (reachableByScroll 18/18). Checkout at the same zoom: 0 raw pairs, 0 clipped, docScrollW 640. Board and Money Desk at 200%: 0 pairs. At 640x800 the rail box grows to 319px and the raw-pair count falls to 4, again 0 painted.
WCAG-1.4.4.threshold: At 200%: 0 clipped text elements, 0 overlapping controls, 0 controls lost; body horizontal scroll width <= viewport width.
WCAG-1.4.4.scope_correction: No screen fails. The one claimed screen (checkout-ledger) passes every clause of the threshold at 200%.
WCAG-1.4.4.why: The 'overlaps' are getBoundingClientRect intersections with controls that are scrolled out of an overflow:auto region and painted nowhere - rail.js:147 already gives #rail max-height 40vh below 1024px for exactly this reason, so nothing covers the page head and no control is lost.

CLT-label-words.my_measurement: 1280x900 light, fresh page per leg, words counted on button/[role=button]/summary text with · — ✓ ▲ ▾ ■ ◆ ● stripped. Board: labelWordsMax 3, accessibleNameWordsMax 13 ('Open checkout for Devon Price (already paid; charges post when the note files)') -> name rule fails. Chairs: chairs.card.a-1042.expand 26 words stripped / 22 raw, both as label and as accessible name. Ledger: ledger.asof 'As of today · by posted date' 6/7 words; ledger.showpatient accessible name 14 words. Checkout: 4 words at rest (passes), but typing 500.00 into checkout.amount reveals three 'Paid in full — don't send to insurance' toggles at 7 words. Close: close.tied.tile 11 stripped / 14 raw; with the tile open close.location.loc-2 is 12 words. Roles: exactly one button over four words (roles.row.u-dr-3 'Dr. Chidi Okafor · DDS, OMS', 5 stripped / 6 raw); accessibleNameWordsMax 9. Risk: labelWordsMax 3, accMax 9 - passes. Money: at load the maximum is 5 (summary 'Why are 37 already matched?'); after Post matched the three read-back buttons read 'Confirm · post $540.00, write-off $50.00' = 5 words; the Credits tab action is named 'Open the chart whose filed note releases the charges this credit applies to' = 13. Phone: phone.simulate 8 words; palette result rows 10 words each. Sign-in: 7 of 9 persona buttons over four words (max 7).
CLT-label-words.threshold: Visible label <= 4 words: 100% pass; accessible name <= 12 words: 100% pass. Baseline: Chairs 22-word summary label, Close 14, Phone 8 and sign-in 7 fail the visible rule; Board 13-word accessible name fails the name rule.
CLT-label-words.scope_correction: All eight claimed screens fail at least one clause, but two counts are inflated: on Roles only 1 of the 7 listed person-row buttons exceeds four words (the other six - 'Dr. Blake Reagan · DDS', 'Bree Lawson · RDH' and so on - are 4 words or fewer once the · is stripped; the auditor quoted the over-THREE-words list), and on sign-in 7 of 9 persona buttons exceed four words, not 8 ('OwnerLands on Daily Close' is 4). Checkout and Money pass at rest: their failing labels need a typed amount and a Post matched press respectively.
CLT-label-words.why: Every screen named reproduces a label or accessible name past its registered ceiling from a clean page, with only the Roles and sign-in failure counts needing correction.
CLT-label-words.fix_direction: Split the long labels from their explanations: caret/word-only buttons on the Chairs strip and Close tile, 'As of today' with the basis in the hint, role names on sign-in with the landing line in aria-describedby, and shorter accessible names on the Board queue and Credits row actions.

CLT-prose-budget.my_measurement: 1280x900 light unless noted, prose = visible text nodes outside controls, headings, th, label and .chip. Ledger: proseBeforeFinishMax 48 (Statement region, before ledger.statement.send) and proseWordsAboveFold 134 desk / 80 at 420. Close: 73 before finish and 153 above the fold at desk (110 at 420, which passes the fold clause); with the confirm step open the above-fold count rises to 221. Risk: 187 above the fold at desk, 140 at 420; proseBeforeFinishMax 0. Roles: 70 above the fold closed, but with the day-pass form open 59 words stand before Issue day pass and 101 above the fold. Money: 94 before finish and 129 above the fold (128 at 420); 145 above the fold with the write-off form open. Phone approvals after Simulate: 64 before finish and 149 above the fold (148 at 420). Checkout, as the auditor says, passes both: 0 before finish, 71 above the fold.
CLT-prose-budget.threshold: proseBeforeFinishMax <= 40 and proseWordsAboveFold <= 120 pass. Baseline failures: Money 94 before finish, Close 73, Phone 64, Ledger 48; above fold Risk 187, Close 153, Phone 149, Ledger 134, Money 129.
CLT-prose-budget.why: Every number the claim gives reproduced to the word from a clean page, on the wrong side of both the 40-word and the 120-word ceilings on all five claimed screens.
CLT-prose-budget.fix_direction: Move the standing explanations (Statement sentences, the frozen-atomically sub-line, the risk rule clauses, the dual-release hint, the repeated store sentence) behind the Why disclosures each region already owns, leaving one line of prose before each finish.

INT-keep-data-and-gate-on-press.my_measurement: 1280x900 light, fresh page per leg. Encounter enc-9002: 0 .refusal before any blur; typing 'Caries #30 DO confirmed.' into Assessment and pressing Tab renders the refusal row 'Chart or dismiss tag #30' within ~300ms with no press (encounter.js:423-433 onNoteBlur), and the typed text is kept verbatim. Palette: '13/45/1990' + Tab sets aria-invalid="true", class 'input pal-dob invalid' and rewrites the hint to 'Use MM/DD/YYYY, for example 04/12/1978.' with 0 .refusal; a wrong-but-valid DOB pressed through Open chart keeps '01/01/1900' in the field and puts focus on refusal.control (correct). Phone Send back: leaving the reason empty and tabbing away rewrites the hint to 'One line for the biller: what should happen first?' in rgb(154, 52, 18), 0 .refusal, aria-invalid unset. Author PIN pad (topbar.author): four digits typed, display '••••'; pressing Go leaves the display '' with the refusal 'Retype the PIN — no match' standing - the typed value is erased by the refusal. Phone step-up pad: same four digits, and a wrong PIN closes the pad entirely, so the digits are gone there too. Perio tag: leaving Observation empty on Tab sets aria-invalid="true", class 'input invalid', border rgb(234, 88, 12) and appends 'Say what you saw.'; pressing Save tag with it empty keeps Tooth '3' and lands focus on the empty field.
INT-keep-data-and-gate-on-press.threshold: 0 fields cleared by a refusal; 0 refusals raised on blur; focus on refusal or field in 100% of cases
