INT-keep-data-and-gate-on-press.scope_correction: All three claimed screens fail, but only Encounter raises an actual .refusal on blur; on Overlays (palette DOB, phone reason) and Perio the blur pass sets aria-invalid + an error hint and raises no .refusal, so the literal 'refusals raised on blur' counter stays at 0 there and the breach is of the statement's second half ('validation happens when they press'), not of that counter. The 'field cleared by a refusal' clause fails on the two PIN pads only.
INT-keep-data-and-gate-on-press.why: Reproduced on a clean page: validation fires on leaving a field on all three screens and both PIN pads wipe the typed digits before the refusal renders, against a threshold of 0 for each; nothing typed into a text field is lost, as the claim also says.
INT-keep-data-and-gate-on-press.fix_direction: Move every blur check to the press (blur may only clear an existing error) and keep the typed digits in the PIN display after a miss, offering the Clear control the gate already carries.

CUST-tokens-rem.my_measurement: #/owner/close at 1280x900 light: baseline html 16px, body 15px, .btn min-height 44px, h1 26px; tokens --target 44px and --fs-1..6 13/15/17/20/26/34px - 7 px-valued tokens. After page.addStyleTag('html{font-size:32px}') the root reads 32px while body stays 15px, .btn min-height stays 44px (rendered height 44px) and h1 stays 26px: 0% growth against the 2x the threshold requires, and still 7 px-valued tokens.
CUST-tokens-rem.threshold: Body computed font-size >= 2x baseline and .btn min-height >= 2x baseline after the html font-size change; 0 px-valued --fs-* or --target tokens.
CUST-tokens-rem.scope_correction: The tokens are global (prototype/css/tokens.css), so the same 0% growth holds on every screen, not only Close - the claim's single-screen scope understates it.
CUST-tokens-rem.why: Doubling the root font size moved neither the body text nor the target height by a pixel, and every --fs-* and --target token is still declared in px.
CUST-tokens-rem.fix_direction: Redeclare --fs-1..--fs-6 and --target in rem against a 16px root so an OS or browser font-size setting scales text and targets together.

CDS-TABLE-density.my_measurement: 1280x900 light. table.data.co-lines (Checkout), table.data.ledger-table (Ledger) and table.data.rl-table (Roles) all compute td/th padding 8px 12px 8px 12px: padding-top 8px is inside [8,12], padding-right 12px is below [16,24]. Passing on all three: border-bottom 1px, th font-weight 700, td font-size 15px = body 15px. Row heights: checkout body rows 54-58px, ledger body rows 39px, roles body rows up to 120px - all above 36px - but every thead row computes 35px, just under the 36px clause. Close .tender rows: row padding 8px 12px 8px 12px (padding-right again 12px), border-bottom 1px solid, row height 46px (head 37px), data cells 15px, head cells 13px/600. table.perio: td padding 0px and border-bottom 0px (44px cells spaced by border-spacing), td 15px, th 13px/600. Distinct body-cell density presets across the prototype: 2 - '8px 12px 8px 12px' (all data tables and the Close tender grid) and '0px' (the perio input matrix).
CDS-TABLE-density.threshold: padding-top in [8,12]px, padding-right in [16,24]px, border-bottom 1px, th font-weight >= 600, td font-size >= body size, row height >= 36px; <= 2 distinct density presets across the prototype.
CDS-TABLE-density.scope_correction: All four claimed screens fail on padding-right (and perio additionally on padding-top 0 and border-bottom 0). Two corrections: the perio row calls its grid 'a third density preset' - counting body cells there are only 2 presets in the whole prototype, so that clause passes; and the header rows of the data tables measure 35px, one pixel under the row-height clause, which no row of the claim mentions.
CDS-TABLE-density.why: Every data table and the Close tender grid pad 12px to the right where the rule asks 16-24px, and the perio grid pads 0 with no bottom rule - reproduced on all four screens.
CDS-TABLE-density.fix_direction: Take table.data and .tender cell padding-right to 16-20px (GOV.UK 8px 20px 8px 0) and either exempt the role=grid input matrix or give it the same rule.

CLT-serial-position.my_measurement: 1280x900 light, region = the enclosing <section>/.card that holds the finish control. Checkout: inside section 'Payment' (10 visible controls) checkout.post is followed by checkout.payment.why - checkout.js:232 renders section('Payment', seg, body, wo, finishRow, why). Ledger: inside section 'Statement' ledger.statement.send is followed by ledger.statement.preview and ledger.statement.why. Money: money.era.era-1.postmatched is followed by money.era.era-1.why; after Post matched each of the three read-back rows puts the irreversible Confirm first, followed by Set aside, Dispute and Why (3 controls after the finish on all three rows); the write-off card ends on its Post. Perio: the page-head perio.save is last in its row (passes), but perio.tag.save is followed by perio.tag.cancel and the omission-gate card 'Reason the sites were not probed' ends with perio.licence.cancel after the four reason buttons. Persona navs all start with their landing screen: frontdesk ['Board', ...], biller ['Money Desk', ...], hygienist ['Chairs', 'Board'], owner ['Daily Close', ...] - that clause passes, as the claim says.
CLT-serial-position.threshold: 100% of finish regions end with the finish button; 100% of persona navs start with the landing screen; >= 90% of card action rows lead with the advancing action.
CLT-serial-position.why: Six finish regions across the three claimed screens end on a Why disclosure, a Preview, a Cancel or three secondary actions instead of on their finish control, against a threshold of 100%.
CLT-serial-position.fix_direction: Render the Why disclosure (and Preview / Cancel) above the finish row so the last control in every region is the one that finishes it.

CUST-3.3.7-remembered-layout.my_measurement: #/temp/board at 1280x900 light as u-temp: before the press the store's only layout-ish root key is railState (keyed by user id, {} at load) and the toggle reads 'Hide'. Pressing rail1.toggle sets window.__proto.state().rail1Collapsed = true as an own property of the store root (rootLevelKey true), with nothing written under any railState[userId] bucket (nestedUnderUser false); the toggle then reads 'Show first-shift steps'. shell.js:171-172 reads and writes S.rail1Collapsed unconditionally, while the chip-retirement state next to it goes through Proto.store.railStateFor() -> S.railState[uid] (store.js:955-960). A reload drops it back to 'Hide' (the store is in-memory), so it is not restored after reload either.
CUST-3.3.7-remembered-layout.threshold: 100% of layout preferences keyed by userId; 0 cross-user leakage on shared devices; restored within the same render on switch and after reload.
CUST-3.3.7-remembered-layout.why: The measurable clause is exactly 'layout keys are nested under a userId, never at store root', and rail1Collapsed lands at the root while the per-user pattern (railState[uid]) sits two lines away in the same function.
CUST-3.3.7-remembered-layout.fix_direction: Write the collapsed flag into S.railState[userId] through railStateFor() so the rail follows the person rather than the device.

WCAG-2.2.1.threshold: 0 time limits under 20 hours without a turn-off, a >=10x adjustment, or a 20-second warning with >=10 extensions.

The gate reads "Wait five minutes — device locked" with the single control "Close"; measured remaining lock 299,914 ms. There is no turn-off, no 10x adjustment, no 20-second warning with extensions, and no countdown — the person is told "five minutes" once and the pad gives no way to see time remaining.

WCAG-4.1.3-status-messages.statement: Every state change that does not move focus is announced once through a live region that already exists at page load, and re-renders never announce chips.
WCAG-4.1.3-status-messages.threshold: 100% of focus-keeping state changes produce exactly one #live announcement within 300 ms; <= 2 live-region mutations per action; 0 assertive regions outside stop-severity; 0 duplicate announcements of the same gate.

rows.measured: Announcement path is right: Arrive -> #live receives "Marisol Vega arrived. Seat is the next step on the same card." once at 66 ms (1 mutation); Seat -> 2 mutations on #live (clear at 40 ms, set at 50 ms), text equals on-screen text. But the page carries 107 live regions (105 .chip[role=status] + #andon aria-live + #live), and every action re-renders the whole canvas: 105 of 105 role=status chips are destroyed and re-created after Arrive, and 106 of 106 after a Details toggle. Whether AT reads newly inserted role=status elements varies, so the "re-renders never announce chips" clause cannot be shown to hold; the 105 regions did not exist at page load as persistent regions.

CLT-chunk-4.statement: Keep each card or control group to at most four visible controls, never more than seven, so a gloved user can hold the whole group in working memory.

rows.measured: controlsPerCardMax = 8 on both routes (measure-baseline, all widths/themes); live: the card with 8 is section.card.flat.stack.queue (Checkout queue: 4 x "Ping chair" + 4 x "Checkout" across its .qrow rows). Appointment cards max 4 (board.card.a-1042: Re-verify, Arrive, Details, Rail); mean 2.75. Readiness card 5 (Hide + 4 row controls).
rows.evidence: measure-baseline.json board/temp-board controlsPerCardMax 8, controlsPerCardMean 2.75; audit/probes/board-probe-out.json probes.content[].maxCtrl, apptMax.
rows.fix: Treat each .qrow as the card (role=group already) and cap the section to the rows that need action now, or paginate the queue past 3 rows; appointment cards already sit at 4.

rows.measured: The Payment card holds 10 visible controls at rest on all 6 Checkout contexts (3 decision segments, 3 tenders, the Amount input, Add write-off, Post, Why) - above the 7 ceiling, not just the 4 target. Opening the write-off raises it to 15 (write-off amount, 4 reason codes, Remove write-off). The Ledger is inside the rule: controlsPerCardMax 3 (Statement: Send, Preview, Why), mean 1.
rows.evidence: measure-baseline.json checkout controlsPerCardMax 10 / controlsPerCardMean 4 at desk, operatory and phone in both themes; ledger controlsPerCardMax 3; audit/probes/out-checkout-ledger.json static.checkout.desk.light.cards[0] {name "Payment", controls 10} and checkout.writeoff-and-selfpay.wo.controlsInPaymentCard 15
rows.fix: Split the Payment card: decision + amount stay, tender and write-off move into their own named regions so no group exceeds four controls.

rows.measured: Risk: the "Due now" .card holds 8 visible controls (4 Why summaries + Open, Renew, Assign, Start) at every width and theme — over the 7 ceiling; each .dc-row inside it holds 2. Roles: the "People and entitlements" .card holds 11 (one row button per seat) at every width and theme, matching the registry baseline; with the day-pass form open the "Add day pass" .card holds 14 (name, 4 role, 3 location, shift end, 3 entitlement toggles, the extras Why, Issue day pass), and 15 once a gate adds its control.
rows.evidence: measure-baseline.json route=risk controlsPerCardMax 8, route=roles controlsPerCardMax 11 (all 6 contexts each); audit/probes/comp-static-out.json static.{risk,roles,rolesform}-*-*.cards[].controls (8 / 11 / 14)
rows.fix: Split the day-pass form into two labelled steps (who and when / what they may do) and page or group the People table by role so no single bounded card offers more than seven controls.

rows.measured: controlsPerCardMax is 40 on the Encounter at every width and theme (the Chart card: 32 teeth + 5 procedures + 3 temporality; the surfaces add 5 more once a tooth is picked, making 45). The registered exemption applies only if the odontogram is marked role='grid'; it is not — the two arches are role='group' with aria-labels 'Upper arch, teeth 1 to 16' and 'Lower arch, teeth 32 to 17' (encounter.js:284-285). Card mean is 9.8 across 5 cards. Exams passes at controlsPerCardMax 1.
rows.evidence: measure-baseline.json route 'encounter' controlsPerCardMax 40 / controlsPerCardMean 9.8 (all 6 records) and route 'exams' controlsPerCardMax 1; out-encounter-static.json static.groups (role 'group' on both arches)
rows.fix: Mark the odontogram role='grid' with roving tabindex (which also cuts 32 Tab stops to 1) so the anatomical map is read as one widget, and split Procedure/When out of the Chart card into their own named card.

rows.measured: 1024 light: page-head .btnrow holds 5 controls (Full chart, Screening, Glove pad, Settings, Save exam) - warning band; the Glove pad role=group holds 15 controls; the "Tag for the dentist" card holds 10 (6 observation buttons + 2 inputs + Save tag + Cancel); the reason card 5. measure-baseline controlsPerCardMax 0 because no .card is rendered at load.

rows.measured: The 'Device and display' .btnrow holds 11 visible controls (Light, Dark, Desk, Operatory, Shared, Phone, Reduced motion, Grayscale, Privacy mode, Simulate outage, After hours) at every width and theme; .personas holds 9. measure-baseline controlsPerCardMax is 0 only because the screen has no .card; the .btnrow is a named container in the test.

rows.fix: Split the row into three labelled groups (Theme 2, Device 4, Options) and move the QA toggles (outage, after hours, grayscale) behind a labelled 'Test options' disclosure.

CLT-topbar-7.statement: Keep the persistent top bar to seven or fewer controls that fit on at most two rows at every supported width.
CLT-topbar-7.threshold: topbarControls <= 7 and topbarRows <= 2 at every width passes; 8-9 controls is a warning; >= 10 controls or >= 3 rows fails. Baseline: Ledger 19 controls / 11 rows desk and 10 rows phone; Close and Risk 14 controls / 5-7 rows; Board 11 controls / 3-4 rows all fail.

rows.measured: measure-baseline: Board topbarControls 11, topbarRows 3 (desk/phone) and 4 (operatory); temp Board 9 / 3. Live probe at 1280/1024/420: frontdesk 9 controls (Main St, Search ⌘K, Board, Money Desk, Roles, author chip, Privacy mode, Dark, Sign out) on 1 row at 1280, 2 rows at 1024 (Sign out wraps), 1 row at 420 but as a horizontal scroller with 6 of 9 controls off-screen; temp 7 controls, 1 row everywhere, 4 of 7 off-screen at 420. The baseline's row count bucketed offsetTop by 8 px, which splits same-row controls of different heights, so its 3-4 rows are not visible rows (the baseline screenshots show 1 row at 1280, 2 at 1024). Live frontdesk = 9 controls is the 8-9 warning band; the phone bar hiding 6 controls is the operative failure.
rows.evidence: measure-baseline.json topbarControls/topbarRows; audit/probes/board-probe-out.json probes.topbar[] (controls, rows, rowTops, offscreen); baseline/frontdesk-board--desk-light.png (1 row), --operatory-light.png (Sign out on row 2), --phone-light.png (bar cut at "Money Des").
rows.fix: Fold Privacy mode, Dark and Sign out behind the author chip (one "You" menu) so the bar is 6 controls on one row at every width and never scrolls sideways.

rows.measured: topbarControls 9 on 6/6 chairs contexts (> 7, inside the 8-9 warning band, not a fail on controls). topbarRows: 2 at desk 1280 and phone 420 (pass), 3 at operatory 1024 in both themes -> the registered ">= 3 rows fails" side. Live rowTops confirm the three bands [-60, 8, 60]: -60 is the off-screen skip link, 8 and 60 are two visible rows (Sign out wraps below at 1024), so the visible count is 2 and the metric counts the skip link consistently at every width. Shell-wide; lens owns the cross-screen count.
rows.evidence: measure-baseline.json route=chairs topbarControls 9, topbarRows 3 (operatory light and dark) vs 2 (desk, phone); audit/probes/chairs-result.json static.operatory-*.topbar.rowTops [-60, 8, 60] vs static.desk-*.topbar.rowTops [-60, 8]; baseline/hygienist-chairs--operatory-light.png (Sign out on a second row)
rows.fix: Let the top bar drop the location and practice text at 1024 (or shrink the nav to icons + label) so Sign out stays on the first row; and stop counting the off-screen skip link as a top-bar row.

rows.measured: Registered counts: Checkout topbarControls 13 with topbarRows 5 (desk and phone) and 6 (operatory); Ledger topbarControls 19 with topbarRows 11 (desk and operatory) and 10 (phone) - the worst top bar in the set on both control count and row count. Scoping note for the verifier: measure.cjs counts every control under #topbar, which on the Ledger takes in the open patient rail; measured against .topbar alone the live counts are 9 controls / 1-2 rows on Checkout and 10 controls / 2 rows on the Ledger at 1280 - still at or over the 10-control fail line on the Ledger, and at 420 the bar becomes a nowrap horizontal scroller hiding 5 (Checkout) and 6 (Ledger) controls off-screen. Shell component, same root cause as the Board.
rows.evidence: measure-baseline.json checkout {topbarControls 13, topbarRows 5/6/5} and ledger {topbarControls 19, topbarRows 11/11/10}; audit/probes/out-checkout-ledger.json static.checkout.desk.light.topbar {controls 9, rows 1} and scroll.ledger["1280"].topbar.rows 2; out-checkout-ledger-2.json topbar.offscreen (checkout@420 5 off-screen, ledger@420 6, ledger@320 7); baseline/ledger-rail--desk-light.png shows Sign out wrapped onto a second row at 1280
rows.fix: Shell fix: move Privacy mode, theme and Sign out behind the author chip so the persistent bar keeps seven or fewer controls on two rows at 420.

rows.measured: measure-baseline records 14 top-bar controls on 5 rows at desk and operatory and 4 rows at phone for this route - both past the failing bar. Re-read live at 1280x800 the sticky header holds 11 visible controls on 2 rows (height 113px, flex-wrap wrap); at 420 and 320 it becomes a single 57px row that scrolls sideways (scrollWidth 1271) with 9 of 11 controls off-screen at rest but still Tab-reachable. Either count is above 7. This is the shell's top bar, not this screen's; it is recorded once here with the surfaces it was seen on.
rows.evidence: measure-baseline.json route close topbarControls 14 / topbarRows 5 (desk, operatory) and 4 (phone); close-probe.json legs['static:desk-light'].topbar (controls 11, rows 2, tops [8,60]) and legs.reflow320.topbarBtnsOffscreenAtRest (9 labels)
rows.fix: Collapse the persona nav and the display switches into one overflow control so the bar keeps at most seven items on two rows.

rows.measured: Measured live on the real #topbar: 9 controls on both routes at every width and theme (Main St, Search ⌘K, Practice risk, Roles, Daily Close, the Noor author chip, Privacy mode, Dark/Light, Sign out) — inside the 8-9 warning band, not the fail band on count. Rows: 1 at 1280 (rowTops [8]), 2 at 1024 (rowTops [8, 60] — Sign out wraps), 1 at 420 but as a horizontal scroller (scrollWidth 995 vs 420) with 6 of the 9 controls off-screen, and 7 of 9 off-screen at 320. measure-baseline reports risk 14 controls / 5-7 rows and roles 10 / 2-3, but those figures are inflated: measure.cjs builds its selector as "#topbar " + CONTROL, so the descendant combinator binds only to the first term and every a[href], summary and input on the page is counted as a top-bar control (risk's 4 "Why" summaries plus the skip link explain 9 + 5 = 14). Shell-wide; the lens owns the cross-screen count.
rows.evidence: audit/probes/comp-static-out.json static.*.topbar {controls 9, rowTops, offscreen, scrolls}; legs.reflow320-*.topbar.offscreen (7 of 9); measure-baseline.json route=risk/roles topbarControls/topbarRows vs measure.cjs:21,46; baseline/compliance-risk--phone-light.png (bar cut after "Role"), roles--phone-light.png
rows.fix: Fold Privacy mode, theme and Sign out behind the author chip so the bar is 6 controls that fit one row at every width and never scrolls sideways.

This is the shell's top bar, seen identically on both of my screens.

rows.fix: Shell-level: keep brand, search, the three nav items and the current screen marker in the bar and move author, privacy, theme and sign out behind one labelled account control.

rows.measured: The shared top bar carries 12 controls on 4 rows at desk and operatory and 3 rows at phone on this route (measure-baseline, all six money records). Live at 1280 it renders 10 visible controls on 2 rows, 113px tall; at 420 it becomes a single 57px row that scrolls sideways (scrollWidth 1075 vs clientWidth 420). Either reading is at or past the fail line of 10 controls.

rows.measured: measure-baseline route "phone": topbarControls 13 and topbarRows 4 at desk (1280) and operatory (1024), 13 controls / 3 rows at 420 — >= 10 controls and >= 3 rows, the outright fail band on both counts. My own count of visible Tab-reachable top-bar controls on the same route is 11 across 2 rows at 1280 and 11 on a single non-wrapping row at 420, where #topbar scrollWidth is 1271 against a 420 viewport (recorded as reflow under WCAG-1.4.10). Same bar stands over the palette (opened from Board) and the author pad (opened from Perio).

Live read at 1024: 8 visible controls on 2 visual rows (Sign out wraps to row 2; the ninth counted control is the off-screen skip link at top:8, which the row bucketing counts as a row). Either way 8-9 controls is the warning band and the operatory profile wraps.

CLT-recognition-keys.statement: Show every keyboard shortcut on the control it triggers, never only in a legend the user has to remember.
CLT-recognition-keys.threshold: 0 legend-only shortcuts per screen. Any shortcut that exists only in the .sub legend fails; the legend may stay as a duplicate but not as the sole source.

rows.measured: The .sub legend names three keys ("keys: A arrive, S seat, C checkout"); 0 of the 3 matching buttons carry aria-keyshortcuts or a <kbd> child (Arrive and Checkout present on load, Seat appears after Arrive and is built by the same btn() call without a marker). 3 legend-only shortcuts.
rows.evidence: audit/probes/board-probe-out.json probes.content[].keyed (ariaKeyshortcuts null, kbd false); probes.static.keyshortcuts = []; board.js:256-258, 363.
rows.fix: Add aria-keyshortcuts="A"/"S"/"C" and a small <kbd> to the Arrive/Seat/Checkout buttons; the legend may stay as a duplicate.

rows.measured: Page-head .sub legend "keys: P perio, N note, R focus Ready for exam" (10 of the sub-line's 18 words) names 3 keys; 0 of the 18 Chart perio / Write note buttons (and 0 of 1 Ready for exam when rendered) carry aria-keyshortcuts or a visible <kbd> -> 3 legend-only shortcuts per screen, the sole source.
rows.evidence: audit/probes/chairs-result.json static.*.cards[].buttons[].{keyshortcuts:null,kbd:false}; head.sub; probes/chairs-tab2.json sub {words 18, keysWords 10}; measure-baseline.json route=chairs subWords 18
rows.fix: Put aria-keyshortcuts="p"/"n"/"r" and a small <kbd> on the buttons themselves; the legend may stay as a duplicate.

rows.measured: One accelerator is live while this screen is mounted - T toggles the tile - and it exists only in the page-head legend: the .sub reads 'Tap the tile or press T', the tile itself carries no aria-keyshortcuts (null), no <kbd> element exists anywhere on the screen (kbd = 0) and the tile's visible label is '▲1 variance / Yesterday 9/2 · 3 locations · detection lag 1 day · bank feed'. 1 legend-only shortcut, threshold 0.
rows.evidence: close-probe.json legs['accelerator:T'].pre (subMentionsKey true, tileKeyshortcuts null, kbd 0) and .post (expanded false -> true on 't')
rows.fix: Print the key on the tile itself (a kbd chip in the tile's caret area) and set aria-keyshortcuts='t' on the button.

rows.measured: The page-head sub line advertises three keys — "Keys: P post matched · W write-off · A appeal" — and no control carries the letter where the hand is. Post matched has no aria-keyshortcuts and no visible <kbd>; the letter survives only inside the accessible name ("Post matched lines (P)", "Write-off or adjustment for Lena Fischer (W)", "Appeal claim c-88 ... (A)"), which a sighted mouse user never sees. 3 legend-only shortcuts.
rows.evidence: measure-baseline.json route "money" subText; a2 static_1280.labelsLoad (txt "Post matched" vs name "Post matched lines (P)"; no kbd child); moneydesk.js onKey() P/W/A
rows.fix: Put the letter on the control (a <kbd>P</kbd> in the label plus aria-keyshortcuts="P") and let the sub line be the duplicate.

rows.measured: Sub legend names 6 keys (1–9 depth, Space bleeding, S suppuration, ⌫ undo, → skip, PgDn next tooth). Glove pad closed at load, so all 6 exist only in the legend; when opened, its keys carry no <kbd> and no aria-keyshortcuts (15/15 false/null): "Bleed" shows no Space, "Supp" no S, "Next tooth" no PgDn. Only ⌫ and → repeat the legend glyph. Screening lane legend (0–4, *, ⌫, →) likewise has no on-control markers.
rows.evidence: perio-probe.cjs interact.pad.keys[].kbd=false, keyshortcuts=null; static_operatory.sub.text; grep aria-keyshortcuts in perio.js = 0.
rows.fix: Print the key on each pad button (<kbd>Space</kbd> Bleed, <kbd>S</kbd> Supp, <kbd>PgDn</kbd> Next tooth) and add aria-keyshortcuts; then the sub legend can shrink.

INT-no-double-submit.statement: A double press on a primary control never performs the action twice.

rows.measured: Arrive on board.card.a-1042: page.dblclick -> status "arrived" once (second click refused by the ev.detail > 1 guard); two mouse clicks 80 ms apart at the same point -> "arrived" once (Chromium counts the second as detail 2). Two separate click events with detail 1 dispatched 80 ms apart at the same slot -> the second landed on the Seat button that rendered into the Arrive slot and the patient is "seated" (events +10 vs +6 for one Arrive): the gap the detail check leaves is real for click sources that do not increment detail (switch/voice/automation).

rows.fix: After a primary press, ignore a second press on the same slot for ~300 ms (timestamp on the card or a data-busy attribute) rather than relying on ev.detail.

The values that are on the scale: .stack gap 12px between cards, .btnrow and .seg gap 8px, .card padding.

CDS-STATUS-roles-max.statement: Keep status semantics to at most five or six named roles (USWDS: error, warning, success, info, emergency; GOV.UK tags add neutral grey), each with a light background/dark ink pair; more steps than a user can name is noise.
CDS-STATUS-roles-max.threshold: <= 6 severity roles total (prototype has exactly 6: stop, required, review, style, info, clear); <= 4 distinct severities on one screen; soft/ink contrast >= 4.5:1 in both themes; luminance strictly monotonic stop < required < review < style < info < clear in grayscale.

rows.measured: 6 severity roles exist and all 6 render on the Board at once (stop: Surgery; required: 1 alert, Device; review: Re-verify, Case not back, Eligibility…; style: Restorative; info: Confirmed, Scheduled…; clear: Active, Note filed) — > 4 on one screen. Soft/ink contrast per severity: light 6.88-16.86:1, dark 8.58-11.38:1 (all >= 4.5). Grayscale luminance order not measured here (tokens lens).
rows.evidence: audit/probes/board-probe-out.json probes.content[].severities (6), probes.contrast[].chipBorder[].inkOnSoft.
rows.fix: Reserve the severity ladder for state that needs action (stop/required/review/clear) and render type words (Hygiene/Restorative/Surgery/Exam) as one neutral chip or plain text.

rows.measured: Six severity roles exist, which is within the ceiling, and at most 3 appear on one screen at once (Checkout review + clear + info; Ledger clear only), also within the ceiling, and every soft/ink pair clears 4.5:1 (the full text sweep found 0 failing nodes in either theme). The ladder fails: relative luminance of the six soft fills is not monotonic in either theme. Light: stop 0.9099, required 0.9390, review 0.9625, style 0.9073, info 0.9536, clear 0.9468 - two inversions (review above style, info above clear). Dark: 0.0145, 0.0194, 0.0257, 0.0173, 0.0215, 0.0220 - one inversion (review above style). In grayscale a review fill reads lighter than an info fill, so the ladder carries no order.
rows.evidence: audit/probes/cl3.json gray.*.sev (light #FEF2F2/#FFF7ED/#FFFBEB/#F5F3FF/#F8FAFC/#ECFDF5; dark #3A1414/#3B1F0E/#3A2A08/#2A1A4A/#1F2937/#0F2E26), relative luminance computed from those hexes; out-checkout-ledger.json static.*.severityFillsFirstScreen 3 (checkout) and 2 (ledger); contrast.*.failing 0
rows.fix: Token fix: restep the six soft fills so luminance rises strictly from stop to clear in both themes (style and clear are the two out of order).

rows.measured: Six severity roles exist product-wide, which is inside the ceiling, and every soft/ink pair clears 4.5:1 in both themes (light 6.88-16.86:1, dark 8.58-10.52:1). Two clauses fail on this screen. Distinct severities visible at once: 4 collapsed (review, info, required, stop) but 5 with the tile open (clear joins) - past the '<= 4 on one screen' bar. Grayscale luminance is not monotonic: light stop 0.9099 < required 0.9390 < clear 0.9468 < info 0.9536 < review 0.9625; dark stop 0.0145 < required 0.0194 < info 0.0215 < review 0.0257, against the registered order stop < required < review < style < info < clear.
rows.evidence: close-probe.json legs['static:*'].chips.severities (4) vs legs['tile:desk'].after.chips.severities (5: clear, review, required, info, stop); close-probe3.json legs['state:allopen-light'].sev[].lum and .inkOnSoft
rows.fix: Re-tune the review and clear soft fills so the ladder is monotonic, and keep 'clear' off a screen that is already showing four severities.

CDS-TAG-tint-shade.threshold: font-size >= 13px; font-weight >= 600; text/background contrast >= 4.5:1 in both themes; padding-x == 8px (prototype 10px fails scale); 0 non-interactive chips with cursor pointer.

rows.measured: .chip: font-size 13px (>= 13 ok), font-weight 600 (ok), text/background contrast 6.88-16.86:1 light and 8.58-11.38:1 dark (ok), cursor auto and no handler (ok), padding-x 10px (fails the 8px rule).
rows.evidence: audit/probes/board-probe-out.json probes.content[].chipStyle, probes.contrast[].chipBorder[].inkOnSoft; components.css:40.
rows.fix: Set .chip padding to 0 8px (same fix as CDS-SPACE-scale-4-8).

rows.measured: .chip: 13px / 600 (pass), padding-x 10px on all 20 chips (registry: 8px; 10px fails the scale) — shared component; and 4 chips inside the strip button carry cursor:pointer (chairs-specific).
rows.evidence: audit/probes/chairs-result.json static.*.chips.{fs ["13px"], fw ["600"], padX ["10px"], cursorPointer 4}; components.css:40
rows.fix: Set .chip padding to 0 8px; take chips out of the strip button.

rows.measured: Chips get the type and the behaviour right - 13px at weight 600, dark ink on a light tint of the same hue with 0 contrast failures in either theme, role="status", cursor auto, tabindex null and no handler, so none looks clickable. The spacing is off-scale: padding-left/right computes 10px on all 6 chips across both screens where the rule asks for 8px.
rows.evidence: audit/probes/out-checkout-ledger.json static.*.chips[] {font "13px", weight "600", padX "10px", cursor "auto", tabindex null, interactive false}; cl3.json contrast.*.failing 0 (chip labels included in the sweep)

Two clauses fail: padding-x is 10px, not the 8px the scale calls for (the registered baseline names this), and 3 of 13 chips have cursor: pointer because they are nested inside the .dc-loc location buttons ('●Tied · independent', '◆Tied · needs a second look', '▲1 variance'), so a static status tag reads as clickable.

CDS-ICON-size-24.threshold: Icon box >= 20px on buttons and >= 16px on chips; 0 meaning-carrying glyphs under 16px (prototype 11px glyphs fail).

rows.measured: Meaning-carrying glyphs on chips (.chip .glyph ■▲◆★▬●) render at 11px (computed font-size), under the 16px chip minimum; the held button's 🔒 ::before is 14px (< 20px for buttons). The glyphs are duplicated by the chip word, but the rule counts the icon box.

The .btn.irreversible ::before bar "▮" computes 11px on both checkout.post and ledger.statement.send, under the 20px button minimum. The refusal severity glyph "▲" computes 15px. CUST-2.1.4-shortcuts-optin.statement: Single-character keyboard accelerators are off by default and switchable per user; only modifier shortcuts (Ctrl/Cmd+K) ship on, and every accelerator duplicates a visible control.
CUST-2.1.4-shortcuts-optin.threshold: 0 single-key actions outside a focused component with accelerators off; 1 off switch; 100% of accelerators have a visible equivalent; state persists per user.

rows.measured: With focus on body and no dialog, pressing "a" on the Board arrives the next patient (arrived count 0 -> 1, hash unchanged); "s" and "c" seat / open checkout the same way (board.js onKey). The accelerators are on by default, there is no off switch (0 controls matching accel|shortcut|keys), and the setting cannot persist per user. Ctrl/Cmd+K is the only modifier shortcut.
rows.evidence: audit/probes/board-probe-out.json probes.arriveSeat.accelerator (arrivedBefore 0, arrivedAfter 1, offSwitch false); board.js:342-356.
rows.fix: Ship A/S/C off by default with a per-user "Keyboard accelerators" toggle (and a visible <kbd> on each control when on).

rows.measured: Default settings, focus on body, no dialog: single key "p" changes route to #/hygienist/perio/enc-9001 (2 events logged), "n" to #/hygienist/encounter/enc-9001, "r" moves focus; 0 accelerator off-switch anywhere on the screen (0 controls matching accelerat|shortcut|keys); the other 33 letters/digits had no effect. Visible equivalents exist (Chart perio, Write note buttons). Accelerators are on by default with no per-user opt-in.
rows.evidence: audit/probes/chairs-result.json actions.keys {afterP.hash, afterN.hash, offSwitch []}; chairs.js:193-211
rows.fix: Gate the keydown handler behind a per-user "accelerators" preference (default off) with a visible switch, and mark the keys on the buttons.

rows.measured: This screen registers a single-character accelerator with no modifier and no off switch: while mounted, 't' or 'T' toggles the tile (aria-expanded false -> true, focus returned to close.tied.tile) whenever focus is outside an input and no overlay is open. There is no per-user switch to turn it off (settingsOff = []) and the key is not exposed on the control (aria-keyshortcuts null). It does duplicate a visible control - the tile itself - so that clause passes. Other single keys (a, s, c, p, w, n, r, m, k, 1, Delete) are logged but change nothing.
rows.evidence: close-probe.json legs['accelerator:T'].pre (settingsOff [], tileKeyshortcuts null) and .post (expanded true); close-probe2.json legs.strayKey (key 'a' logged, tile unchanged; 't' expands); dailyclose.js onKey/attachKeys
rows.fix: Ship T off by default behind the same per-user accelerator switch the customization body describes, and print the key on the tile.

rows.measured: The Money Desk installs three single-key accelerators while it is mounted — P, W and A on document keydown — with no way to turn them off anywhere in the product and no per-user state. They are mitigated by design: the handler ignores keys while an INPUT/TEXTAREA/SELECT has focus or a dialog is open, and each key only moves the keyboard to the control (pressing "p" left the ledger at 119 rows and focused money.era.era-1.postmatched), and each has a visible on-screen equivalent. The missing piece is the off switch.
rows.evidence: a2 behaviour.keyP {ledgerBefore 119, ledgerAfter 119, active "money.era.era-1.postmatched"}; moneydesk.js onKey()/attachKeys(); no toggle in the shell top bar (mp A_load_desk_light.topbar.navLabels)
rows.fix: Add one product-wide "single-key shortcuts" switch (default on is fine) and key it per user; the screens already route every key through one handler.

rows.measured: The perio grammar (1–9, 0, S, Space, Backspace, arrows, PageUp/Down) is a document-level keydown handler active whenever the route is mounted and focus is not in an input/dialog - including when focus is on Save exam or Settings (Space on a focused control toggles bleeding instead of activating it: flow.spaceOnSave lastBleed 1, saved false). No per-user off switch, no remap. Every key duplicates a visible pad control (when the pad is open).
rows.evidence: perio.js:147-179 onKey (document keydown; onControl && k===" " -> bleed); perio-probe.cjs flow.spaceOnSave {saved:false, lastBleed:1}; interact.afterKey3 (key acts with focus on h1).
rows.fix: Scope the handler to focus inside .perio-wrap / .pad / the active-site line (make the grid role=grid the focused component), or add a per-user "Keys on/off" switch in Perio settings; keep Enter/Space native on buttons.

CUST-3.3.7-remembered-layout.statement: Remember each user's layout choices (rail open/collapsed, first-shift rail hidden, last filter) under their user id and restore them on PIN switch, so nobody re-sets what they already set.
CUST-3.3.7-remembered-layout.threshold: 100% of layout preferences keyed by userId; 0 cross-user leakage on shared devices; restored within the same render on switch and after reload.

rows.measured: Pressing rail1 Hide on the temp Board writes S.rail1Collapsed = true at the store root (window.__proto.state().rail1Collapsed exists, not nested under a userId), so the first-shift rail's collapsed state is shared by every user on the device; the toggle then reads "Show first-shift steps".
rows.evidence: audit/probes/board-probe-out.json probes.temp.rail1Hidden (rootLevelKey true, value true); shell.js:171-172.
rows.fix: Move rail1Collapsed under S.railState[userId] (the pattern railStateFor() already uses) so it follows the person, not the device.

CDS-WARNING-text-icon.statement: Before an irreversible or legally significant action, show bold warning text with a large non-colour icon (GOV.UK: 35px black circle with '!') so the warning survives grayscale and forced colours.
CDS-WARNING-text-icon.threshold: 100% of irreversible confirms carry bold text plus an icon >= 24px; icon contrast >= 3:1 in grayscale.

rows.measured: The board refusal (temp Board, Arrive without a day pass) carries bold text (span.verb font-weight 600, 15 px, "Issue a day pass before arriving") but its only icon is the text glyph span.glyph "▲" whose bounding box is 11.5 x 21.8 px at font-size 15 px — under the 24 px floor; there is no ::before (content: none) and 0 svg. Glyph contrast is 14.9:1 light, 13.66:1 dark, and it survives data-grayscale=1 (html filter grayscale(1)), so only the size clause fails. The one irreversible confirm reachable from this screen, the author PIN pad (topbar.author -> pin.submit "Go", kind irreversible), has bold text ("Who is charting?") and 0 glyphs and 0 svg icons at all.
rows.evidence: audit/probes/board-probe4.cjs -> board-probe4-out.json refusal_light/refusal_dark/refusal_grayscale (boldEls, glyph.box 11.5x21.8, glyph.contrast, beforePseudo.content = none, svgs = 0) and pinDialog (irreversible ["Go"], glyphs [], svgs 0); ui.js refusal() span.glyph.
rows.fix: Give .refusal .glyph and the irreversible confirm a 24 px block (font-size 20-24 px with a fixed 24x24 box, or an inline svg) so the severity mark is legible at arm length on the operatory tablet.

rows.measured: The refusal block raised on this screen (outage gate, severity stop) has its verb at weight 600 but the glyph ■ is 15px (box 14x22) < 24px; the irreversible Ready for exam opens no confirm dialog at all (see INT-irreversible-identity). Shared .refusal component.
rows.evidence: audit/probes/chairs-result.json actions.outage.gate.{verbFw "600", glyphFs "15px", glyphRect}; components.css:51; shot audit/shots/chairs-outage-gate.png
rows.fix: Size .refusal .glyph at 24px (var(--fs-5)) and keep it non-transparent under grayscale.

rows.measured: Nothing warns before the irreversible press on either screen. checkout.post and ledger.statement.send have no adjacent bold warning text and no icon of any size before they are pressed (warningTextNear false on both), and neither opens a confirm dialog (confirmDialog false on both commits), so there is no confirm step for a warning to live in. The one warning shape in the flow is the refusal that appears after a refused press, and its icon is undersized: the "▲" glyph computes 15px against the 24px the rule asks, though the verb beside it is correctly bold (600) at 15px and the block carries the sr-only word "Required" and a 6px severity rail that survives grayscale.
rows.evidence: audit/probes/out-checkout-ledger.json static.checkout.desk.light.irreversible[0].warningTextNear false and static.ledger.desk.light.irreversible[0].warningTextNear false, checkout.post-success.post.confirmDialog false, ledger.send-statement.post.confirmDialog false; cl4.json warn.checkout and warn.ledger {glyphText "▲", glyphSize "15px", verbWeight "600", borderLeft "6px", srWord "Required"}
rows.fix: Add a bold warning line with a >=24px non-colour icon to the read-back step that INT-irreversible-identity asks for, and raise the refusal glyph to 24px.

rows.measured: The Confirm close day step has bold warning text - the h3 'Close Main Street for 9/3?' at 17px weight 600 - but no icon at all: its ::before computes to 'none' and there is no glyph anywhere in the group. The nearest non-colour mark is the 11px '▮' bar inside the confirm button's ::before, well under the 24px the row asks for. Same at desk, operatory and phone. 0 of 1 irreversible confirms carry an icon.
rows.evidence: close-probe.json legs['closeday:desk'|'closeday:phone'].confirm.warningIcon (text, weight '600', before 'none'); legs['static:desk-light'].buttons close.closeday.before '▮' at 11px per legs['state:*'].sizes
rows.fix: Put a 24px or larger seal/lock mark beside the confirm heading - the Closed stamp already owns one (🔒) and could be reused.

The Amount hint before typing reads "Prefilled with the patient portion estimate."; the rule that it must exceed $0 appears for the first time in the refusal Why ("it cannot be blank, negative, or a value that is not a number"). The write-off hint reads "The dollar amount to write off this account." and never mentions the dual-release threshold that will hold the posting. The PIN field is capped at 6 characters by maxlength with no visible statement of the length. The Ledger is better: its as-of input is a constrained type=date with min 2026-06-01 and max 2026-09-03 and a hint stating the basis.

CUST-3.3.8-prefs-no-auth-cost.statement: Changing a preference never triggers an extra authentication step, and the PIN that identifies the user on shared devices has at least one non-memory alternative or assist.
CUST-3.3.8-prefs-no-auth-cost.threshold: 0 authentication prompts caused by preference changes; >= 1 non-memory alternative or assist on the PIN pad.

rows.measured: 0 authentication prompts are caused by a preference change - flipping theme, privacy or device profile from the top bar never raises a gate, and the PIN field is simply emptied when the device profile changes (by design, so a PIN typed for one device never carries). The second clause fails: the shared-desk PIN pad has no non-memory alternative and no assist - the field is a bare 6-character password box with inputmode numeric, no badge/tap alternative, no reveal, no 'forgot PIN' path, and the only recovery route offered is the refusal's own 'Enter PIN' control which returns to the same box.
rows.evidence: close-probe.json legs['pin:shared'].form (type password, inputmode numeric, maxlength 6, hint text, no alternative control) and .wrongGate ('Three misses lock this device for five minutes.'); dailyclose.js pinField() renders one input and nothing else
rows.fix: Offer at least one assist beside the field - a reveal toggle or a badge tap - so the shared desk does not rest on memory alone.

rows.measured: The preference half passes: pressing topbar.theme with the author pad or the phone screen open opens 0 PIN pads and writes 0 auth events. The PIN half fails on every clause. Both pads are pure memorised-secret entry with no alternative and no assist: a scan of the author pad for badge/NFC/tap/card/scan/password words returns false, there is no show-digits or reveal control (showDigitsControl false), and dispatching a paste of "222" onto pin.display leaves the display unchanged — the display is a role=textbox div with no paste handling. The typed digits cannot be reviewed before Go either: the display renders only "•" per digit, so a person who mistypes has no way to check what they entered and, on a miss, the buffer is cleared and all digits must be retyped from memory.
rows.evidence: audit/probes/overlays2-result.json pinpad/desk/light.head.{altAuth false, showDigitsControl false} and .pasteAttempt "•" (unchanged after a paste of "222"), .wrongPin.dotsCleared ""; overlays3-result.json pinpadTail/desk/light.themeToggle.pads 0; overlays-result.json phone/desk/light.themeToggle.pads 0
rows.fix: Add at least one assist to both pads — a show-digits toggle on the display, or paste support, or a badge tap — so identifying yourself is not a pure memory test.

rows.measured: Two failures. (1) Validation fires on blur on two of the five fields: typing "13/45/1990" into palette.confirm.dob and pressing Tab sets aria-invalid="true", adds .invalid and rewrites the hint to "Use MM/DD/YYYY, for example 04/12/1978." before any press; leaving the phone Send back reason empty and tabbing away rewrites its hint to "One line for the biller: what should happen first?" in the warn colour rgb(154, 52, 18). (2) A refusal erases what was typed: the author pad's submit() clears the digit buffer and the display before it verifies, so after "Retype the PIN — no match" the display reads "" and all four to six digits must be retyped. The palette behaves correctly — a mismatched DOB keeps "01/01/1900" in the field and lands focus on the refusal control; focus after a refusal lands on the refusal control, the field or the pressed control in 100% of the cases measured.
rows.evidence: audit/probes/overlays2-result.json palette/desk/light.blurValidation {ariaInvalid "true", cls "input pal-dob invalid", hint changed, refusals 0} and .mismatch.dobValueKept "01/01/1900"; pinpad/desk/light.wrongPin.dotsCleared ""; overlays-result.json phone/desk/light.reasonBlur {hintCls "hint ph-hint-warn", hintColor "rgb(154, 52, 18)"}
rows.fix: Move both blur checks to the press, and keep the typed PIN in the display after a miss (offer the Clear control that is already in the gate) instead of wiping it.

rows.measured: Tag form: after "Save tag" with an empty Observation, Tooth keeps "3" and the empty field keeps focus (ok); with tooth 1 + "Mobility", both values kept, focus on Tooth (ok). But leaving the empty Observation field (Tab out) sets aria-invalid="true", class invalid, orange border and appends "Say what you saw." on blur alone - validation on leave, not on press (no .refusal component is used, so the literal ".refusal on blur" check passes).
rows.evidence: perio-probe.cjs interact.tagBlur {ariaInvalid:"true", cls:"input invalid", hint:"… Say what you saw.", refusal:false}; perio.js:358-359 onBlur -> validateTag.
rows.fix: Validate on Save tag only; clear the blur handlers (or limit blur to removing an existing error).

TYPE-min-any-text-12.statement: Never render readable text below 12px; decorative glyphs may be smaller only if the same information is also given in text of 12px or more.
TYPE-min-any-text-12.threshold: Zero text nodes < 12px. Prototype has .psite .ghost 10px (168 instances on perio), .psite.bleed::after 9px, .psite.sup::before 9px, .chip .glyph 11px, .count 12px; the 9 and 10px cases fail unless the value is duplicated in >= 12px text.

rows.measured: Two text nodes render under 12px on the Encounter. The chip glyph '▲' at 11px is excused — it is aria-hidden and the same information is in 'Needs disposition' at 13px beside it. The charted-tooth mark '●' at 10px (inline style on the tooth button) is not: it is the only visible non-colour cue that a tooth has been charted, and no text of 12px or more repeats it — 'charted' appears only in the button's accessible name. Exams has 0 nodes under 12px.
rows.evidence: out-encounter-static.json static.textUnder12 [{text '▲', fs 11, sel 'glyph', ariaHidden 'true'}] (measured at load, before any paint) and exams leg static.textUnder12 []; /home/user/Dental_Mgmt/prototype/js/screens/encounter.js:282 ('font-size:10px' on the charted mark); out-enc-audit4.json axeIncomplete_light (the ▲ and ✓ nodes)
rows.fix: Draw the charted mark as a >= 16px shape (or a border treatment) and keep the word 'Charted' visible in the transaction card, which it already is.

rows.measured: Two text sources render under 12px on this screen, both of them meaning-carrying: .chip .glyph at 11px (the severity shape, which is the non-colour cue WCAG-1.4.1 relies on) and .btn.irreversible::before at 11px (the ▮ that marks an irreversible control). The 12px .count pills in the tabs are at the floor and pass.
rows.evidence: a2 static_1280.smallText [{fs:11, cls:"btn irreversible::before", t:"▮"}]; a3 res.*.chips (glyph 11px); measure-baseline.json route "money" fontSizes {"11px":3, "12px":7, ...}
rows.fix: Raise both glyph sizes to at least 12px (16px would also clear CDS-ICON-size-24).

rows.measured: Two text sizes under 12px on these surfaces, both 11px. The chip .glyph (▬ ◆ ● ▲) at 11px is excused by the registry's own rule — it is aria-hidden and the same meaning is carried by the chip word beside it at 13px. The ::before "▮" at 11px on pin.submit, phone.stepup.submit and each card Approve is not: it is the non-colour cue for the irreversible identity and no text of 12px or more says "irreversible" anywhere on the control. 3 nodes per screen (1 per irreversible button), at 1280 and 1024, both themes. No other text node in the three dialogs is under 13px.
rows.evidence: audit/probes/final.json pinpad@1280.pseudo [{sel "pin.submit", content "▮", fs 11}], stepup@1280.pseudo, phone@1280.pseudo; palette@1280.small (6 x 11px aria-hidden ▬, each beside "Patient" at 13px)
rows.fix: Render the ▮ at 12px or more, or add a visually hidden word so the identity is also in text.

rows.measured: 168 .psite .ghost prior-depth values at 10 px (rgb(86,97,122) light; rgb(167,178,196) dark) at every width and theme; only the active cell's prior value is duplicated in >= 12 px text ("Tooth 2 · site 1 · prior 3" at 20 px); the rest are exposed only via aria-description. Bleeding ● and suppuration ◆ pseudo-glyphs render at 9 px (meaning duplicated in the legend and aria-description). measure-baseline fontSizes "10px":168.
rows.evidence: measure-baseline.json perio fontSizes {"10px":168}; perio-probe.cjs static_operatory.ghost {fontSize:"10px", count:168}; interact.bleed.after "● 9px"; components.css:90, 93, 229.
rows.fix: Raise .ghost to 12-13 px (fits in a 44 px cell top-right) and the ●/◆ glyphs to 12 px, or show prior depths as a toggleable row under each cell row.

WCAG-3.3.1.statement: When input is rejected, name the field in error and say what is wrong in text next to it, not only with colour or a shake.
WCAG-3.3.1.threshold: 100% of automatically detected input errors produce visible text that identifies the item; 0 errors signalled by colour or border change alone.

rows.measured: Blur-time detection is colour only: typing "-50" in money.writeoff.amount and blurring sets class .invalid and repaints the border to rgb(234,88,12) with 0 refusals rendered, no aria-invalid, no aria-describedby and no error text anywhere in the canvas (canvasHasErrorText false). Press-time detection is fine: Post renders the refusal "Enter an amount above zero" 73px below the field within 24 ms and names the item.
rows.evidence: mp E_writeoff_refusal.blurInvalid {invalidClass:true, bc:"rgb(234,88,12)", refusals:0, canvasHasErrorText:false, ariaInvalid:null, describedby:null}; mp E_writeoff_refusal.postInvalid.refusals[0].verb
rows.fix: Give the blur state a text partner: render the same "Enter an amount above zero" line under the field (aria-describedby on money.writeoff.amount, aria-invalid="true") instead of only toggling .invalid.

rows.measured: Tag form at 1024 light: Save tag with empty Observation -> perio.tag.text gets aria-invalid="true" and class invalid, but the message "Say what you saw." is appended to the shared hint #pe-tag-hint 142.8 px above the field (threshold 100 px) and does not name the field. Tooth error "Tooth must be 1 to 32 and present in the mouth." names the field but sits in the same distant hint. Depth > 15: refusal "Type a depth of 15 mm or less" + control "Re-enter the depth", 100.8 px above the active cell, verb announced once.
rows.evidence: perio-probe.cjs interact.tagSubmitEmpty (hintToInputDist 142.8, hintPrecedesInput true, aria-describedby=pe-tag-hint), tagBadTooth, depthGate (distToCell 100.8); shots/perio-1024-tag-error.png.
rows.fix: Render each field's error as its own line directly under its label ("Observation: say what you saw") and keep the shared hint for the explanation only.

WCAG-3.3.2.statement: Give every input a visible, persistent label or instruction — a placeholder alone is not a label.
WCAG-3.3.2.threshold: 100% of fields have a visible persistent label; 0 fields labelled by placeholder or aria-label alone.

rows.measured: 5 fields across the three surfaces; 3 have no visible persistent label. palette.input (role=combobox) is named only by aria-label "Search patients, appointments, claims, reports, and actions" plus a 10-word placeholder — no label[for], no aria-labelledby, and the h2 "Search" is a heading, not a label. pin.display and phone.stepup.display are <div role="textbox" tabindex="0"> named only by aria-label ("PIN typed so far; Enter is Go" / "…is Approve"), and both compute border 0px none with background rgba(0,0,0,0), so the empty field has no visible boundary at all (see baseline/pinpad-open--desk-light.png: a blank strip above the keypad). Only palette.confirm.dob ("Date of birth") and phone.request.*.reason ("Send back with one line") carry a visible label. 1280 and 1024, light and dark.
rows.evidence: audit/probes/final.json palette@1280.fields / pinpad@1280.fields / stepup@1280.fields (label:false, border "0px none", bg "rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)"); overlays-result.json phone/desk/light.sendBackOpen.labelAbove true; screenshot baseline/pinpad-open--desk-light.png
rows.fix: Give palette.input a visible "Search" label above it and give both PIN displays a visible label ("PIN" / "Your PIN") plus a 2px input border, so the empty field is visible and named on screen.

INT-labels-visible-above.statement: Every input has a visible label placed above it, and no input relies on placeholder text as its label.
INT-labels-visible-above.threshold: 100% of inputs labelled by visible text; 100% labels above (except check/radio); 0 placeholder-only labels; 0 trailing colons

rows.measured: 3 of 5 inputs have no visible label at all: palette.input (aria-label + placeholder only), pin.display and phone.stepup.display (aria-label only, and both compute border 0px none on a transparent background, so there is no visible field either). The 2 that are labelled are labelled correctly and above: "Date of birth" sits above palette.confirm.dob (labelAbove true, no trailing colon) and "Send back with one line" above the phone reason input (labelAbove true). So 40% labelled by visible text, 40% above, 2 placeholder-or-aria-only fields.
rows.evidence: audit/probes/final.json palette@1280.fields[0].label false, pinpad@1280.fields[0].label false, stepup@1280.fields[0].label false; palette-confirm@1280.fields[0].label true; overlays-result.json phone/desk/light.sendBackOpen.{label,labelAbove true}
rows.fix: Add a visible "Search" label over the palette input and a visible "PIN" label over each pad display (and a border on the display so the empty field is visible).

WCAG-1.4.3.statement: Give every piece of text a contrast ratio of at least 4.5:1 against what it sits on (3:1 for text at or above 24px, or 18.66px bold), in both the light and the dark theme.
WCAG-1.4.3.threshold: >= 4.5:1 for text under 24px (or under 18.66px bold); >= 3:1 for text at or above 24px or >= 18.66px and bold. 0 failing text nodes per theme.

rows.measured: DARK theme, 1024 and 1280: the two clinical state glyphs are CSS generated content and fail. .psite.bleed::after "●" 9 px rgb(185,28,28) on --surface rgb(23,32,51) = 2.51:1, and on a deep cell fill rgb(59,31,14) = 2.34:1; .psite.sup::before "◆" 9 px rgb(124,58,237) on --surface = 2.85:1 (threshold 4.5:1). The same glyphs pass in light (● 6.47:1 / 6.09:1, ◆ 5.70:1) - the rails are light-theme colours reused unchanged on a dark fill. Every ordinary text node passes: 249 visible nodes per theme at 1024 and 1280, 0 below 4.5:1 (min light 5.89:1 .psite.missing "x", min dark 7.17:1); including the 168 aria-hidden 10 px .ghost prior values (418 nodes) still 0 failures (light ghosts 5.28-6.20:1).
rows.evidence: audit/probes/perio-verify4.cjs light/dark.shallowBleedSup.after/.before and .deepBleed.after (getComputedStyle(el, "::after").color vs the cell's own computed background, WCAG relative luminance); textNoHidden.failAA 0 / textWithHidden.failAA 0; components.css:93 and :229 set the glyph colour to var(--stop-rail) / var(--style-rail) with no dark override; shots/perio-1024-dark-bleedsup.png. axe reports 0 violations because generated content is not a text node.
rows.fix: Give --stop-rail and --style-rail dark-theme values (or paint the ●/◆ in --stop-ink / --style-ink on the dark fill) and raise the glyphs from 9 px, so the only non-colour cue for bleeding and suppuration is legible in both themes.

WCAG-1.4.12.statement: Survive a user text-spacing override (line-height 1.5, paragraph spacing 2em, letter-spacing 0.12em, word-spacing 0.16em) without clipping or losing anything.
WCAG-1.4.12.threshold: 0 clipped or overlapping elements after the override; every control still readable and clickable.

rows.measured: With the text-spacing override injected at 1280 (desk), both themes: 3 persona buttons overflow their own box — signin.persona.frontdesk scrollWidth 249 vs clientWidth 244, .biller 250 vs 244, .temp 251 vs 244 (.btn white-space: nowrap inside a 3-column grid cell). In the screenshot 'Office manager / biller' and 'Front-desk coordinator' run into the 2px border and 'Board with the first-shift rail' is cut at the grid edge. 0 overlaps between controls; 0 clipping at 420 (single column).
rows.evidence: signin-probe.out.json textSpacing.light.btnOverflow / textSpacing.dark.btnOverflow; audit/shots/signin-textspacing-light.png (row 1 col 1-2, row 3 col 3)
rows.fix: Let .personas .btn wrap (white-space: normal on the label spans, which are already a column flex) or raise the grid minmax so the longest label fits at 0.12em letter-spacing.

MQ5-color-scheme-follow-os.statement: Default the colour scheme to the OS preference and paint it before first render; the Light/Dark control is a per-user override with a way back to 'System'.
MQ5-color-scheme-follow-os.threshold: OS scheme honoured on first paint with 0 flash frames; override persists per user across reload; 3-state control (System/Light/Dark) present.

rows.measured: Fresh context, OS colorScheme dark, #/signin with no theme query: index.html serves <html data-theme="light">, final data-theme 'light', body background rgb(243,241,235) (cream) — the OS preference is not honoured at first paint. tokens.css has no prefers-color-scheme block. The theme control offers Light/Dark only; no 'System' option (signin.theme.* testids: light, dark).
rows.evidence: signin-probe.out.json osDark (htmlAttrInSource, finalTheme light, systemOption false); prototype/index.html line 2; tokens.css (no @media prefers-color-scheme)
rows.fix: Add a prefers-color-scheme default in tokens.css and a third 'System' state on signin.theme; lens owns per-user persistence.

CUST-settings-surface-small.statement: Offer real users at most seven preferences, each with two to four options and a default that needs no decision; keep simulation and QA toggles (outage, after hours, device profile, grayscale) out of the production settings surface.
CUST-settings-surface-small.threshold: <= 7 user-facing preferences; <= 4 options each; 0 QA/simulation toggles visible to production personas; 1 reset control; depth <= 1.

rows.measured: Sign-in renders 20 aria-pressed preference controls to every persona including Temp (9 persona + 2 theme + 4 device + 5 toggles), 11 of them in the 'Device and display' row. QA/simulation toggles signin.outage, signin.afterhours, signin.device.{desk,operatory,shared,phone} and signin.grayscale are all visible for non-QA personas. No 'System' default is marked for theme or motion; 0 'Reset to defaults' control. Nesting depth 1.
rows.evidence: signin-probe.out.json legs.*.controls (ariaPressed non-null count 20), groups[2].controls 11; signin.js lines 21-32
rows.fix: Keep theme (System/Light/Dark), motion (System/Reduced) and privacy on the sign-in; move device profile, grayscale, outage and after-hours behind a 'Test harness' disclosure or a ?qa=1 flag; add one Reset control.
